# The taxonomy, in full

An **energy smell** is code that spends energy on work the program does not
need, and that a specific refactoring can remove without changing what the
program does. This taxonomy names them: twelve categories, sixty-five root
causes.

This page is what to look for in step 1. Read it before you read the code, and
keep it beside you: of every function, ask whether any of these is happening
there. The **category table** says what each family of waste covers; the
**root cause table** below it lists all sixty-five, one line each — enough to
recognise one, not enough to decide it. Deciding is step 2, with the root
cause's card.

Cards live at `reference/categories/<ID>.md` — a category's root causes, with
the repair for each — and `reference/root-causes/<ID>.<S>.md`, which open at
`step.py done 1`.

## Categories

| ID | Category | Covers | Card |
|---|---|---|---|
| **C1** | Redundant Computation | Energy waste from executing work that does not contribute to the program's required output or that leaves program state unchanged | `reference/categories/C1.md` (8) |
| **C2** | Unnecessary Call Overhead | Energy waste from extra layers of function calls, method delegation, or dynamic dispatch that add overhead without proportional benefit | `reference/categories/C2.md` (3) |
| **C3** | Inefficient Iteration Patterns | Energy waste from loops that perform more per-iteration work than necessary, iterate more times than required, use suboptimal loop constructs, or fail to terminate correctly | `reference/categories/C3.md` (7) |
| **C4** | Inefficient Control Flow | Energy waste from branching, conditions, or dispatch logic that performs unnecessary checks, uses suboptimal evaluation order, or employs patterns that prevent interpreter optimization | `reference/categories/C4.md` (8) |
| **C5** | Suboptimal Data Structures | Energy waste from choosing, provisioning, or converting data structures that do not match the workload's access pattern or size requirements | `reference/categories/C5.md` (4) |
| **C6** | Unnecessary Memory Usage | Patterns that allocate, copy, retain, or leak memory beyond what the workload requires, increasing garbage collection overhead, memory-bus traffic, and system energy consumption | `reference/categories/C6.md` (7) |
| **C7** | Suboptimal Algorithmic | Energy waste from choosing an algorithm, decomposition, or computation strategy that explores more of the problem space than necessary or uses higher complexity than the problem requires | `reference/categories/C7.md` (5) |
| **C8** | Missing Reuse | Energy waste from failing to store and reuse results of expensive computations, lookups, or data fetches, causing the same work to be repeated across calls, requests, or access sites | `reference/categories/C8.md` (4) |
| **C9** | Inefficient External Data Access | Energy waste from inefficient interaction with external systems: databases, file systems, network services, and APIs | `reference/categories/C9.md` (4) |
| **C10** | Underused Language Primitives | Energy waste from not using available optimized language features, standard library functions, or runtime-specific constructs that would accomplish the same task more efficiently | `reference/categories/C10.md` (6) |
| **C11** | Inefficient Concurrency Management | Energy waste from thread/task misuse, synchronization overhead, contention, or failure to exploit available parallelism | `reference/categories/C11.md` (5) |
| **C12** | Poor Hardware Locality Usage | Energy waste driven by CPU and memory hierarchy behavior such as cache misses, branch misprediction, and suboptimal memory access patterns | `reference/categories/C12.md` (4) |

## Every root cause, one line each

### C1 — Redundant Computation

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C1.S1** | Dead Code | a value computed and bound to a name that nothing ever reads |
| **C1.S2** | Redundant Assignment | a store that leaves the program's state exactly as it already was |
| **C1.S3** | Redundant Control Flow | a branch whose outcome is the same whichever way it goes |
| **C1.S4** | Repeated Computation | the same value computed twice in one scope, where one local would serve both |
| **C1.S5** | Resultless Computation | a computation run in full whose result nothing downstream actually needs |
| **C1.S6** | Unnecessary Initialization | setup done unconditionally that only one path actually needs |
| **C1.S7** | Unnecessary Variable | a name bound, read exactly once, and never needed again |
| **C1.S8** | Excessive Runtime-Management Calls | runtime housekeeping invoked far more often than anything needs it |

### C2 — Unnecessary Call Overhead

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C2.S1** | Unnecessary Method Delegation | a wrapper or property that forwards, adds nothing, and sits on a hot path |
| **C2.S2** | Missing Static Declaration | a method that never touches `self` and still pays to be bound to an instance |
| **C2.S3** | Excessive Modularization in Hot Path | a chain of thin layers whose frames cost more than the work at the bottom |

### C3 — Inefficient Iteration Patterns

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C3.S1** | Inefficient Iteration Construct | a loop written in a form that does more interpreter work per element than it needs to |
| **C3.S2** | Recomputing Loop-Invariant Values | an expression recomputed every iteration whose answer never changes |
| **C3.S3** | Inefficient Per-Iteration Setup | an object or resource created once per iteration that the whole loop could share |
| **C3.S4** | Inefficient Nested Iteration | an inner loop that searches, where a lookup would turn n*m into n+m |
| **C3.S5** | Missing Loop Early Exit | a loop that keeps going after its answer is already settled |
| **C3.S6** | Unfiltered Bulk Iteration | the whole collection processed when only a subset was ever wanted |
| **C3.S7** | Inefficient Array Mutation in Loop | a collection edited while it is being walked |

### C4 — Inefficient Control Flow

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C4.S1** | Poor Short-Circuit Ordering | a boolean chain that evaluates its expensive operand before the cheap one that usually decides |
| **C4.S2** | Redundant Conditional Evaluation | a test whose answer was already settled before it ran |
| **C4.S3** | Inefficient Conditional Nesting | a nest or chain of branches that tests more than it has to, where a lookup would test once |
| **C4.S4** | Missing Else-If | consecutive `if`s on one subject that are exclusive in fact but not in form |
| **C4.S5** | Expensive Comparison | a type check made per element where the answer never varies or the types could dispatch themselves |
| **C4.S6** | Expensive Exception Control Flow | an exception used as ordinary control flow, on a path where it is raised often |
| **C4.S7** | Missing Edge-Case Guards | a missing cheap test that would let a common trivial input skip the expensive path |
| **C4.S8** | Non-Idiomatic Condition | a condition spelled the long way round, missing the interpreter's fast path |

### C5 — Suboptimal Data Structures

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C5.S1** | Inefficient Data Structure Choice | a container whose type makes its most frequent operation the expensive one |
| **C5.S2** | Missing Helper Type | a collection searched again and again where one index built beside it would answer every question |
| **C5.S3** | Over-Provisioned Data Type | a representation heavier than the data it holds actually requires |
| **C5.S4** | Unnecessary Representation Change | a conversion between representations that the code on either side did not need |

### C6 — Unnecessary Memory Usage

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C6.S1** | Unnecessary Object | objects created and thrown away that never needed to exist |
| **C6.S2** | Unnecessary Copying | data duplicated when the original could have been used or changed in place |
| **C6.S3** | Unnecessary Data Materialization | a whole sequence built in memory when the consumer wanted it one element at a time |
| **C6.S4** | Oversized Data Retaining | something long-lived holding far more data than anything later reads |
| **C6.S5** | Over-Allocation | capacity reserved up front for data that never arrives |
| **C6.S6** | Leaked Resource Handles | a file, socket or connection acquired with nothing guaranteeing its release |
| **C6.S7** | Leaking Mutable Default Arguments | a mutable default argument that quietly accumulates across every call |

### C7 — Suboptimal Algorithmic

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C7.S1** | Suboptimal Algorithm Choice | an algorithm of worse complexity than the problem requires |
| **C7.S2** | Inefficient Problem Decomposition | a search exploring subproblems it could have pruned, reordered or reused |
| **C7.S3** | Avoidable Recursive Implementation | a recursion paying a frame per level where a loop would use one |
| **C7.S4** | Inefficient Operation Ordering | two commuting operations in the order that makes the expensive one see more data |
| **C7.S5** | Unsimplified Operation | an operation doing more work than an algebraic fact about its inputs requires |

### C8 — Missing Reuse

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C8.S1** | Missing Memoization Cache | a deterministic computation repeated across calls that a cache would answer |
| **C8.S2** | Missing Derived-Value Reuse | an expensive artefact derived again on every use instead of once for the process |
| **C8.S3** | Missing Local Lookup Caching | a name or attribute chain re-resolved every iteration for a value that never moves |
| **C8.S4** | Redundant Data Fetching | the same external data fetched again when the copy in memory was still good |

### C9 — Inefficient External Data Access

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C9.S1** | Fragmented I/O Calls | many small independent external operations where one bulk operation would do |
| **C9.S2** | Oversized Data Retrieval | more data pulled across a process boundary than the program ever consults |
| **C9.S3** | Inefficient Retrieval Paths | one fetch per row of an earlier fetch, where a join would have taken one trip |
| **C9.S4** | Expensive Query Pattern | a query whose shape makes the engine do far more work than the answer needs |

### C10 — Underused Language Primitives

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C10.S1** | Skipping Optimized Built-ins | a hand-written loop doing bulk work a C-level primitive already does |
| **C10.S2** | Inefficient Built-in Choice | one primitive used where a cheaper primitive computes the same answer |
| **C10.S3** | Missing Bulk Primitive Usage | a per-element call inside a loop that a single batched call would replace |
| **C10.S4** | Inefficient String Concatenation | a string grown with `+=` in a loop, where the target is aliased or the parts are many |
| **C10.S5** | Inefficient Scope Lookup | a global or builtin re-resolved through the module namespace on every iteration |
| **C10.S6** | Expensive Operator Overloads | an operator on a user-defined type dispatching and allocating once per element |

### C11 — Inefficient Concurrency Management

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C11.S1** | Excessive Lock Contention | a lock held across work that shares nothing, serialising what could overlap |
| **C11.S2** | Forced Serial Bottleneck | concurrency paid for in full while one shared resource serialises all of it |
| **C11.S3** | Leaked Background Threads | workers started and never stopped, accumulating for the life of the process |
| **C11.S4** | Blocking The Main Thread | a synchronous blocking call inside a coroutine, stopping every other task |
| **C11.S5** | Missed Parallelism Opportunities | independent work run one item at a time when the waits could have overlapped |

### C12 — Poor Hardware Locality Usage

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C12.S1** | Inefficient Large-Stride Traversal | a contiguous buffer traversed against the direction its memory is laid out in |
| **C12.S2** | Sparse Element Access | scattered reads into a large buffer, using one element of every cache line fetched |
| **C12.S3** | Unpredictable Branches | a data-dependent branch in a compiled hot loop that the CPU cannot predict |
| **C12.S4** | Inefficient Array Declaration Order | a declared struct whose field order puts cold data in front of hot data |

## Using this well

**Any category may apply to any code.** Nothing about a repository rules a
category in or out in advance. Work from what the code actually does.

**Read the card, not the name, and not the line above.** These names are three
or four words long and several of them cover something narrower — or wider —
than they sound like. The one-line summaries here are index entries, precise
enough to recognise something by and not enough to decide anything from. The
card is the claim.

**The index tells you what to look for, not what you will find.** A unit goes
on your list because of what its code does, not because a line here sounds
like it. Finding nothing in a category is a perfectly ordinary outcome.

**Cards overlap.** When two root causes both describe what you repaired,
either attribution is fine — say which you chose.

## What tools can and cannot contribute

Any static rule, in any tool, recognises a syntactic shape that somebody
described in advance. That makes rules dependable about the shapes they know
and completely blind to everything else. Two consequences, and they point in
opposite directions:

- **A rule firing has observed a pattern, not diagnosed a problem.** Every
  pattern in this taxonomy is the right thing to write somewhere, which is what
  each card's `Looks like it, but is not` section records.
  Some of what any rule reports is therefore wrong here, and saying which is
  part of the job.
- **A rule staying quiet has observed nothing.** Waste that lives in the
  arrangement of a program — work computed and discarded, a data shape that
  forces every later step to compensate, a query issued once per row — has no
  fixed syntactic shape at all, and is usually the expensive kind.

Reading the code is the primary method here. Anything a tool tells you is a
second opinion to reconcile with what you already worked out.

33	# TODO: are these the correct names?
34	BATCH_ID = "batch ID"
35	
36	# Figure out the type for each input, by describing the
37	# executable
38	def _get_types_for_inputs(executable):
39	    exec_desc = executable.describe()
40	    input_spec = []
41	    if ('inputs' in exec_desc and
42	        exec_desc['inputs'] is not None):
43	        # workflow-level inputs were defined for the workflow
44	        input_spec = exec_desc['inputs']
45	    elif ('inputSpec' in exec_desc and
46	          exec_desc['inputSpec'] is not None):
47	        input_spec = exec_desc['inputSpec']
48	    else:
49	        raise Exception("executable {} does not have an input specification".format(executable.get_id()))
50	
51	    input_key_classes={}
52	    for arg_desc in input_spec:
53	        input_key_classes[arg_desc['name']] = arg_desc['class']
54	
55	    return input_key_classes
56	
57	# val: a value of type string, that needs to be converted
58	# col_class: the class of the executable argument
59	#
60	# return:
61	#   - the value in the correct type
62	#   - any platform files referenced in the type
63	def _type_convert_primitive(val, klass):
64	    retval = None
65	    ref_files = []
66	    if klass == 'string':
67	        retval = val
68	    elif klass == 'int':
69	        retval = int(val)
70	    elif klass == "boolean":
71	        retval = bool(val)
72	    elif klass == 'float':
73	        retval = float(val)
74	    elif klass == 'hash':
75	        retval = json.loads(val)
76	    elif klass == 'file':
77	        if val.startswith("project-"):
78	            val = val.split(":")
79	            retval = dxpy.dxlink(object_id=val[1], project_id=val[0])
80	            ref_files.append(retval)
81	        elif val.startswith("file-"):
82	            retval = dxpy.dxlink(val)
83	            ref_files.append(retval)
84	        else:
85	            raise Exception("Malformed file {}, must start with 'file-' or 'project-'".format(val))
86	    else:
87	        raise Exception("class {} not currently supported".format(klass))
88	    return retval, ref_files
89	
90	# An array type, such as array:file
91	def _type_convert_array(val, klass):
92	    inner_type = klass.split(":")[1]
93	    len_val = len(val)
94	    if (len_val < 2 or
95	        val[0] != '[' or
96	        val[len_val-1] != ']'):
97	        raise Exception("Malformed array {}".format(val))
98	    val_strip_brackets = val[1:(len_val-1)]
99	    retval = []
100	    ref_files = []
101	    elements = [e.strip() for e in val_strip_brackets.split(',')]
102	    for e in elements:
103	        e_with_type,files = _type_convert_primitive(e, inner_type)
104	        retval.append(e_with_type)
105	        ref_files += files
106	    return retval, ref_files

108	def _type_convert(val, klass):
109	    try:
110	        if klass.startswith("array:"):
111	            return _type_convert_array(val, klass)
112	        else:
113	            # A primitive type, like {int, float, file, hash}
114	            return _type_convert_primitive(val, klass)
115	    except Exception:
116	        raise Exception("value={} cannot be converted into class {}".format(val, klass))

118	# For a column that represents files, assume it is named "pair", look for
119	# the index of column "pair ID".
120	def _search_column_id(col_name, header_line):
121	    for i, col_name2 in enumerate(header_line):
122	        if col_name2 == (col_name + " ID"):
123	            return i
124	    raise Exception("Could not find a column with file IDs for {}".format(col_name))
125	
126	# Parse the TSV file. Create a dictionary with the input arguments for
127	# each invocation. Return an array of dictionaries.
128	#
129	# For each line, except the header:
130	#   remove informational columns
131	#   create a dictionary of inputs we can pass to the executable
132	#
133	# Example TSV input:
134	# batch ID, pair1,       pair1 ID, pair2,       pair2 ID
135	# 23,       SRR123_1.gz, file-XXX, SRR223_2.gz, file-YYY
136	#
137	def batch_launch_args(executable, input_json, batch_tsv_file):
138	    header_line = []
139	    lines = []
140	    read_mode = "r"
141	    with open(batch_tsv_file, read_mode) as f:
142	        reader = csv.reader(f, delimiter=str(u'\t'))
143	        header_line = next(reader)
144	        lines = list(reader)
145	
146	    # Get the classes for the executable inputs
147	    input_classes = _get_types_for_inputs(executable)
148	
149	    # which columns to use. Note that a file input uses two columns.
150	    # For example, argument 'pair1' exposes two columns {'pair1, 'pair1 ID'}.
151	    batch_index = None
152	    index_2_column = {}
153	    for i, col_name in enumerate(header_line):
154	        if col_name == BATCH_ID:
155	            batch_index = i
156	        if col_name not in input_classes:
157	            continue
158	        if input_classes[col_name] in ['file', 'array:file']:
159	            idx = _search_column_id(col_name, header_line)
160	            index_2_column[idx] = col_name
161	        else:
162	            index_2_column[i] = col_name
163	    if batch_index is None:
164	        raise Exception("Could not find column {}".format(BATCH_ID))
165	
166	    # A dictionary of inputs. Each column in the TSV file is mapped to a row.
167	    # {
168	    #    "a": [{dnanexus_link: "file-xxxx"}, {dnanexus_link: "file-yyyy"}, ....],
169	    #    "b": [1,null, ...]
170	    # }
171	    columns=defaultdict(list)
172	    all_files=[]
173	    for line in lines:
174	        for i, val in enumerate(line):
175	            if i not in index_2_column:
176	                continue
177	            col_name = index_2_column[i]
178	            klass = input_classes[col_name]
179	            val_w_correct_type, ref_files = _type_convert(val.strip(), klass)
180	            all_files += ref_files
181	            columns[col_name].append(val_w_correct_type)
182	
183	    # Create an array of batch_ids
184	    batch_ids = [line[batch_index].strip() for line in lines]
185	
186	    # call validate
187	    #
188	    # Output: list of dictionaries, each dictionary corresponds to expanded batch call
189	    expanded_args = dxpy.api.applet_validate_batch(executable.get_id(),
190	                                                   { "batchInput": columns,
191	                                                     "commonInput": input_json,
192	                                                     "files": all_files,
193	                                                     "instanceTypes": [] })
194	
195	    ## future proofing
196	    if isinstance(expanded_args, dict):
197	        assert('expandedBatch' in expanded_args)
198	        launch_args = expanded_args['expandedBatch']
199	    else:
200	        launch_args = expanded_args
201	    if len(launch_args) != len(batch_ids):
202	        raise Exception("Mismatch in number of launch_args vs. batch_ids ({} != {})"
203	                        .format(len(launch_args), len(batch_ids)))
204	
205	    return { "launch_args": launch_args,
206	             "batch_ids": batch_ids }
207	
208	#
209	# executable: applet, app, or workflow
210	# launch_args: array of dictionaries, each of which contains all arguments needed to
211	#     invoke the executable.
212	# set_batch_folders: boolean, if True, the results from each batch
213	#     run will be placed in a separate output folder named after batch ID.
214	#     The folders will be created/used relative to the output folder set with
215	#     the --destination arg
216	def batch_run(executable, b_args, run_kwargs, set_batch_folders=False):
217	    run_args = run_kwargs.copy()
218	    exec_name = executable.describe()["name"]
219	    launch_args = b_args["launch_args"]
220	    batch_ids = b_args["batch_ids"]
221	    executions = []
222	    for idx, input_json in enumerate(launch_args):
223	        batch_id = batch_ids[idx]
224	        name = "{}-{}".format(exec_name, batch_id)
225	        properties = {
226	            'batch-id': batch_id,
227	            'batch-name': name
228	        }
229	        run_args['name'] = name
230	        if run_args.get('properties') is not None:
231	            run_args['properties'].update(properties)
232	        else:
233	            run_args['properties'] = properties
234	
235	        if set_batch_folders:
236	            run_args['folder'] = run_kwargs['folder'] + "/" + batch_id
237	
238	        try:
239	            dxexecution = executable.run(input_json, **run_args)
240	            executions.append(dxexecution)
241	        except Exception:
242	            err_exit()
243	    return executions

25	def _train(features):
26	    model = collections.defaultdict(lambda: 1)

33	def _edits1(word):
34	   splits     = [(word[:i], word[i:]) for i in range(len(word) + 1)]
35	   deletes    = [a + b[1:] for a, b in splits if b]
36	   transposes = [a + b[1] + b[0] + b[2:] for a, b in splits if len(b)>1]
37	   replaces   = [a + c + b[1:] for a, b in splits for c in _alphabet if b]
38	   inserts    = [a + c + b     for a, b in splits for c in _alphabet]
39	   return set(deletes + transposes + replaces + inserts)
40	
41	def _known_edits2(word, NWORDS):
42	    return set(e2 for e1 in _edits1(word) for e2 in _edits1(e1) if e2 in NWORDS)
43	
44	def _known(words, NWORDS):
45	    return set(w for w in words if w in NWORDS)
46	
47	def correct(word, known_words):
48	    """
49	    :param word: Word to correct
50	    :type word: string
51	    :param known_words: List of known words
52	    :type known_words: iterable of strings
53	
54	    Given **word**, suggests a correction from **known_words**. If no reasonably close correction is found, returns
55	    **word**.
56	    """
57	    NWORDS = _train(known_words)
58	    candidates = _known([word], NWORDS) or _known(_edits1(word), NWORDS) or _known_edits2(word, NWORDS) or [word]
59	    return max(candidates, key=NWORDS.get)

# The taxonomy, in full

An **energy smell** is code that spends energy on work the program does not
need, and that a specific refactoring can remove without changing what the
program does. This taxonomy names them: twelve categories, sixty-five root
causes.

This page is what to look for in step 1. Read it before you read the code, and
keep it beside you: of every function, ask whether any of these is happening
there. The **category table** says what each family of waste covers; the
**root cause table** below it lists all sixty-five, one line each — enough to
recognise one, not enough to decide it. Deciding is step 2, with the root
cause's card.

Cards live at `reference/categories/<ID>.md` — a category's root causes, with
the repair for each — and `reference/root-causes/<ID>.<S>.md`, which open at
`step.py done 1`.

## Categories

| ID | Category | Covers | Card |
|---|---|---|---|
| **C1** | Redundant Computation | Energy waste from executing work that does not contribute to the program's required output or that leaves program state unchanged | `reference/categories/C1.md` (8) |
| **C2** | Unnecessary Call Overhead | Energy waste from extra layers of function calls, method delegation, or dynamic dispatch that add overhead without proportional benefit | `reference/categories/C2.md` (3) |
| **C3** | Inefficient Iteration Patterns | Energy waste from loops that perform more per-iteration work than necessary, iterate more times than required, use suboptimal loop constructs, or fail to terminate correctly | `reference/categories/C3.md` (7) |
| **C4** | Inefficient Control Flow | Energy waste from branching, conditions, or dispatch logic that performs unnecessary checks, uses suboptimal evaluation order, or employs patterns that prevent interpreter optimization | `reference/categories/C4.md` (8) |
| **C5** | Suboptimal Data Structures | Energy waste from choosing, provisioning, or converting data structures that do not match the workload's access pattern or size requirements | `reference/categories/C5.md` (4) |
| **C6** | Unnecessary Memory Usage | Patterns that allocate, copy, retain, or leak memory beyond what the workload requires, increasing garbage collection overhead, memory-bus traffic, and system energy consumption | `reference/categories/C6.md` (7) |
| **C7** | Suboptimal Algorithmic | Energy waste from choosing an algorithm, decomposition, or computation strategy that explores more of the problem space than necessary or uses higher complexity than the problem requires | `reference/categories/C7.md` (5) |
| **C8** | Missing Reuse | Energy waste from failing to store and reuse results of expensive computations, lookups, or data fetches, causing the same work to be repeated across calls, requests, or access sites | `reference/categories/C8.md` (4) |
| **C9** | Inefficient External Data Access | Energy waste from inefficient interaction with external systems: databases, file systems, network services, and APIs | `reference/categories/C9.md` (4) |
| **C10** | Underused Language Primitives | Energy waste from not using available optimized language features, standard library functions, or runtime-specific constructs that would accomplish the same task more efficiently | `reference/categories/C10.md` (6) |
| **C11** | Inefficient Concurrency Management | Energy waste from thread/task misuse, synchronization overhead, contention, or failure to exploit available parallelism | `reference/categories/C11.md` (5) |
| **C12** | Poor Hardware Locality Usage | Energy waste driven by CPU and memory hierarchy behavior such as cache misses, branch misprediction, and suboptimal memory access patterns | `reference/categories/C12.md` (4) |

## Every root cause, one line each

### C1 — Redundant Computation

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C1.S1** | Dead Code | a value computed and bound to a name that nothing ever reads |
| **C1.S2** | Redundant Assignment | a store that leaves the program's state exactly as it already was |
| **C1.S3** | Redundant Control Flow | a branch whose outcome is the same whichever way it goes |
| **C1.S4** | Repeated Computation | the same value computed twice in one scope, where one local would serve both |
| **C1.S5** | Resultless Computation | a computation run in full whose result nothing downstream actually needs |
| **C1.S6** | Unnecessary Initialization | setup done unconditionally that only one path actually needs |
| **C1.S7** | Unnecessary Variable | a name bound, read exactly once, and never needed again |
| **C1.S8** | Excessive Runtime-Management Calls | runtime housekeeping invoked far more often than anything needs it |

### C2 — Unnecessary Call Overhead

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C2.S1** | Unnecessary Method Delegation | a wrapper or property that forwards, adds nothing, and sits on a hot path |
| **C2.S2** | Missing Static Declaration | a method that never touches `self` and still pays to be bound to an instance |
| **C2.S3** | Excessive Modularization in Hot Path | a chain of thin layers whose frames cost more than the work at the bottom |

### C3 — Inefficient Iteration Patterns

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C3.S1** | Inefficient Iteration Construct | a loop written in a form that does more interpreter work per element than it needs to |
| **C3.S2** | Recomputing Loop-Invariant Values | an expression recomputed every iteration whose answer never changes |
| **C3.S3** | Inefficient Per-Iteration Setup | an object or resource created once per iteration that the whole loop could share |
| **C3.S4** | Inefficient Nested Iteration | an inner loop that searches, where a lookup would turn n*m into n+m |
| **C3.S5** | Missing Loop Early Exit | a loop that keeps going after its answer is already settled |
| **C3.S6** | Unfiltered Bulk Iteration | the whole collection processed when only a subset was ever wanted |
| **C3.S7** | Inefficient Array Mutation in Loop | a collection edited while it is being walked |

### C4 — Inefficient Control Flow

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C4.S1** | Poor Short-Circuit Ordering | a boolean chain that evaluates its expensive operand before the cheap one that usually decides |
| **C4.S2** | Redundant Conditional Evaluation | a test whose answer was already settled before it ran |
| **C4.S3** | Inefficient Conditional Nesting | a nest or chain of branches that tests more than it has to, where a lookup would test once |
| **C4.S4** | Missing Else-If | consecutive `if`s on one subject that are exclusive in fact but not in form |
| **C4.S5** | Expensive Comparison | a type check made per element where the answer never varies or the types could dispatch themselves |
| **C4.S6** | Expensive Exception Control Flow | an exception used as ordinary control flow, on a path where it is raised often |
| **C4.S7** | Missing Edge-Case Guards | a missing cheap test that would let a common trivial input skip the expensive path |
| **C4.S8** | Non-Idiomatic Condition | a condition spelled the long way round, missing the interpreter's fast path |

### C5 — Suboptimal Data Structures

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C5.S1** | Inefficient Data Structure Choice | a container whose type makes its most frequent operation the expensive one |
| **C5.S2** | Missing Helper Type | a collection searched again and again where one index built beside it would answer every question |
| **C5.S3** | Over-Provisioned Data Type | a representation heavier than the data it holds actually requires |
| **C5.S4** | Unnecessary Representation Change | a conversion between representations that the code on either side did not need |

### C6 — Unnecessary Memory Usage

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C6.S1** | Unnecessary Object | objects created and thrown away that never needed to exist |
| **C6.S2** | Unnecessary Copying | data duplicated when the original could have been used or changed in place |
| **C6.S3** | Unnecessary Data Materialization | a whole sequence built in memory when the consumer wanted it one element at a time |
| **C6.S4** | Oversized Data Retaining | something long-lived holding far more data than anything later reads |
| **C6.S5** | Over-Allocation | capacity reserved up front for data that never arrives |
| **C6.S6** | Leaked Resource Handles | a file, socket or connection acquired with nothing guaranteeing its release |
| **C6.S7** | Leaking Mutable Default Arguments | a mutable default argument that quietly accumulates across every call |

### C7 — Suboptimal Algorithmic

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C7.S1** | Suboptimal Algorithm Choice | an algorithm of worse complexity than the problem requires |
| **C7.S2** | Inefficient Problem Decomposition | a search exploring subproblems it could have pruned, reordered or reused |
| **C7.S3** | Avoidable Recursive Implementation | a recursion paying a frame per level where a loop would use one |
| **C7.S4** | Inefficient Operation Ordering | two commuting operations in the order that makes the expensive one see more data |
| **C7.S5** | Unsimplified Operation | an operation doing more work than an algebraic fact about its inputs requires |

### C8 — Missing Reuse

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C8.S1** | Missing Memoization Cache | a deterministic computation repeated across calls that a cache would answer |
| **C8.S2** | Missing Derived-Value Reuse | an expensive artefact derived again on every use instead of once for the process |
| **C8.S3** | Missing Local Lookup Caching | a name or attribute chain re-resolved every iteration for a value that never moves |
| **C8.S4** | Redundant Data Fetching | the same external data fetched again when the copy in memory was still good |

### C9 — Inefficient External Data Access

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C9.S1** | Fragmented I/O Calls | many small independent external operations where one bulk operation would do |
| **C9.S2** | Oversized Data Retrieval | more data pulled across a process boundary than the program ever consults |
| **C9.S3** | Inefficient Retrieval Paths | one fetch per row of an earlier fetch, where a join would have taken one trip |
| **C9.S4** | Expensive Query Pattern | a query whose shape makes the engine do far more work than the answer needs |

### C10 — Underused Language Primitives

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C10.S1** | Skipping Optimized Built-ins | a hand-written loop doing bulk work a C-level primitive already does |
| **C10.S2** | Inefficient Built-in Choice | one primitive used where a cheaper primitive computes the same answer |
| **C10.S3** | Missing Bulk Primitive Usage | a per-element call inside a loop that a single batched call would replace |
| **C10.S4** | Inefficient String Concatenation | a string grown with `+=` in a loop, where the target is aliased or the parts are many |
| **C10.S5** | Inefficient Scope Lookup | a global or builtin re-resolved through the module namespace on every iteration |
| **C10.S6** | Expensive Operator Overloads | an operator on a user-defined type dispatching and allocating once per element |

### C11 — Inefficient Concurrency Management

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C11.S1** | Excessive Lock Contention | a lock held across work that shares nothing, serialising what could overlap |
| **C11.S2** | Forced Serial Bottleneck | concurrency paid for in full while one shared resource serialises all of it |
| **C11.S3** | Leaked Background Threads | workers started and never stopped, accumulating for the life of the process |
| **C11.S4** | Blocking The Main Thread | a synchronous blocking call inside a coroutine, stopping every other task |
| **C11.S5** | Missed Parallelism Opportunities | independent work run one item at a time when the waits could have overlapped |

### C12 — Poor Hardware Locality Usage

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C12.S1** | Inefficient Large-Stride Traversal | a contiguous buffer traversed against the direction its memory is laid out in |
| **C12.S2** | Sparse Element Access | scattered reads into a large buffer, using one element of every cache line fetched |
| **C12.S3** | Unpredictable Branches | a data-dependent branch in a compiled hot loop that the CPU cannot predict |
| **C12.S4** | Inefficient Array Declaration Order | a declared struct whose field order puts cold data in front of hot data |

## Using this well

**Any category may apply to any code.** Nothing about a repository rules a
category in or out in advance. Work from what the code actually does.

**Read the card, not the name, and not the line above.** These names are three
or four words long and several of them cover something narrower — or wider —
than they sound like. The one-line summaries here are index entries, precise
enough to recognise something by and not enough to decide anything from. The
card is the claim.

**The index tells you what to look for, not what you will find.** A unit goes
on your list because of what its code does, not because a line here sounds
like it. Finding nothing in a category is a perfectly ordinary outcome.

**Cards overlap.** When two root causes both describe what you repaired,
either attribution is fine — say which you chose.

## What tools can and cannot contribute

Any static rule, in any tool, recognises a syntactic shape that somebody
described in advance. That makes rules dependable about the shapes they know
and completely blind to everything else. Two consequences, and they point in
opposite directions:

- **A rule firing has observed a pattern, not diagnosed a problem.** Every
  pattern in this taxonomy is the right thing to write somewhere, which is what
  each card's `Looks like it, but is not` section records.
  Some of what any rule reports is therefore wrong here, and saying which is
  part of the job.
- **A rule staying quiet has observed nothing.** Waste that lives in the
  arrangement of a program — work computed and discarded, a data shape that
  forces every later step to compensate, a query issued once per row — has no
  fixed syntactic shape at all, and is usually the expensive kind.

Reading the code is the primary method here. Anything a tool tells you is a
second opinion to reconcile with what you already worked out.

28	    Code adapted from logging.handlers.SysLogHandler.

38	        logging.getLogger().addHandler(DXLogHandler())

40	    '''
41	    def __init__(self, priority_log_address="/opt/dnanexus/log/priority",
42	                 bulk_log_address="/opt/dnanexus/log/bulk",
43	                 source="DX_APP"):
44	        logging.Handler.__init__(self)
45	
46	        self.priority_log_address = priority_log_address
47	        self.priority_log_socket = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)

53	            raise DXError("The path %s does not exist, but is required for application logging" % (priority_log_address))
54	        if not os.path.exists(bulk_log_address):
55	            raise DXError("The path %s does not exist, but is required for application logging" % (bulk_log_address))
56	
57	        self.priority_log_socket.connect(priority_log_address)
58	        self.bulk_log_socket.connect(bulk_log_address)
59	
60	        self.source = source
61	
62	    def close(self):
63	        self.priority_log_socket.close()
64	        self.bulk_log_socket.close()

67	    def encodePriority(self, record):
68	        # See logging.handlers.SysLogHandler for an explanation of this.
69	        return self.priority_names[self.priority_map.get(record.levelname, "warning")]

71	    def truncate_message(self, message):
72	        msg_bytes = message.encode('utf-8')
73	
74	        if len(json.dumps(message)) <= 8015:
75	            return message
76	
77	        msg_bytes = msg_bytes[:8000]
78	        while len(json.dumps(_bytes2utf8(msg_bytes))) > 8000:
79	            msg_bytes = msg_bytes[:-1]
80

89	        message = record.getMessage()

91	        # with the extra padding introduced by the log function, the
92	        # incoming message needs to be smaller - we truncate it to
93	        # at most 8015 bytes here.
94	        message = self.truncate_message(message)
95	
96	        data = json.dumps({"source": self.source, "timestamp": int(round(time.time() * 1000)),
97	                           "level": level, "msg": message}).encode('utf-8', 'ignore')
98	
99	        levelno = int(record.levelno)
100	        if levelno >= logging.CRITICAL or (levelno == logging.INFO and self.is_resource_log(message)):
101	            # Critical, alert, emerg, or resource status
102	            cur_socket = self.priority_log_socket
103	            cur_socket_address = self.priority_log_address
104	        else:
105	            cur_socket = self.bulk_log_socket
106	            cur_socket_address = self.bulk_log_address
107	
108	        try:
109	            cur_socket.send(data)

111	            cur_socket.connect(cur_socket_address)
112	            cur_socket.send(data)
113	        except (KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit):

34	    ''' Copy the source to a destination that does not currently
35	    exist. This involves creating the target file/folder.
36	    '''
37	    # Destination folder path is new => renaming
38	    if len(args.sources) != 1:
39	        # Can't copy and rename more than one object
40	        raise DXCLIError('The destination folder does not exist')
41	    last_slash_pos = get_last_pos_of_char('/', dest_path)
42	    if last_slash_pos == 0:
43	        dest_folder = '/'
44	    else:
45	        dest_folder = dest_path[:last_slash_pos]
46	    dest_name = dest_path[last_slash_pos + 1:].replace('\/', '/')
47	    try:
48	        dx_dest.list_folder(folder=dest_folder, only='folders')
49	    except dxpy.DXAPIError as e:
50	        if isinstance(e, ResourceNotFound):
51	            raise DXCLIError('The destination folder does not exist')
52	        else:
53	            raise
54	    except:
55	        err_exit()
56	
57	    # Clone and rename either the data object or the folder.
58	    # src_result is None if it could not be resolved to an object.
59	    src_proj, src_path, src_results = try_call(resolve_existing_path,
60	                                               args.sources[0],

77	                                                    {"folder": src_path, "includeHidden": True})

82	                                             "project": dest_proj,

94	                                             "project": dest_proj,
95	                                             "destination": dest_folder})['exists']
96	            if len(exists) > 0:

109	def cp(args):
110	    dest_proj, dest_path, _none = try_call(resolve_path, args.destination, expected='folder')
111	    if dest_path is None:
112	        raise DXCLIError('Cannot copy to a hash ID')
113	    dx_dest = dxpy.get_handler(dest_proj)
114	    try:
115	        # check if the destination exists
116	        dx_dest.list_folder(folder=dest_path, only='folders')
117	    except:
118	        cp_to_noexistent_destination(args, dest_path, dx_dest, dest_proj)
119	        return

121	    # The destination exists, we need to copy all of the sources to it.
122	    if len(args.sources) == 0:
123	        raise DXCLIError('No sources provided to copy to another project')
124	    src_objects = []
125	    src_folders = []
126	    for source in args.sources:
127	        src_proj, src_folderpath, src_results = try_call(resolve_existing_path,
128	                                                         source,
129	                                                         allow_mult=True, all_mult=args.all)
130	        if src_proj == dest_proj:

133	                # purely assumed, so give a better error message.
134	                raise DXCLIError(fill('Error: You must specify a source project for ' + source))

138	                                    'different source and destination containers, e.g.') +

41	
42	    for path in os.environ["PATH"].split(os.pathsep):

50	def _verify(filename, md5digest):
51	    md5sum_exe = _which("md5sum")
52	    if md5sum_exe is None:
53	        err_exit("md5sum is not installed on this system")
54	    cmd = [md5sum_exe, "-b", filename]
55	    try:
56	        print("Calculating checksum")
57	        cmd_out = subprocess.check_output(cmd)
58	    except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
59	        err_exit("Failed to run md5sum: " + str(cmd))
60	
61	    line = cmd_out.strip().split()
62	    if len(line) != 2:
63	        err_exit("md5sum returned weird results: " + str(line))
64	    actual_md5 = line[0]
65	    if actual_md5 != md5digest:
66	        err_exit("Checksum doesn't match " + actual_md5 + "  expected:" + md5digest)
67	    print("Checksum correct")

168	def _download_folders(folders, destdir, args):
169	    try:
170	        show_progress = args.show_progress
171	    except AttributeError:
172	        show_progress = False
173	    for project in folders:
174	        for folder, strip_prefix in folders[project]:
175	            if not args.recursive:
176	                err_exit('Error: "' + folder + '" is a folder but the -r/--recursive option was not given')
177	            assert(folder.startswith(strip_prefix))
178	            folder_destdir = os.path.join(destdir, folder[len(strip_prefix):].lstrip('/'))
179	            try:
180	                dxpy.download_folder(project, folder_destdir, folder=folder, overwrite=args.overwrite,
181	                                     show_progress=show_progress)
182	            except:
183	                err_exit()
184	
185	
186	# Main entry point.
187	def download(args):
188	    folders_to_get, files_to_get, count = collections.defaultdict(list), collections.defaultdict(list), 0
189	    foldernames, filenames = [], []
190	    for path in args.paths:
191	        # Attempt to resolve name. If --all is given or the path looks like a glob, download all matches.
192	        # Otherwise, the resolver will display a picker (or error out if there is no tty to display to).
193	        resolver_kwargs = {'allow_empty_string': False}
194	        if args.all or _is_glob(path):
195	            resolver_kwargs.update({'allow_mult': True, 'all_mult': True})
196	
197	        # include "parts" and a few additional fields in the description so that
198	        # we don't have to call a separate describe method downstream
199	        resolver_kwargs.update({"describe": {"parts": True,
200	                                             "size": True,
201	                                             "drive": True,
202	                                             "md5": True,
203	                                             "checksumType": True
204	                                             }})
205	
206	        project, folderpath, matching_files = try_call(resolve_existing_path, path, **resolver_kwargs)
207	
208	        if matching_files is None:
209	            matching_files = []
210	        elif not isinstance(matching_files, list):
211	            matching_files = [matching_files]
212	
213	        # TODO: this could also be returned as metadata by resolve_path since
214	        # resolve_path knows these things in some circumstances
215	        path_has_explicit_proj = is_project_explicit(path) or is_jbor_str(path)
216	
217	        if is_jbor_str(path):
218	            assert len(matching_files) == 1
219	            project = matching_files[0]["describe"]["project"]
220	        matching_folders = []
221	        # project may be none if path is an ID and there is no project context
222	        if project is not None:
223	            colon_pos = get_first_pos_of_char(":", path)
224	            if colon_pos >= 0:
225	                path = path[colon_pos + 1:]
226	            abs_path, strip_prefix = _rel2abs(path, project)
227	            parent_folder = os.path.dirname(abs_path)
228	            folder_listing = dxpy.list_subfolders(project, parent_folder, recurse=False)
229	            matching_folders = pathmatch.filter(folder_listing, abs_path)
230	            if '/' in matching_folders and len(matching_folders) > 1:
231	                # The list of subfolders is {'/', '/A', '/B'}.
232	                # Remove '/', otherwise we will download everything twice.
233	                matching_folders.remove('/')
234	
235	        if len(matching_files) == 0 and len(matching_folders) == 0:
236	            err_exit(fill('Error: {path} is neither a file nor a folder name'.format(path=path)))
237	
238	        # If the user did not explicitly provide the project, don't pass any
239	        # project parameter to the API call but continue with the download.
240	        if not path_has_explicit_proj:
241	            project = dxpy.DXFile.NO_PROJECT_HINT
242	
243	        # If the user explicitly provided the project and it doesn't contain
244	        # the files, don't allow the download.
245	
246	        # For speed's sake, skip this check (i.e. one API call) if the user
247	        # passed the lightweight argument
248	        #
249	        # If length of matching_files is 0 then we're only downloading folders
250	        # so skip this logic since the files will be verified in the API call.
251	        if not args.lightweight \
252	            and len(matching_files) > 0 \
253	            and path_has_explicit_proj \
254	            and not any(object_exists_in_project(f['describe']['id'], project) for f in matching_files):
255	                err_exit(fill('Error: specified project does not contain specified file object'))
256	
257	        files_to_get[project].extend(matching_files)
258	        folders_to_get[project].extend(((f, strip_prefix) for f in matching_folders))
259	        count += len(matching_files) + len(matching_folders)
260	        filenames.extend(f["describe"]["name"] for f in matching_files)
261	        foldernames.extend(f[len(strip_prefix):].lstrip('/') for f in matching_folders)
262	
263	    if len(filenames) > 0 and len(foldernames) > 0:
264	        name_conflicts = set(filenames) & set(foldernames)
265	        if len(name_conflicts) > 0:
266	            msg = "Error: The following paths are both file and folder names, and " \
267	                  "cannot be downloaded to the same destination: "
268	            msg += ", ".join(sorted(name_conflicts))
269	            err_exit(fill(msg))
270	
271	    if args.output is None:
272	        destdir, dest_filename = os.getcwd(), None
273	    elif count > 1:
274	        if not os.path.exists(args.output):
275	            err_exit(fill("Error: When downloading multiple objects, --output must be an existing directory"))
276	        destdir, dest_filename = args.output, None
277	    elif os.path.isdir(args.output):
278	        destdir, dest_filename = args.output, None
279	    elif args.output.endswith('/'):
280	        err_exit(fill("Error: {path} could not be found".format(path=args.output)))
281	    else:
282	        destdir, dest_filename = os.getcwd(), args.output
283	
284	    _download_folders(folders_to_get, destdir, args)
285	    _download_files(files_to_get, destdir, args, dest_filename=dest_filename)

571	class TestNextflowOfflineMode(unittest.TestCase):
572	    """
573	    Offline mode (NXF_OFFLINE) is decided in bash, before Nextflow is launched, because
574	    Nextflow reads NXF_OFFLINE when the JVM starts (nextflow.plugin.PluginsFacade) and it
575	    cannot be set from nextflow.config. These tests source the generated applet script and
576	    execute the decision function with a stubbed `dx` command.
577	    """
578	
579	    @classmethod
580	    def setUpClass(cls):
581	        cls.tempdir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
582	        cls.src_file = os.path.join(cls.tempdir, "nextflow.sh")
583	        with open(cls.src_file, "w") as f:
584	            f.write(get_nextflow_src())
585	        # `dx api <id> describe <json>` stub. It logs every described id to $DX_STUB_CALLS, so a
586	        # test can assert that the project is described only as a fallback, and answers per id
587	        # ($DX_STUB_JOB_JSON / $DX_STUB_PROJECT_JSON, both defaulting to $DX_STUB_JSON) so the
588	        # job and its project can disagree the way they do when the flag was not propagated.
589	        cls.stub_dir = os.path.join(cls.tempdir, "stub")
590	        os.makedirs(cls.stub_dir)
591	        dx_stub = os.path.join(cls.stub_dir, "dx")
592	        with open(dx_stub, "w") as f:
593	            f.write(textwrap.dedent("""\
594	                #!/usr/bin/env bash
595	                echo "$2" >>"$DX_STUB_CALLS"
596	                [[ $DX_STUB_FAIL == 1 ]] && exit 1
597	                case $2 in
598	                job-*) echo "${DX_STUB_JOB_JSON-$DX_STUB_JSON}" ;;
599	                project-*) echo "${DX_STUB_PROJECT_JSON-$DX_STUB_JSON}" ;;
600	                *) echo "$DX_STUB_JSON" ;;
601	                esac
602	                """))
603	        os.chmod(dx_stub, 0o755)
604	        # the platform's error reporter: prints the message and aborts the job
605	        reporter = os.path.join(cls.stub_dir, "dx-jobutil-report-error")
606	        with open(reporter, "w") as f:
607	            f.write('#!/usr/bin/env bash\necho "$@" >&2\nexit 1\n')
608	        os.chmod(reporter, 0o755)

611	    def tearDownClass(cls):
612	        shutil.rmtree(cls.tempdir, ignore_errors=True)

614	    def _run_bash(self, snippet, describe_json="", api_fails=False, run_opts="", nxf_offline=None,
615	                  job_json=None, project_json=None, top_level_opts="", expect_error=False):
616	        """Runs `snippet` against the sourced applet script; returns (stdout, described ids).
617	
618	        With expect_error the run must fail instead, and stderr is returned in place of stdout.
619	        """
620	        calls_file = os.path.join(self.tempdir, "dx_calls.log")
621	        if os.path.exists(calls_file):
622	            os.remove(calls_file)
623	        env = dict(os.environ)
624	        env["PATH"] = self.stub_dir + os.pathsep + env["PATH"]
625	        env["DX_JOB_ID"] = "job-xxxx"
626	        env["DX_PROJECT_CONTEXT_ID"] = "project-yyyy"
627	        env["DX_STUB_JSON"] = describe_json
628	        env["DX_STUB_FAIL"] = "1" if api_fails else "0"
629	        env["DX_STUB_CALLS"] = calls_file
630	        if job_json is not None:
631	            env["DX_STUB_JOB_JSON"] = job_json
632	        if project_json is not None:
633	            env["DX_STUB_PROJECT_JSON"] = project_json
634	        env["nextflow_run_opts"] = run_opts
635	        env["nextflow_top_level_opts"] = top_level_opts
636	        if nxf_offline is not None:
637	            env["NXF_OFFLINE"] = nxf_offline
638	        else:
639	            env.pop("NXF_OFFLINE", None)
640	        # `set -e` without pipefail mirrors how the platform runs an applet script
641	        # (execserver bash template), so a helper that aborts the job is caught here
642	        result = subprocess.run(
643	            ["bash", "-c", "set -e; source '{}'; {}".format(self.src_file, snippet)],
644	            env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, universal_newlines=True)
645	        if expect_error:
646	            self.assertNotEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stdout)
647	        else:
648	            self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0, result.stderr)
649	        described = []
650	        if os.path.exists(calls_file):
651	            with open(calls_file) as f:
652	                described = f.read().split()
653	        return (result.stderr if expect_error else result.stdout).strip(), described

817	                                      describe_json=describe_json, run_opts=run_opts)

820	    @parameterized.expand([
821	        # The option string is only rewritten when a token actually changed, so a run that has
822	        # nothing to do with offline mode gets its options through untouched. `read -a` used to
823	        # rebuild the string from a single line, which silently dropped everything after a line
824	        # break and collapsed repeated spaces inside quoted values -- on every run, offline or not.
825	        ("line_break_preserved", "-resume\n-profile docker", '{"jobOutboundInternet":true}',

856	    @parameterized.expand([
857	        # A value the user quoted arrives with the quotes attached; without normalising it, the
858	        # token matched no pattern and reached Nextflow, which rejects it as an unknown option
859	        ('double_quoted_true', '-offline="true"', "true", ""),

924	        ("preset_false_left_alone_when_online", "false", '{"jobOutboundInternet":true}', "false"),

933	        # variable is belt-and-braces for a launcher that only honours the dedicated knob
934	        flag, _calls = self._run_bash(
935	            'setup_offline_mode >/dev/null; echo "${NXF_DISABLE_CHECK_LATEST:-unset}"',

939	    def test_src_reports_offline_mode_in_context_info(self):
940	        # Asserts the observability contract, not how it is written: the exact echo text and the
941	        # variable-expansion syntax are free to change as long as both branches still report the
942	        # mode with a reason. Note this only inspects the rendered script -- it cannot show that
943	        # the line is reached, and it is not: a Nextflow failure inside get_nextflow_environment
944	        # aborts before log_context_info runs.

946	        # setup_offline_mode is not only defined, it is called

948	                               if l.strip() == "setup_offline_mode"]), 0)
949	        # both branches report the mode, and each states a reason
950	        reported = [l for l in src.splitlines() if "NF offline mode" in l]
951	        self.assertEqual(len(reported), 2, reported)

17	'''

20	
21	The following helper functions are useful shortcuts for interacting with Database objects.

23	'''
24	
25	from __future__ import print_function, unicode_literals, division, absolute_import

27	import os, sys, math, mmap, stat

40	from ..exceptions import DXFileError, DXChecksumMismatchError, DXIncompleteReadsError, err_exit
41	from ..utils import response_iterator
42	import subprocess
43	
44	def download_dxdatabasefile(dxid, dst_filename, src_filename, file_status, chunksize=dxfile.DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE, append=False, show_progress=False,
45	                            project=None, describe_output=None, **kwargs):
46	    '''
47	    :param dxid: DNAnexus database ID or DXDatabase (database handler) object
48	    :type dxid: string or DXDatabase
49	    :param dst_filename: Local filename
50	    :type dst_filename: string
51	    :param src_filename: Name of database file or folder being downloaded
52	    :type src_filename: string
53	    :param file_status: Metadata for the source file being downloaded
54	    :type file_status: dict
55	    :param append: If True, appends to the local file (default is to truncate local file if it exists)
56	    :type append: boolean
57	    :param project: project to use as context for this download (may affect
58	            which billing account is billed for this download). If None or
59	            DXFile.NO_PROJECT_HINT, no project hint is supplied to the API server.
60	    :type project: str or None
61	    :param describe_output: (experimental) output of the database-xxxx/describe API call,
62	            if available. It will make it possible to skip another describe API call.
63	            It should contain the default fields of the describe API call output and
64	            the "parts" field, not included in the output by default.
65	    :type describe_output: dict or None
66	
67	    Downloads the remote file referenced by *src_filename* from database referenced
68	    by *dxid* and saves it to *dst_filename*.
69	
70	    Example::
71	
72	        download_dxdatabasefile("database-xxxx", "localfilename", "tablename/data.parquet)
73	
74	    '''
75	    # retry the inner loop while there are retriable errors
76	
77	    part_retry_counter = defaultdict(lambda: 3)
78	    success = False
79	    while not success:
80	        success = _download_dxdatabasefile(dxid,
81	                                           dst_filename,
82	                                           src_filename,
83	                                           file_status,
84	                                           part_retry_counter,
85	                                           chunksize=chunksize,
86	                                           append=append,
87	                                           show_progress=show_progress,
88	                                           project=project,
89	                                           describe_output=describe_output,
90	                                           **kwargs)
91	
92	
93	# Check if a program (wget, curl, etc.) is on the path, and
94	# can be called.
95	def _which(program):
96	    def is_exe(fpath):
97	        return os.path.isfile(fpath) and os.access(fpath, os.X_OK)
98	
99	    for path in os.environ["PATH"].split(os.pathsep):
100	        exe_file = os.path.join(path, program)
101	        if is_exe(exe_file):
102	            return exe_file
103	    return None
104	
105	# Caluclate the md5 checkum for [filename], and raise
106	# an exception if the checksum is wrong.
107	def _verify(filename, md5digest):
108	    md5sum_exe = _which("md5sum")
109	    if md5sum_exe is None:
110	        err_exit("md5sum is not installed on this system")
111	    cmd = [md5sum_exe, "-b", filename]
112	    try:
113	        print("Calculating checksum")
114	        cmd_out = subprocess.check_output(cmd)
115	    except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
116	        err_exit("Failed to run md5sum: " + str(cmd))
117	
118	    line = cmd_out.strip().split()
119	    if len(line) != 2:
120	        err_exit("md5sum returned weird results: " + str(line))
121	    actual_md5 = line[0]
122	    md5digest = md5digest.encode("ascii")
123	
124	    # python-3 : both digests have to be in bytes
125	    if actual_md5 != md5digest:
126	        err_exit("Checksum doesn't match " + str(actual_md5) + "  expected:" + str(md5digest))
127	    print("Checksum correct")
128	
129	def do_debug(msg):
130	    logger.debug(msg)
131	
132	def _download_dxdatabasefile(dxid, filename, src_filename, file_status, part_retry_counter,
133	                     chunksize=dxfile.DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE, append=False, show_progress=False,
134	                     project=None, describe_output=None, **kwargs):
135	    '''
136	    Core of download logic. Download the specified file/folder *src_filename*
137	    associated with database-id *dxid* and store it in
138	    a local file *filename*.
139	
140	    The return value is as follows:
141	    - True means the download was successfully completed
142	    - False means the download was stopped because of a retryable error
143	    - Exception raised for other errors
144	    '''
145	    def print_progress(bytes_downloaded, file_size, action="Downloaded"):
146	        num_ticks = 60
147	
148	        effective_file_size = file_size or 1
149	        if bytes_downloaded > effective_file_size:
150	            effective_file_size = bytes_downloaded
151	
152	        ticks = int(round((bytes_downloaded / float(effective_file_size)) * num_ticks))
153	        percent = int(math.floor((bytes_downloaded / float(effective_file_size)) * 100))
154	
155	        fmt = "[{done}{pending}] {action} {done_bytes:,}{remaining} bytes ({percent}%) {name}"
156	        # Erase the line and return the cursor to the start of the line.
157	        # The following VT100 escape sequence will erase the current line.
158	        sys.stderr.write("\33[2K")
159	        sys.stderr.write(fmt.format(action=action,
160	                                    done=("=" * (ticks - 1) + ">") if ticks > 0 else "",
161	                                    pending=" " * (num_ticks - ticks),
162	                                    done_bytes=bytes_downloaded,
163	                                    remaining=" of {size:,}".format(size=file_size) if file_size else "",
164	                                    percent=percent,
165	                                    name=filename))
166	        sys.stderr.flush()
167	        sys.stderr.write("\r")
168	        sys.stderr.flush()
169	
170	    _bytes = 0
171	
172	    if isinstance(dxid, DXDatabase):
173	        dxdatabase = dxid
174	    else:
175	        dxdatabase = DXDatabase(dxid, project=(project if project != DXFile.NO_PROJECT_HINT else None))
176	
177	    do_debug("dxdatabase_functions.py _download_dxdatabasefile - dxdatabase: {}".format(dxdatabase)) 
178	
179	    if describe_output and describe_output.get("parts") is not None:
180	        dxdatabase_desc = describe_output
181	    else:
182	        dxdatabase_desc = dxdatabase.describe(fields={"parts"}, default_fields=True, **kwargs)
183	
184	    # For database files, the whole parquet file is one 'part'.
185	    # Consider a multi part download approach in the future.
186	    parts = {u'1': {u'state': u'complete', u'size': file_status["size"]}}
187	    parts_to_get = sorted(parts, key=int)
188	    file_size = file_status["size"]
189	
190	    offset = 0
191	    for part_id in parts_to_get:
192	        parts[part_id]["start"] = offset
193	        offset += parts[part_id]["size"]
194	
195	    do_debug("dxdatabase_functions.py _download_dxdatabasefile - parts {}".format(parts))
196	
197	    # Create proper destination path, including any subdirectories needed within path.
198	    ensure_local_dir(filename);
199	    dest_path = os.path.join(filename, src_filename)
200	    dest_dir_idx = dest_path.rfind("/");
201	    if dest_dir_idx != -1:
202	        dest_dir = dest_path[:dest_dir_idx]
203	        ensure_local_dir(dest_dir)      
204	
205	    do_debug("dxdatabase_functions.py _download_dxdatabasefile - dest_path {}".format(dest_path)) 
206	
207	    if append:
208	        fh = open(dest_path, "ab")
209	    else:
210	        try:
211	            fh = open(dest_path, "rb+")
212	        except IOError:
213	            fh = open(dest_path, "wb")
214	
215	    if show_progress:
216	        print_progress(0, None)
217	
218	    def get_chunk(part_id_to_get, start, end):
219	        do_debug("dxdatabase_functions.py get_chunk - start {}, end {}, part id {}".format(start, end, part_id_to_get))
220	        url, headers = dxdatabase.get_download_url(src_filename=src_filename, project=project, **kwargs)
221	        # No sub ranges for database file downloads
222	        sub_range = False
223	        data = dxpy._dxhttp_read_range(url, headers, start, end, FILE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT, sub_range)
224	        return part_id_to_get, data
225	
226	    def chunk_requests():
227	        for part_id_to_chunk in parts_to_get:
228	            part_info = parts[part_id_to_chunk]
229	            for chunk_start in range(part_info["start"], part_info["start"] + part_info["size"], chunksize):
230	                chunk_end = min(chunk_start + chunksize, part_info["start"] + part_info["size"]) - 1
231	                yield get_chunk, [part_id_to_chunk, chunk_start, chunk_end], {}
232	
233	    def verify_part(_part_id, got_bytes, hasher):
234	        if got_bytes is not None and got_bytes != parts[_part_id]["size"]:
235	            msg = "Unexpected part data size in {} part {} (expected {}, got {})"
236	            msg = msg.format(dxdatabase.get_id(), _part_id, parts[_part_id]["size"], got_bytes)
237	            raise DXPartLengthMismatchError(msg)
238	        if hasher is not None and "md5" not in parts[_part_id]:
239	            warnings.warn("Download of file {} is not being checked for integrity".format(dxdatabase.get_id()))
240	        elif hasher is not None and hasher.hexdigest() != parts[_part_id]["md5"]:
241	            msg = "Checksum mismatch in {} part {} (expected {}, got {})"
242	            msg = msg.format(dxdatabase.get_id(), _part_id, parts[_part_id]["md5"], hasher.hexdigest())
243	            raise DXChecksumMismatchError(msg)
244	
245	    with fh:
246	
247	        try:
248	            # Main loop. In parallel: download chunks, verify them, and write them to disk.
249	            get_first_chunk_sequentially = (file_size > 128 * 1024 and dxpy.JOB_ID)
250	            cur_part, got_bytes, hasher = None, None, None
251	            for chunk_part, chunk_data in response_iterator(chunk_requests(),
252	                                                            dxdatabase._http_threadpool,
253	                                                            do_first_task_sequentially=get_first_chunk_sequentially):
254	                if chunk_part != cur_part:
255	                    # TODO: remove permanently if we don't find use for this
256	                    # verify_part(cur_part, got_bytes, hasher)
257	
258	                    cur_part, got_bytes, hasher = chunk_part, 0, md5_hasher()
259	                got_bytes += len(chunk_data)
260	                hasher.update(chunk_data)
261	                fh.write(chunk_data)
262	                if show_progress:
263	                    _bytes += len(chunk_data)
264	                    print_progress(_bytes, file_size)
265	            # TODO: same as above
266	            # verify_part(cur_part, got_bytes, hasher)
267	            if show_progress:
268	                print_progress(_bytes, file_size, action="Completed")
269	        except DXFileError:
270	            print(traceback.format_exc(), file=sys.stderr)
271	            part_retry_counter[cur_part] -= 1
272	            if part_retry_counter[cur_part] > 0:
273	                print("Retrying {} ({} tries remain for part {})".format(dxdatabase.get_id(), part_retry_counter[cur_part], cur_part),
274	                      file=sys.stderr)
275	                return False
276	            raise
277	
278	        if show_progress:
279	            sys.stderr.write("\n")
280	
281	        return True
282	
283	def ensure_local_dir(d):
284	    if not os.path.isdir(d):
285	        if os.path.exists(d):
286	            raise DXFileError("Destination location '{}' already exists and is not a directory".format(d))
287	        logger.debug("Creating destination directory: '%s'", d)
288	        os.makedirs(d)

42	    # Increase HTTP request buffer size when we are running within the
43	    # platform.
44	    DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE = 1024*1024*96
45	
46	MD5_READ_CHUNK_SIZE = 1024*1024*4
47	FILE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 60
48	
49	
50	def _validate_headers(headers):
51	    for key, value in headers.items():
52	        if not isinstance(key, basestring):
53	            raise ValueError("Expected key %r of headers to be a string" % (key,))
54	        if not isinstance(value, basestring):
55	            raise ValueError("Expected value %r of headers (associated with key %r) to be a string"
56	                             % (value, key))
57	    return headers
58	
59	
60	def _readable_part_size(num_bytes):
61	    "Returns the file size in readable form."
62	    B = num_bytes
63	    KB = float(1024)
64	    MB = float(KB * 1024)
65	    GB = float(MB * 1024)
66	    TB = float(GB * 1024)
67	
68	    if B < KB:
69	        return '{0} {1}'.format(B, 'bytes' if B != 1 else 'byte')
70	    elif KB <= B < MB:
71	        return '{0:.2f} KiB'.format(B/KB)
72	    elif MB <= B < GB:
73	        return '{0:.2f} MiB'.format(B/MB)
74	    elif GB <= B < TB:
75	        return '{0:.2f} GiB'.format(B/GB)
76	    elif TB <= B:
77	        return '{0:.2f} TiB'.format(B/TB)
78	
79	def do_debug(msg):
80	    logger.debug(msg)
81	
82	class DXDatabase(DXDataObject):
83	    '''Remote database object handler.
84	
85	    :param dxid: Object ID
86	    :type dxid: string
87	    :param project: Project ID
88	    :type project: string
89	
90	    '''
91	
92	    _class = "database"
93	
94	    _describe = staticmethod(dxpy.api.file_describe)
95	
96	    _http_threadpool_size = DXFILE_HTTP_THREADS
97	    _http_threadpool = dxpy.utils.get_futures_threadpool(max_workers=_http_threadpool_size)
98	
99	    NO_PROJECT_HINT = 'NO_PROJECT_HINT'
100	
101	    def __init__(self, dxid=None, project=None, read_buffer_size=DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE,
102	                 expected_file_size=None, file_is_mmapd=False):
103	        """
104	        :param dxid: Object ID
105	        :type dxid: string
106	        :param project: Project ID
107	        :type project: string
108	        :param read_buffer_size: size of read buffer in bytes
109	        :type read_buffer_size: int
110	        :param expected_file_size: size of data that will be written, if
111	            known
112	        :type expected_file_size: int
113	        :param file_is_mmapd: True if input file is mmap'd (if so, the
114	            write buffer size will be constrained to be a multiple of
115	            the allocation granularity)
116	        :type file_is_mmapd: bool
117	        """
118	
119	        DXDataObject.__init__(self, dxid=dxid, project=project)
120	
121	        self._read_buf = BytesIO()
122	        self._read_bufsize = read_buffer_size
123	        self._expected_file_size = expected_file_size
124	        self._file_is_mmapd = file_is_mmapd
125	
126	        # These are cached once for all download threads. This saves calls to the apiserver.
127	        self._download_url, self._download_url_headers, self._download_url_expires = None, None, None
128	
129	        # This lock protects accesses to the above three variables, ensuring that they would
130	        # be checked and changed atomically. This protects against thread race conditions.
131	        self._url_download_mutex = Lock()
132	
133	        self._request_iterator, self._response_iterator = None, None
134	        self._http_threadpool_futures = set()
135	
136	
137	    def get_download_url(self, filename=None, src_filename=None, project=None, **kwargs):
138	        """
139	        :param filename: desired filename of the local downloaded file
140	        :type filename: str
141	        :param project: ID of a project containing the file (the download URL
142	            will be associated with this project, and this may affect which
143	            billing account is billed for this download).
144	            If no project is specified, an attempt will be made to verify if the database is
145	            in the project from the DXDatabase handler (as specified by the user or
146	            the current project stored in dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID). Otherwise, no hint is supplied.
147	            This fall back behavior does not happen inside a job environment.
148	        :type project: str
149	        :returns: download URL and dict containing HTTP headers to be supplied
150	            with the request
151	        :rtype: tuple (str, dict)
152	        :raises: :exc:`~dxpy.exceptions.ResourceNotFound` if a project context was
153	            given and the database was not found in that project context.
154	        :raises: :exc:`~dxpy.exceptions.ResourceNotFound` if no project context was
155	            given and the database was not found in any projects.
156	
157	        Obtains a URL that can be used to directly download files associated
158	        with the specified database.
159	
160	        """
161	
162	        args = {}
163	
164	        if src_filename is not None:
165	            args["filename"] = src_filename
166	
167	        # If project=None, we fall back to the project attached to this handler
168	        # (if any). If this is supplied, it's treated as a hint: if it's a
169	        # project in which this file exists, it's passed on to the
170	        # apiserver. Otherwise, NO hint is supplied. In principle supplying a
171	        # project in the handler that doesn't contain this file ought to be an
172	        # error, but it's this way for backwards compatibility. We don't know
173	        # who might be doing downloads and creating handlers without being
174	        # careful that the project encoded in the handler contains the file
175	        # being downloaded. They may now rely on such behavior.
176	        if project is None and 'DX_JOB_ID' not in os.environ:
177	            project_from_handler = self.get_proj_id()
178	            if project_from_handler and object_exists_in_project(self.get_id(), project_from_handler):
179	                project = project_from_handler
180	
181	        if project is not None and project is not DXDatabase.NO_PROJECT_HINT:
182	            args["projectContext"] = project
183	
184	        # Test hook to write 'project' argument passed to API call to a
185	        # local file
186	        if '_DX_DUMP_BILLED_PROJECT' in os.environ:
187	            with open(os.environ['_DX_DUMP_BILLED_PROJECT'], "w") as fd:
188	                if project is not None and project != DXDatabase.NO_PROJECT_HINT:
189	                    fd.write(project)
190	
191	        with self._url_download_mutex:
192	
193	            if self._download_url is None or self._download_url_expires < time.time():
194	                # The idea here is to cache a download URL for the entire file, that will
195	                # be good for a few minutes. This avoids each thread having to ask the
196	                # server for a URL, increasing server load.
197	                #
198	                # To avoid thread race conditions, this check/update procedure is protected
199	                # with a lock.
200	
201	                # logging.debug("Download URL unset or expired, requesting a new one")
202	                if "timeout" not in kwargs:
203	                    kwargs["timeout"] = FILE_REQUEST_TIMEOUT
204	                do_debug("dxdatabase get_download_url - download_file args = {}".format(args))
205	                resp = dxpy.api.database_download_file(self._dxid, args, **kwargs)
206	                do_debug("dxdatabase get_download_url - download_file resp = {}".format(resp));
207	                self._download_url = resp["url"]
208	                self._download_url_headers = _validate_headers(resp.get("headers", {}))
209	                self._download_url_expires = 32503680000  # doesn't expire (year 3000)
210	
211	            # Make a copy, ensuring each thread has its own mutable
212	            # version of the headers.  Note: python strings are
213	            # immutable, so we can safely give a reference to the
214	            # download url.
215	            retval_download_url = self._download_url
216	            retval_download_url_headers = copy.copy(self._download_url_headers)
217	
218	        return retval_download_url, retval_download_url_headers
