150	            log.info(f"Retrying docker manifest inspect for {ref} in {delay}s (attempt {i + 1}/{len(attempts)})")
151	            time.sleep(delay)
152	        try:
153	            result = subprocess.run(
154	                ["docker", "manifest", "inspect", ref],
155	                capture_output=True, text=True,
156	            )
157	            if result.returncode == 0:
158	                return json.loads(result.stdout)
159	            log.warning(f"docker manifest inspect failed for {ref} (rc={result.returncode}, attempt {i + 1}/{len(attempts)})")
160	        except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError) as e:
161	            log.warning(f"docker manifest inspect error for {ref} (attempt {i + 1}/{len(attempts)}): {e}")
162	    return None
163	
164	
165	def _resolve_digest(full_ref, use_manifest_digest=False):
166	    """Resolve the image digest via ``docker manifest inspect``.
167	
168	    By default returns the **config digest** (``config.digest``), which is
169	    the same value as ``docker images --no-trunc``.  This matches the
170	    lookup behavior of nextaur >= 1.12.1.
171	
172	    When ``use_manifest_digest=True``, returns the **platform manifest
173	    digest** instead (a single API call).  This matches the lookup
174	    behavior of older nextaur versions (< 1.12.1) which use the manifest
175	    digest from ``docker manifest inspect`` to search the cache.
176	
177	    For multi-arch images with ``use_manifest_digest=False``, this
178	    requires two calls: one to get the manifest list, then a second to
179	    fetch the platform manifest and extract its config digest.
180	
181	    Single-arch images always return the config digest directly,
182	    regardless of ``use_manifest_digest``.  This is safe because old
183	    nextaur's ``implicitLatestGetDigest()`` cannot parse single-arch
184	    manifests (no ``manifests`` array) and returns null, so it never
185	    does a digest-based lookup for single-arch images.
186	
187	    Returns the ``sha256:...`` digest string, or ``None`` on failure.
188	    """
189	    data = _docker_manifest_inspect(full_ref)
190	    if data is None:
191	        return None
192	
193	    # Multi-arch: find the amd64/linux manifest.
194	    manifests = data.get("manifests") or []
195	    for manifest in manifests:
196	        platform = manifest.get("platform", {})
197	        if (platform.get("architecture") == "amd64"
198	                and platform.get("os") == "linux"):
199	            platform_digest = manifest.get("digest")
200	            if not platform_digest:
201	                break
202	            if use_manifest_digest:
203	                return platform_digest
204	            return _get_config_digest(full_ref, platform_digest)
205	
206	    # Single-arch: config digest is directly in the flat manifest
207	    config = data.get("config")
208	    if isinstance(config, dict):
209	        config_digest = config.get("digest")
210	        if config_digest:
211	            return config_digest
212	
213	    log.warning(f"No digest found for {full_ref}")
214	    return None
215	
216	
217	def _get_config_digest(image_ref, platform_digest):
218	    """Fetch the config digest from a platform-specific manifest.
219	
220	    Given the platform manifest digest (from a multi-arch manifest list),
221	    fetches ``<image_ref>@<platform_digest>`` and extracts ``config.digest``.
222	    """
223	    # Strip :tag from image_ref (e.g. "quay.io/bio/samtools:1.17" → "quay.io/bio/samtools")
224	    # so we can address the platform manifest by digest.  Use the same
225	    # host:port disambiguation as _parse_docker_ref: the tag is after
226	    # the last colon only if there's no "/" after it.
227	    colon_idx = image_ref.rfind(":")
228	    if colon_idx != -1 and "/" not in image_ref[colon_idx + 1:]:
229	        base_ref = image_ref[:colon_idx]
230	    else:
231	        base_ref = image_ref
232	    ref_by_digest = f"{base_ref}@{platform_digest}"
233	    data = _docker_manifest_inspect(ref_by_digest)
234	    if data is None:
235	        return None
236	    config = data.get("config")
237	    if isinstance(config, dict):
238	        return config.get("digest")
239	    log.warning(f"No config digest in platform manifest for {ref_by_digest}")
240	    return None
241	
242	
243	def collect_docker_images(resources_dir, profile, nextflow_pipeline_params, use_manifest_digest=False):
244	    """Collect container image references using ``nextflow inspect``.
245	
246	    Uses the native ``nextflow inspect`` command.  It scans
247	    pipeline ``include`` statements statically — no plugins, parameters,
248	    or profile are required for container discovery.
249	
250	    :param resources_dir: Path to the local(ized) NF pipeline.
251	    :type resources_dir: str
252	    :param profile: Custom Nextflow profile (comma-separated, no spaces).
253	    :type profile: str
254	    :param nextflow_pipeline_params: Pipeline parameters forwarded to inspect
255	        (e.g. ``"--input samplesheet.csv --outdir results"``).  Some older
256	        nf-core pipelines have hard parameter validation that runs before
257	        process definitions are reached; passing the required params here
258	        lets ``nextflow inspect`` get past those checks.
259	    :type nextflow_pipeline_params: str
260	    :param use_manifest_digest: If True, store the platform manifest digest
261	        (instead of config digest) for latest/untagged images.  This is needed
262	        for nextaur versions prior to 1.12.1 which look up cached images by
263	        manifest digest.  Only affects images without a specific tag — tagged
264	        images always use config digest for cache deduplication consistency.
265	    :type use_manifest_digest: bool
266	    :returns: List of dicts with keys: process, repository, image_name,
267	              tag, digest, file_id, engine.
268	    """
269	    cmd_parts = ["nextflow", "inspect", resources_dir, "-format", "json"]
270	    if profile:
271	        cmd_parts.extend(["-profile", profile])
272	    if nextflow_pipeline_params:
273	        try:
274	            cmd_parts.extend(shlex.split(nextflow_pipeline_params))
275	        except ValueError as e:
276	            raise ImageRefFactoryError(f"Malformed pipeline parameters: {e}")
277	
278	    process = subprocess.run(cmd_parts, capture_output=True, text=True)
279	    if process.returncode != 0:
280	        raise ImageRefFactoryError(
281	            f"nextflow inspect failed (rc={process.returncode}): stdout: {process.stdout}\nstderr: {process.stderr}")
282	
283	    try:
284	        inspect_data = json.loads(process.stdout)
285	    except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError) as e:
286	        raise ImageRefFactoryError(f"Failed to parse nextflow inspect output: {e}")
287	
288	    processes = inspect_data.get("processes", [])
289	    if not processes:
290	        log.warning("No processes found in nextflow inspect output")
291	        return []
292	
293	    image_refs = []
294	    resolved_digests = {}
295	    _progress(f"Resolving {len(processes)} container image(s) from pipeline...")
296	    for entry in processes:
297	        container = entry.get("container", "")
298	        if not container:
299	            continue
300	
301	        # dx:// URIs reference platform files directly — no pull/save/upload
302	        # needed. Extract the file ID so _package_bundle() reuses it.
303	        if container.startswith("dx://"):
304	            _, file_id = _parse_dx_uri(container)
305	            if not file_id:
306	                raise ImageRefFactoryError(f"Could not parse dx:// URI: {container}")
307	            _progress(f"  {container} -> platform file")
308	            image_refs.append(_ImageRef(
309	                process=entry.get("name", ""),
310	                repository=None,
311	                image_name=file_id,
312	                tag=None,
313	                digest=None,
314	                file_id=file_id,
315	                engine="docker",
316	            ))
317	            continue
318	
319	        repository, image_name, tag, digest = _parse_docker_ref(container)
320	
321	        # Reject refs that specify both tag and digest. A ref should
322	        # identify an image by tag OR by digest, not both.
323	        if tag and digest:
324	            raise ImageRefFactoryError(f"Image reference has both tag and digest: {container}")
325	
326	        # Track whether the digest came from the original reference (@sha256:...)
327	        # vs resolved by us. Original digests are manifest digests (pullable),
328	        # resolved digests are config digests (not pullable, used for cache only).
329	        digest_is_original = bool(digest)
330	
331	        # Resolve registry digest for all images that don't already have one.
332	        # The digest is used for cache validation in _populate_cached_file_ids()
333	        # to prevent cross-registry collisions (see dx-toolkit/devdocs/nextflow/cache_collision_scenarios.md).
334	        if not digest:
335	            full_ref = (repository or "") + image_name
336	            if tag:
337	                full_ref += ":" + tag
338	            # Only use manifest digest for latest/untagged images where old
339	            # nextaur (<1.12.1) does a digest-based lookup.  Tagged images use
340	            # name-based lookup at runtime, so keep config digest for cache
341	            # deduplication consistency with existing cached files.
342	            # Note: "image" and "image:latest" get separate cache keys via
343	            # full_ref, but both use manifest digest when use_manifest_digest
344	            # is True — old nextaur treats both as implicit-latest.
345	            is_implicit_latest = not tag or tag.lower() == "latest"
346	            effective_use_manifest = use_manifest_digest and is_implicit_latest
347	            cache_key = (full_ref, effective_use_manifest)
348	            if cache_key not in resolved_digests:
349	                resolved_digests[cache_key] = _resolve_digest(full_ref, use_manifest_digest=effective_use_manifest)
350	            digest = resolved_digests[cache_key]
351	
352	        display_ref = (repository or "") + image_name + (":" + tag if tag else "")
353	        if digest:
354	            # Show algo prefix (sha256:) + first 12 hex chars
355	            _progress(f"  {display_ref} (digest: {digest[:19]}...)")
356	        else:
357	            _progress(f"  {display_ref} (digest: unresolved)")
358	
359	        image_refs.append(_ImageRef(
360	            process=entry.get("name", ""),
361	            repository=repository,
362	            image_name=image_name,
363	            tag=tag,
364	            digest=digest,
365	            file_id=None,
366	            engine="docker",
367	            digest_is_original=digest_is_original,
368	        ))
369	
370	    _populate_cached_file_ids(image_refs)
371	    return [dataclasses.asdict(ref) for ref in image_refs]
372	
373	
374	def _populate_cached_file_ids(image_refs):
375	    """Look up previously cached Docker images in the current project.
376	
377	    Searches ``/.cached_docker_images/<image_name>/`` for files matching
378	    ``<image_name>_<tag>``.  When found, verifies the image digest stored
379	    in the file's ``properties`` and populates ``file_id`` so that
380	    ``DockerImageRef._package_bundle()`` skips the pull/save/upload cycle
381	    and reuses the existing platform file.
382	
383	    This benefits:
384	    - Repeat builds of the same pipeline (faster rebuilds)
385	    - Colleagues in the same project building other pipelines that share
386	      images (e.g. samtools, fastqc are used across many nf-core pipelines)
387	    """
388	    project_id = config.get("DX_PROJECT_CONTEXT_ID")
389	    if not project_id:
390	        return
391	
392	    # Skip cache lookup when digest is unknown (e.g. _resolve_digest
393	    # failed).  Without a digest we cannot guarantee correctness of
394	    # the cache hit.  Also skip refs that already have a file_id (dx:// URIs).
395	    cacheable = [ref for ref in image_refs if ref.digest and not ref.file_id]
396	    if not cacheable:
397	        return
398	
399	    _progress(f"Checking project cache for {len(cacheable)} docker image(s)...")
400	    cache_hits = 0
401	    for ref in cacheable:
402	        display = ref.image_name + (":" + ref.tag if ref.tag else "")
403	        cache_file_name = "_".join(filter(lambda x: x, [ref.image_name, ref.tag]))
404	        cache_folder = f"/.cached_docker_images/{ref.image_name}/"
405	
406	        try:
407	            results = list(find_data_objects(
408	                classname="file",
409	                state="closed",
410	                project=project_id,
411	                folder=cache_folder,
412	                name=cache_file_name,
413	                properties={"image_digest": ref.digest},
414	                describe={"fields": {"name": True, "folder": True, "project": True}},
415	                limit=1,
416	            ))
417	        except Exception as e:
418	            log.warning(f"Docker image cache: failed to search for {display}: {e}")
419	            _progress(f"  {display}: SKIP (lookup error)")
420	            continue
421	
422	        if results:
423	            ref.file_id = results[0]["id"]
424	            cache_hits += 1
425	            desc = results[0]["describe"]
426	            _progress(f"  {display}: CACHED ({desc['project']}:{desc['folder']}/{desc['name']} ({results[0]['id']}))")
427	        else:
428	            _progress(f"  {display}: MISS (will pull and upload)")
429	
430	    cache_misses = len(cacheable) - cache_hits
431	    _progress(f"Docker image cache: {cache_hits} cached, {cache_misses} to upload")
432

6	class ImageRefFactoryError(Exception):
7	    """
8	    Class to handle errors with instantiation of ImageRef subclasses

12	class ImageRefFactory(object):
13	    def __init__(
14	            self,
15	            image_ref
16	    ):
17	        """
18	        A class to instantiate subclasses of ImageRef based on the container engine. Ususally instantiated after using the
19	        nextaur:collect function to collect images for docker and other container engines.
20	        :param image_ref: Image ref details
21	        :type image_ref: Dict
22	        """
23	        self._image_ref = image_ref
24	        self._engine = image_ref.get("engine", None)
25	        if not self._engine:
26	            raise ImageRefFactoryError("Provide the container engine")
27	        self._imageRef_switch = {
28	            "docker": DockerImageRef
29	        }
30	
31	    def get_image(self):
32	        image = self._imageRef_switch.get(self._engine, None)
33	        if not image:
34	            raise ImageRefFactoryError(f"Unsupported container engine: {self._engine}")
35	        return image(
36	            process=self._image_ref["process"],
37	            digest=self._image_ref["digest"],
38	            dx_file_id=self._image_ref.get("file_id", None),
39	            repository=self._image_ref.get("repository", None),
40	            image_name=self._image_ref.get("image_name", None),
41	            tag=self._image_ref.get("tag", None),

1	# Output format
2	
3	A run leaves four files in the repository's root — the directory you were
4	started in, next to its README — and nowhere else: not in a subdirectory, not
5	in a scratch directory. They are your record of the work, not edits to the
6	code, so writing them there does not touch the repository:
7	
8	- **`step1.jsonl`**, **`step2.jsonl`**, **`step3.jsonl`** — what each step
9	  produced, one JSON line per record. Each is finished with
10	  `python $SKILL/scripts/step.py done N`, and read-only after that.
11	- **`submissions.jsonl`** — the repairs, one per line, written in step 3. The
12	  script measures each and writes the result into it.
13	
14	Nothing else is written. Your summary at the end of the run is your final
15	message, not a file.
16	
17	---
18	
19	## step1.jsonl to step3.jsonl
20	
21	One JSON object per line, in the file of the step that produced it, each
22	tagged with its step.
23	
24	**Every record has exactly the keys listed for it — all of them, every time,
25	and no others.** A key with nothing to say is `null` or `[]`, never left out.
26	The same keys in every run are what make runs comparable.
27	
28	| Record | One per | Keys |
29	|---|---|---|
30	| step 1, in `step1.jsonl` | unit where something may be wasteful | `step`, `unit`, `suspicions` |
31	| step 2, in `step2.jsonl` | unit on the step-1 list | `step`, `unit`, `what_it_does`, `decisions` |
32	| step 3, in `step3.jsonl` | unit with an accepted suspicion | `step`, `unit`, `outcomes` |
33	| a suspicion, in `suspicions` | | `label`, `root_cause`, `lines`, `why` |
34	| a decision, in `decisions` | | `label`, `root_cause`, `lines`, `verdict`, `why` |
35	| an outcome, in `outcomes` | | `label`, `outcome`, `submission`, `why` |
36	
37	Step 4 writes no record: its output is your final message.
38	
39	Shown expanded here; each is written on a single line.
40	
41	```jsonc
42	{"step": 1, "unit": "src/render.py::Report.render", "suspicions": [
43	  {"label": "a", "root_cause": "C10.S4", "lines": [47],
44	   "why": "`self.buf` is grown with += once per row; nothing reads it in the loop"},
45	  {"label": "b", "root_cause": "C3.S2",  "lines": [44,45],
46	   "why": "`sorted(self.columns)` is recomputed per row and does not depend on the row"}
47	]}
48	```
49	
50	```jsonc
51	{"step": 2, "unit": "src/router.py::Router.allowed",
52	 "what_it_does": "checks each request against `self.blocked`, a list built once in __init__",
53	 "decisions": [
54	  {
55	    "label": "a", "root_cause": "C5.S2", "lines": [58], "verdict": "rejected",
56	    "why": "`Looks like it, but is not` — nothing needs the list's order, so the container's type changes rather than an index being added beside it. Added `b` instead."
57	  },
58	  {
59	    "label": "b", "root_cause": "C5.S1", "lines": [31], "verdict": "accepted",
60	    "why": "`self.blocked` is a list searched once per request, built in __init__ at line 31 and read nowhere else; as a set each search is one hash lookup"
61	  }
62	]}
63	```
64	
65	```jsonc
66	{"step": 3, "unit": "src/render.py::Report.render", "outcomes": [
67	  {"label": "a", "outcome": "submitted",      "submission": "C10S4-render-concat", "why": null},
68	  {"label": "b", "outcome": "same_repair_as", "submission": "C10S4-render-concat", "why": null},
69	  {"label": "c", "outcome": "blocked",        "submission": null, "why": "inputs.py: no inputs could be generated: every call opens a database connection"},
70	  {"label": "d", "outcome": "deferred",       "submission": null, "why": "outside the 20 repairs measured"}
71	]}
72	```
73	
74	### Field rules
75	
76	**`label`** names a suspicion within its unit — `a`, `b`, `c` — and is how steps
77	2 and 3 refer to it. A suspicion added in step 2 gets a label of its own.
78	
79	**`lines`** is a list of line numbers in the unit's file.
80	
81	**`why`** is the reason, under one name everywhere. On a suspicion: what looks
82	wasteful. On a decision: what decided it — for `accepted`, the mechanism, what
83	work stops happening; for `rejected`, the check that failed. On an outcome: why
84	it was `blocked` or `deferred`, and `null` otherwise. It must be specific to
85	this code: name the variable, the line, the structure. "Inefficient string
86	handling" is not a reason; "`self.buf` is grown with `+=` across `rows`" is.
87	
88	**`verdict`** is `"accepted"` or `"rejected"`.
89	
90	**`what_it_does`**, in step 2, is one sentence: what the unit computes, and
91	where its work goes. It is written after reading the unit in full, which is
92	what it shows.
93	
94	**`root_cause`** is one of the 65 IDs exactly as its card names it, such as
95	`C5.S1` — never a category such as `C5`. In step 1 it is the one the index
96	line matched; step 2 settles it against the card.
97	
98	**`outcome`**, in step 3, is one of: `submitted` (`submission` is its `id` in
99	`submissions.jsonl`), `same_repair_as` (`submission` is the `id` of the
100	submission that already makes this edit), `blocked` (the tools showed no repair
101	can be measured here — inputs that could not be generated, a module that does
102	not load, a repair that cannot be made to behave identically — and `why`
103	quotes that message) or `deferred` (accepted, and not measured: outside the 20,
104	or never tried). A suspicion you did not ask inputs for is `deferred`, not
105	`blocked`. A deferred suspicion is still a finding.
106	
107	Every unit from step 1 has a step-2 record, and every suspicion is accounted
108	for: rejected in step 2, or given an outcome in step 3. A run that examined
109	three functions and one that examined three hundred have to be
110	distinguishable, and so do a suspicion you dropped and one you forgot.
111	
112	---
113	
114	## submissions.jsonl
115	
116	Every line has every field listed in `$SKILL/reference/verifying.md` — none
117	are optional, and no others are accepted. Three rules connect it to the
118	step files:
119	
120	- every outcome `submitted` in `step3.jsonl` names a line here, and every line
121	  here is named by exactly one;
122	- every line ends with the `agent_measurement` the script wrote. Never write
123	  or edit it, and never write a verdict anywhere yourself;
124	- every measured repair stays, whatever its verdict.
125	
126	What the script writes into a line:
127	
128	```jsonc
129	"agent_measurement": {
130	  "status": "confirmed",
131	  "reason": "25.9% +-3.0% energy saved on 'many-rows', clearing the 1.4% noise floor. ...",
132	  "profile": "fast",
133	  "noise_floor_pct": 1.4,
134	  "noise_floor_from": "session calibration",
135	  "equivalence_relaxed": [],      // what this environment weakened (stand-in packages, skipped statements); repeat wherever the saving is quoted
136	  "stubbed": [],                  // uninstalled packages stood in for while loading; normally empty
137	  "per_case": [
138	    {"label": "typical", "repeats": 9500, "clamped": false,
139	     "before_energy_j": 51.03, "after_energy_j": 47.29,
140	     "before_time_s": 1.04, "after_time_s": 0.96,
141	     "energy_ci_pct": 1.2, "significant": true}
142	    // ... one row per input, all four
143	  ],
144	  "submission_hash": "3f2a9c01d4e5b6a7"
145	  // abridged: a few more fields record provenance -- the meter, its coverage, the canary case
146	}
147	```
148	
149	`per_case` carries joules and seconds for each version on every case, and no
150	percentage: the joules are the result, and a percentage stored beside them is a
151	second copy that can disagree. `energy_ci_pct` is not a saving — it is the
152	half-width of the 95% interval on the paired comparison, which `significant`
153	is judged from.
154

```jsonc
  {"label": "a", "root_cause": "C10.S4", "lines": [47],
   "why": "`self.buf` is grown with += once per row; nothing reads it in the loop"},
  {"label": "b", "root_cause": "C3.S2",  "lines": [44,45],
   "why": "`sorted(self.columns)` is recomputed per row and does not depend on the row"}
]}
```

```jsonc
{"step": 2, "unit": "src/router.py::Router.allowed",
 "what_it_does": "checks each request against `self.blocked`, a list built once in __init__",
 "decisions": [
  {
    "label": "a", "root_cause": "C5.S2", "lines": [58], "verdict": "rejected",
    "why": "`Looks like it, but is not` — nothing needs the list's order, so the container's type changes rather than an index being added beside it. Added `b` instead."
  },
  {
    "label": "b", "root_cause": "C5.S1", "lines": [31], "verdict": "accepted",
    "why": "`self.blocked` is a list searched once per request, built in __init__ at line 31 and read nowhere else; as a set each search is one hash lookup"
  }
]}
```

```jsonc
{"step": 3, "unit": "src/render.py::Report.render", "outcomes": [
  {"label": "a", "outcome": "submitted",      "submission": "C10S4-render-concat", "why": null},
  {"label": "b", "outcome": "same_repair_as", "submission": "C10S4-render-concat", "why": null},
  {"label": "c", "outcome": "blocked",        "submission": null, "why": "inputs.py: no inputs could be generated: every call opens a database connection"},
  {"label": "d", "outcome": "deferred",       "submission": null, "why": "outside the 20 repairs measured"}
]}
```

### Field rules

**`label`** names a suspicion within its unit — `a`, `b`, `c` — and is how steps
2 and 3 refer to it. A suspicion added in step 2 gets a label of its own.

**`lines`** is a list of line numbers in the unit's file.

**`why`** is the reason, under one name everywhere. On a suspicion: what looks
wasteful. On a decision: what decided it — for `accepted`, the mechanism, what
work stops happening; for `rejected`, the check that failed. On an outcome: why
it was `blocked` or `deferred`, and `null` otherwise. It must be specific to
this code: name the variable, the line, the structure. "Inefficient string
handling" is not a reason; "`self.buf` is grown with `+=` across `rows`" is.

**`verdict`** is `"accepted"` or `"rejected"`.

**`what_it_does`**, in step 2, is one sentence: what the unit computes, and
where its work goes. It is written after reading the unit in full, which is
what it shows.

**`root_cause`** is one of the 65 IDs exactly as its card names it, such as
`C5.S1` — never a category such as `C5`. In step 1 it is the one the index
line matched; step 2 settles it against the card.

**`outcome`**, in step 3, is one of: `submitted` (`submission` is its `id` in
`submissions.jsonl`), `same_repair_as` (`submission` is the `id` of the
submission that already makes this edit), `blocked` (the tools showed no repair
can be measured here — inputs that could not be generated, a module that does
not load, a repair that cannot be made to behave identically — and `why`
quotes that message) or `deferred` (accepted, and not measured: outside the 20,
or never tried). A suspicion you did not ask inputs for is `deferred`, not
`blocked`. A deferred suspicion is still a finding.

Every unit from step 1 has a step-2 record, and every suspicion is accounted
for: rejected in step 2, or given an outcome in step 3. A run that examined
three functions and one that examined three hundred have to be
distinguishable, and so do a suspicion you dropped and one you forgot.

---

## submissions.jsonl

Every line has every field listed in `$SKILL/reference/verifying.md` — none
are optional, and no others are accepted. Three rules connect it to the
step files:

- every outcome `submitted` in `step3.jsonl` names a line here, and every line
  here is named by exactly one;
- every line ends with the `agent_measurement` the script wrote. Never write
  or edit it, and never write a verdict anywhere yourself;
- every measured repair stays, whatever its verdict.

What the script writes into a line:

```jsonc
"agent_measurement": {
  "status": "confirmed",
  "reason": "25.9% +-3.0% energy saved on 'many-rows', clearing the 1.4% noise floor. ...",
  "profile": "fast",
  "noise_floor_pct": 1.4,
  "noise_floor_from": "session calibration",
  "equivalence_relaxed": [],      // what this environment weakened (stand-in packages, skipped statements); repeat wherever the saving is quoted
  "stubbed": [],                  // uninstalled packages stood in for while loading; normally empty
  "per_case": [
    {"label": "typical", "repeats": 9500, "clamped": false,
     "before_energy_j": 51.03, "after_energy_j": 47.29,
     "before_time_s": 1.04, "after_time_s": 0.96,
     "energy_ci_pct": 1.2, "significant": true}
    // ... one row per input, all four
  ],
  "submission_hash": "3f2a9c01d4e5b6a7"
  // abridged: a few more fields record provenance -- the meter, its coverage, the canary case
}
```

`per_case` carries joules and seconds for each version on every case, and no
percentage: the joules are the result, and a percentage stored beside them is a
second copy that can disagree. `energy_ci_pct` is not a saving — it is the
half-width of the 95% interval on the paired comparison, which `significant`
is judged from.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python
2	
3	import os
4	import subprocess
5	
6	from dxpy import DXFile, config, upload_local_file
7	from dxpy.exceptions import err_exit
8	
9	
10	class ImageRef(object):
11	    def __init__(
12	            self,
13	            process,
14	            digest,
15	            dx_file_id=None,
16	            repository=None,
17	            image_name=None,
18	            tag=None,
19	            digest_is_original=False
20	    ):
21	        """
22	        A class to handle an image reference from nextflow pipeline.
23	        :param process: An NPA proces name (aka task name) which uses a given image
24	        :type process: String
25	        :param digest: An image digest
26	        :type digest: String
27	        :param dx_file_id: dx file id on the platform
28	        :type dx_file_id: Optional[String]
29	        :param repository: Image repository
30	        :type repository: Optional[String]
31	        :param image_name: Image name (usually a basename of the image referenced with repository)
32	        :type image_name: Optional[String]
33	        :param tag: A version tag
34	        :type tag: Optional[String]
35	        :param digest_is_original: True if the digest came from the original image reference
36	            (@sha256:...), False if it was resolved by _resolve_digest(). Original digests
37	            are manifest digests (pullable); resolved digests are config digests (for cache
38	            validation only, not pullable).
39	        :type digest_is_original: bool
40	        """
41	        self._caching_dir = os.path.join("/.cached_docker_images/", image_name or "")
42	        self._dx_file_id = dx_file_id
43	        self._bundled_depends = None
44	        self._repository = repository
45	        self._image_name = image_name
46	        self._tag = tag
47	        self._digest = digest
48	        self._digest_is_original = digest_is_original
49	        self._process = process
50	
51	    @property
52	    def bundled_depends(self):
53	        if not self._bundled_depends:
54	            self._bundled_depends = self._package_bundle()
55	        return self._bundled_depends
56	
57	    @property
58	    def identifier(self):
59	        return self._join_if_exists("_", [self._repository, self._image_name, self._tag, self._digest])
60	
61	    def _cache(self, file_name):
62	        """
63	        Function to store an image on the platform as a dx file object. Should be implemented in subclasses.
64	        :param file_name: A file name under which the image will be saved on the platform
65	        :type file_name: String
66	        :returns: Tuple[String, String] dx file id, file name (basename)
67	        """
68	        raise NotImplementedError("Abstract class. Method not implemented. Use the concrete implementations.")
69	
70	    def _reconstruct_image_ref(self):
71	        raise NotImplementedError("Abstract class. Method not implemented. Use the concrete implementations.")
72	
73	    def _construct_cache_file_name(self):
74	        return self._join_if_exists("_", [self._image_name, self._tag])
75	
76	    @staticmethod
77	    def _join_if_exists(delimiter, parts):
78	        return delimiter.join([x for x in parts if x])
79	
80	    def _dx_file_get_name(self):
81	        dx_file_handle = DXFile(self._dx_file_id, config["DX_PROJECT_CONTEXT_ID"])
82	        return dx_file_handle.describe().get("name")
83	
84	    def _package_bundle(self):
85	        """
86	        Function to include a container image stored on the platform into NPA
87	        :returns: Dict in the format of {"name": "bundle.tar.gz", "id": {"$dnanexus_link": "file-xxxx"}}
88	        """
89	        if not self._dx_file_id:
90	            cache_file_name = self._construct_cache_file_name()
91	            self._dx_file_id = self._cache(cache_file_name)
92	        else:
93	            cache_file_name = self._dx_file_get_name()
94	        return {
95	            "name": cache_file_name,
96	            "id": {"$dnanexus_link": self._dx_file_id}
97	        }
98	
99	
100	class DockerImageRef(ImageRef):
101	    def __init__(
102	            self,
103	            process,
104	            digest,
105	            dx_file_id=None,
106	            repository=None,
107	            image_name=None,
108	            tag=None,
109	            digest_is_original=False
110	    ):
111	        super().__init__(
112	            process,
113	            digest,
114	            dx_file_id,
115	            repository,
116	            image_name,
117	            tag,
118	            digest_is_original)
119	
120	    def _cache(self, file_name):
121	        full_image_ref = self._reconstruct_image_ref()
122	        docker_pull_cmd = f"sudo docker pull {full_image_ref}"
123	        docker_save_cmd = f"sudo docker save {full_image_ref} | gzip > {file_name}"
124	        for cmd in [docker_pull_cmd, docker_save_cmd]:
125	            try:
126	                _ = subprocess.check_output(cmd, shell=True)
127	            except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
128	                err_exit(f"Failed to run a subprocess command: {cmd}")
129	        # may need wait_on_close = True??
130	        extracted_digest = self._digest
131	        if not self._digest:
132	            digest_cmd = f"docker images --no-trunc --quiet {full_image_ref}"
133	            extracted_digest = subprocess.check_output(digest_cmd, shell=True).decode().strip()
134	        uploaded_dx_file = upload_local_file(
135	            filename=file_name,
136	            project=config["DX_PROJECT_CONTEXT_ID"],
137	            folder=self._caching_dir,
138	            name=file_name,
139	            parents=True,
140	            properties={"image_digest": self._digest or extracted_digest}
141	        )
142	        return uploaded_dx_file.get_id()
143	
144	    def _reconstruct_image_ref(self):
145	        """
146	        Docker image reference has the form of <REPOSITORY_NAME>/<IMAGE_NAME>:<VERSION_TAG> or
147	        <REPOSITORY_NAME>/<IMAGE_NAME>@<DIGEST>
148	
149	        Tag takes precedence over digest so that ``docker pull`` and
150	        ``docker save`` use the human-readable tag.
151	
152	        Only original digests (from ``@sha256:...`` in the pipeline source) are
153	        used for pull — these are manifest digests that registries can resolve.
154	        Resolved digests (from ``_resolve_digest()``) are config digests used
155	        only for cache validation; they are not pullable references.
156	        """
157	        repo_and_image_name = self._join_if_exists("", [self._repository, self._image_name])
158	        if self._tag:
159	            full_ref = self._join_if_exists(":", [repo_and_image_name, self._tag])
160	        elif self._digest and self._digest_is_original:
161	            full_ref = self._join_if_exists("@", [repo_and_image_name, self._digest])
162	        else:
163	            full_ref = repo_and_image_name
164	        return full_ref

1	# Verifying a saving
2	
3	A repair comes with a claim: that this refactoring saves energy. This is how
4	the claim gets tested. Read this before writing your first submission.
5	
6	The rule: **no repair is reported as saving anything until it has been
7	measured on this machine.**
8	
9	You do not edit the repository. You describe the repair; the script applies it
10	to a copy, and `before` is whatever the repository already contains.
11	
12	---
13	
14	## The submission
15	
16	One JSON object per line of `submissions.jsonl`, one line per repair:
17	
18	```jsonc
19	{
20	  "id": "C10S4-render-concat",
21	  "root_cause": "C10.S4",
22	  "unit": "src/render.py::Report.render",
23	  "changed": {
24	    "src/render.py::Report.render": "def render(self):\n    return \"\".join(_row(r) for r in self.rows)"
25	  },
26	  "sole_caller_evidence": null,
27	  "notes": "C10.S4. Sizes taken from the fixtures in tests/; `_row` left as the real helper."
28	}
29	```
30	
31	**Every line has every field below, and no others** — none is optional; the
32	ones with nothing to say take the empty value shown.
33	
34	| Field | What it holds |
35	|---|---|
36	| `id` | a name for this repair, unique in the file |
37	| `root_cause` | the root cause the repair removes, as it appears on its card |
38	| `unit` | the function or method whose behaviour must be preserved, as `path::qualname` |
39	| `changed` | `path::qualname` → the full replacement source of that function |
40	| `sole_caller_evidence` | how you know nothing else calls or reads what you changed; `null` when `changed` holds only the unit |
41	| `notes` | a few sentences a reader would otherwise have to guess; `""` if none |
42	| `agent_measurement` | written by the script, never by you |
43	
44	`changed` holds **source text, not a diff and not an AST**: the whole function
45	as you would commit it, decorators and `def` line included, written at column
46	zero even when it is a method. Each entry replaces exactly that function and
47	nothing around it — so a repair that needs a module the file does not import
48	yet imports it inside the function. After the first call, an `import`
49	statement is a single dictionary lookup.
50	
51	## You do not supply `before`
52	
53	`before` is the function already in the repository, loaded from the file you
54	named. You cannot simplify it or substitute an illustration of the pattern,
55	because you never write it. A repair worth 30% of a five-line sketch and 2% of
56	the real function always measures against the real function.
57	
58	The rest is real too: the helpers are the real helpers, the constants the real
59	constants, the imports the real imports. So the replacement must differ from
60	the repository by **the repair alone**. If it also renames a variable, inlines
61	a helper or fixes a second thing, the measurement no longer attributes to
62	one root cause and the result is unusable.
63	
64	## Changing more than the unit
65	
66	The unit's **contract** is what has to survive: everything a caller can see,
67	listed under "What "the same" means" below.
68	Anything only the unit depends on — a helper nothing else calls, state nothing
69	else reads — is implementation detail, and may change.
70	
71	Give each changed function its own entry in `changed`, in whatever file it
72	lives, and fill in `sole_caller_evidence`: the search you ran, or the call sites
73	and attribute reads you checked. The check watches the unit's contract only, so
74	anything else broken by the change would pass every check here. A submission
75	that changes more than the unit without this is rejected.
76	
77	## Several repairs in one unit
78	
79	Each repair is written against the original code and measured against it, on
80	its own. There is no order to take them in, and no repair is built on another.
81	
82	- **The same edit** for two suspicions is one repair. Submit it once; the other
83	  suspicion is `same_repair_as` it.
84	- **Different edits to the same code** are separate repairs. Submit each.
85	- **Every repair of one unit is measured on that unit's inputs**, so their
86	  savings are measured on identical inputs and can be compared.
87	
88	## The inputs
89	
90	You do not write them. Ask for every unit you will measure, in one request:
91	
92	```bash
93	python $SKILL/scripts/inputs.py request src/render.py::Report.render src/parse.py::tokenize
94	python $SKILL/scripts/inputs.py status          # which are ready
95	```
96	
97	A generator outside this session writes each unit's inputs from the
98	repository's own code — the unit, its class, what it uses, and where the
99	repository calls it. It asks for more candidates than it needs, runs each on
100	the original code, keeps those that complete and give the same output on a
101	second, fresh run, and of those keeps the four that do the most work. They are
102	fixed for the unit: every repair of it is measured on the same four, and so is
103	the re-measurement after the session, which uses our own copy of them.
104	
105	Requests open in step 3, at `step.py done 2`. The request returns at once.
106	Generation runs outside this session, every unit at the same time, and usually
107	takes a minute or two; a hard unit can take five. Ask for all of them in one
108	request; a unit you add later is another request. Up to 30 units can have
109	inputs or be generating at once: more than the 20 repairs measured, so there is
110	room for units you decide against. A unit that fails gives its place back, so
111	ask for another in its place; up to 30 different units may fail in a session.
112	
113	verify.py does not measure while anything is still being generated: it waits
114	first, up to ten minutes, printing which units it is waiting for. Give its
115	first run a timeout to match — fifteen minutes plus a minute per repair — or
116	run it in the background. A unit still not ready after that comes back
117	`no_inputs` and is measured by the next run.
118	
119	**A module that does work when it is imported can still be measured** — a
120	script that reads `sys.argv`, opens files or calls a server at its top level.
121	When importing it fails, it is loaded one top-level statement at a time: the
122	statements that fail are skipped and reported, and the unit is measured if it
123	is still defined. So ask for its inputs rather than assuming it cannot run; the
124	generator says so when it cannot.
125	
126	**A unit listed as `failed` can be asked for again** once you have fixed what
127	stopped it. If the reason is a package missing from this environment, install
128	it into this venv — whatever you install stays for the re-measurement after
129	the session — and request the unit again; it is generated once more, up to
130	three times a session. When the generator simply did not manage — none of its
131	inputs ran on the original, or it produced none — another try may succeed: it
132	writes new inputs every time. `inputs.py status` says which case each failure
133	is.
134	
135	Each unit's inputs are one file in `.energy-inputs/`, read-only. Read it before
136	you write the repair: it is exactly what the repair will be measured on. They
137	cannot be changed, and editing the file would change nothing that counts —
138	the result after the session is measured on our copy.
139	The file defines two functions, each returning `(label, thunk)` pairs:
140	
141	- **`checks()`** — edge inputs: empty, one element, `None`, an odd type. Both
142	  versions run them and must behave the same; they are never measured.
143	- **`cases()`** — the four measured inputs, each making the unit do different
144	  work. Every one counts on its own: a repair is `confirmed` only if it saves
145	  energy on all four, and one that measurably loses on any of them is `mixed`.
146	
147	A thunk returns the unit's arguments as a tuple, or `call(...)` when the unit
148	takes keyword arguments. **A method takes its instance as the first
149	argument**, so the thunk builds the instance and passes it.
150	
151	**Why each input is called many times.** One call is usually too short for the
152	energy meter to see, so each input is called many times in a row and the
153	energy of all the calls is added up. That is the only reason for the
154	repetition. Every call gets a fresh copy of the input, built before the
155	calls are measured, and the outputs are compared once, before anything is
156	measured.
157	
158	**A coroutine is run, a generator is drained.** An `async def` unit is run to
159	completion on an event loop of its own, and a generator's output is collected
160	and compared as what it yielded — so a repair that turns a list into a
161	generator counts as returning something different.
162	
163	**Files are output like any other.** Inputs put the files a unit reads under
164	`WORKDIR`, a directory the script gives each side, and every file the unit
165	creates, changes or deletes, under `WORKDIR` or inside the repository, has to
166	come out the same on both sides.
167	
168	**A unit with no inputs.** An input counts only if the original completes on
169	it here, from this machine alone, and gives the same output on every run: that
170	is what lets the two versions be compared. A unit that needs the network, a
171	remote service, credentials, hardware or data the repository does not hold, or
172	whose own output changes from run to run, cannot give that, whatever the input.
173	`inputs.py status` lists it as `failed`, with the reason and what to do next,
174	and verify.py reports its repairs as `no_inputs` with the same. Record their
175	suspicions as `blocked`, quoting the reason — the suspicion is still a
176	finding; only its saving cannot be measured here — and ask for the next unit
177	you would measure in its place: a failed unit does not count toward the 30.
178	
179	**`blocked` needs that evidence.** A suspicion is `blocked` only when the tools
180	showed it cannot be measured here: its inputs could not be generated, its
181	module does not load, the result is `error` for something you cannot install,
182	or the repair cannot be made to behave identically. Quote the message as
183	`why`. One you did not ask inputs for — because you expect it cannot run, or
184	because it is outside the 20 — is `deferred`, not blocked: ask for its inputs
185	instead whenever you can, and let the generator say whether it runs.
186	
187	## What "the same" means
188	
189	The replacement must do everything the original does, on every input:
190	
191	- the same **return value**;
192	- the same effect on its **arguments**, an object's own attributes included;
193	- the same changes to the **module-level and class-level values** the
194	  original's code uses;
195	- the same **files** written;
196	- the same **printed output** and the same **log records**;
197	- the same **exception** type.
198	
199	Nothing in a submission relaxes this. A repair that stops changing the
200	caller's data — `lst.sort()` becomes `sorted(lst)` — stops updating a
201	module-level cache, or drops a log call changes what callers can see, and
202	comes back `not_equivalent`; so does one that returns the same answer in a
203	different form. Two things are left out on purpose: the numbers inside a log
204	message, so a logged duration is not behaviour, and a new module-level value
205	the repair keeps for itself, such as a cache only it reads.
206	
207	## Running it
208	
209	```bash
210	python $SKILL/scripts/verify.py --calibrate                    # optional, see below
211	python $SKILL/scripts/verify.py submissions.jsonl --repo .     # the whole file
212	```
213	
214	`--calibrate` measures two copies of identical code against each other, the
215	way repairs are measured. The answer must come back
216	*insignificant*; its width is this host's resolution limit, and the bar every
217	real effect has to clear. It is kept for the session, and taken automatically
218	if you forget. If it comes back significant, something else is using the
219	machine, and nothing measured until it stops means anything.
220	
221	The second command goes through the file once — about a minute per repair,
222	plus half a minute to calibrate, after any inputs still being generated are
223	ready — so give the command a timeout to match, or run it in the background
224	and wait for it. It writes each result into its line,
225	as `agent_measurement`, with the verdict in `agent_measurement.status`. Run it again after fixing broken lines and it
226	measures only what needs it: a line never measured, a line that was
227	`not_equivalent`, `invalid` or `error` and has since been fixed, and anything
228	`inconclusive` or `error`, which is simply tried again.
229	
230	A line with a measured result — `confirmed`, `partial`, `mixed`,
231	`regressed`, `negligible` — is final and is never measured again. If it has been edited
232	since, the script reports it `invalid` and leaves the result it had exactly as
233	it was. A different repair is a new line.
234	
235	## When the environment gets in the way
236	
237	- **A package is missing** — the result is `error`, naming it: install it into
238	  this environment, `python -m pip install <package>`, and run again. Never
239	  install the repository's own code, and never create another environment.
240	- **Anything else cannot run here** — the result says what failed: record the
241	  suspicion as `blocked`, with the message.
242	
243	Always measure with `--repo .`, against the repository itself: a result taken
244	against an edited copy is discarded.
245	
246	## What the script does
247	
248	1. **Stages** two fresh copies of the repository, the second with your
249	   replacements spliced in, and loads both side by side in one process.
250	2. **Equivalence.** Every input from `checks()` and `cases()` runs once
251	   through both versions, and everything in "What "the same" means" above is
252	   compared. A mismatch is `not_equivalent`, and nothing is measured.
253	3. **Measurement.** The two versions take turns, one window of about a second
254	   each, three pairs per input, the order flipped every pair, so the machine's
255	   own drift affects both alike.
256	4. **Statistics.** The energy difference is averaged over the pairs, with a 95%
257	   confidence interval. Energy decides the verdict; time is reported beside it
258	   and decides nothing.
259	
260	## Verdicts

# Verifying a saving

A repair comes with a claim: that this refactoring saves energy. This is how
the claim gets tested. Read this before writing your first submission.

The rule: **no repair is reported as saving anything until it has been
measured on this machine.**

You do not edit the repository. You describe the repair; the script applies it
to a copy, and `before` is whatever the repository already contains.

---

## The submission

One JSON object per line of `submissions.jsonl`, one line per repair:

```jsonc
{
  "id": "C10S4-render-concat",
  "root_cause": "C10.S4",
  "unit": "src/render.py::Report.render",
  "changed": {
    "src/render.py::Report.render": "def render(self):\n    return \"\".join(_row(r) for r in self.rows)"
  },
  "sole_caller_evidence": null,
  "notes": "C10.S4. Sizes taken from the fixtures in tests/; `_row` left as the real helper."
}
```

**Every line has every field below, and no others** — none is optional; the
ones with nothing to say take the empty value shown.

| Field | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `id` | a name for this repair, unique in the file |
| `root_cause` | the root cause the repair removes, as it appears on its card |
| `unit` | the function or method whose behaviour must be preserved, as `path::qualname` |
| `changed` | `path::qualname` → the full replacement source of that function |
| `sole_caller_evidence` | how you know nothing else calls or reads what you changed; `null` when `changed` holds only the unit |
| `notes` | a few sentences a reader would otherwise have to guess; `""` if none |
| `agent_measurement` | written by the script, never by you |

`changed` holds **source text, not a diff and not an AST**: the whole function
as you would commit it, decorators and `def` line included, written at column
zero even when it is a method. Each entry replaces exactly that function and
nothing around it — so a repair that needs a module the file does not import
yet imports it inside the function. After the first call, an `import`
statement is a single dictionary lookup.

## You do not supply `before`

`before` is the function already in the repository, loaded from the file you
named. You cannot simplify it or substitute an illustration of the pattern,
because you never write it. A repair worth 30% of a five-line sketch and 2% of
the real function always measures against the real function.

The rest is real too: the helpers are the real helpers, the constants the real
constants, the imports the real imports. So the replacement must differ from
the repository by **the repair alone**. If it also renames a variable, inlines
a helper or fixes a second thing, the measurement no longer attributes to
one root cause and the result is unusable.

## Changing more than the unit

The unit's **contract** is what has to survive: everything a caller can see,
listed under "What "the same" means" below.
Anything only the unit depends on — a helper nothing else calls, state nothing
else reads — is implementation detail, and may change.

Give each changed function its own entry in `changed`, in whatever file it
lives, and fill in `sole_caller_evidence`: the search you ran, or the call sites
and attribute reads you checked. The check watches the unit's contract only, so
anything else broken by the change would pass every check here. A submission
that changes more than the unit without this is rejected.

## Several repairs in one unit

Each repair is written against the original code and measured against it, on
its own. There is no order to take them in, and no repair is built on another.

- **The same edit** for two suspicions is one repair. Submit it once; the other
  suspicion is `same_repair_as` it.
- **Different edits to the same code** are separate repairs. Submit each.
- **Every repair of one unit is measured on that unit's inputs**, so their
  savings are measured on identical inputs and can be compared.

## The inputs

You do not write them. Ask for every unit you will measure, in one request:

```bash
python $SKILL/scripts/inputs.py request src/render.py::Report.render src/parse.py::tokenize
python $SKILL/scripts/inputs.py status          # which are ready
```

A generator outside this session writes each unit's inputs from the
repository's own code — the unit, its class, what it uses, and where the
repository calls it. It asks for more candidates than it needs, runs each on
the original code, keeps those that complete and give the same output on a
second, fresh run, and of those keeps the four that do the most work. They are
fixed for the unit: every repair of it is measured on the same four, and so is
the re-measurement after the session, which uses our own copy of them.

Requests open in step 3, at `step.py done 2`. The request returns at once.
Generation runs outside this session, every unit at the same time, and usually
takes a minute or two; a hard unit can take five. Ask for all of them in one
request; a unit you add later is another request. Up to 30 units can have
inputs or be generating at once: more than the 20 repairs measured, so there is
room for units you decide against. A unit that fails gives its place back, so
ask for another in its place; up to 30 different units may fail in a session.

verify.py does not measure while anything is still being generated: it waits
first, up to ten minutes, printing which units it is waiting for. Give its
first run a timeout to match — fifteen minutes plus a minute per repair — or
run it in the background. A unit still not ready after that comes back
`no_inputs` and is measured by the next run.

**A module that does work when it is imported can still be measured** — a
script that reads `sys.argv`, opens files or calls a server at its top level.
When importing it fails, it is loaded one top-level statement at a time: the
statements that fail are skipped and reported, and the unit is measured if it
is still defined. So ask for its inputs rather than assuming it cannot run; the
generator says so when it cannot.

**A unit listed as `failed` can be asked for again** once you have fixed what
stopped it. If the reason is a package missing from this environment, install
it into this venv — whatever you install stays for the re-measurement after
the session — and request the unit again; it is generated once more, up to
three times a session. When the generator simply did not manage — none of its
inputs ran on the original, or it produced none — another try may succeed: it
writes new inputs every time. `inputs.py status` says which case each failure
is.

Each unit's inputs are one file in `.energy-inputs/`, read-only. Read it before
you write the repair: it is exactly what the repair will be measured on. They
cannot be changed, and editing the file would change nothing that counts —
the result after the session is measured on our copy.
The file defines two functions, each returning `(label, thunk)` pairs:

- **`checks()`** — edge inputs: empty, one element, `None`, an odd type. Both
  versions run them and must behave the same; they are never measured.
- **`cases()`** — the four measured inputs, each making the unit do different
  work. Every one counts on its own: a repair is `confirmed` only if it saves
  energy on all four, and one that measurably loses on any of them is `mixed`.

A thunk returns the unit's arguments as a tuple, or `call(...)` when the unit
takes keyword arguments. **A method takes its instance as the first
argument**, so the thunk builds the instance and passes it.

**Why each input is called many times.** One call is usually too short for the
energy meter to see, so each input is called many times in a row and the
energy of all the calls is added up. That is the only reason for the
repetition. Every call gets a fresh copy of the input, built before the
calls are measured, and the outputs are compared once, before anything is
measured.

**A coroutine is run, a generator is drained.** An `async def` unit is run to
completion on an event loop of its own, and a generator's output is collected
and compared as what it yielded — so a repair that turns a list into a
generator counts as returning something different.

**Files are output like any other.** Inputs put the files a unit reads under
`WORKDIR`, a directory the script gives each side, and every file the unit
creates, changes or deletes, under `WORKDIR` or inside the repository, has to
come out the same on both sides.

**A unit with no inputs.** An input counts only if the original completes on
it here, from this machine alone, and gives the same output on every run: that
is what lets the two versions be compared. A unit that needs the network, a
remote service, credentials, hardware or data the repository does not hold, or
whose own output changes from run to run, cannot give that, whatever the input.
`inputs.py status` lists it as `failed`, with the reason and what to do next,
and verify.py reports its repairs as `no_inputs` with the same. Record their
suspicions as `blocked`, quoting the reason — the suspicion is still a
finding; only its saving cannot be measured here — and ask for the next unit
you would measure in its place: a failed unit does not count toward the 30.

**`blocked` needs that evidence.** A suspicion is `blocked` only when the tools
showed it cannot be measured here: its inputs could not be generated, its
module does not load, the result is `error` for something you cannot install,
or the repair cannot be made to behave identically. Quote the message as
`why`. One you did not ask inputs for — because you expect it cannot run, or
because it is outside the 20 — is `deferred`, not blocked: ask for its inputs
instead whenever you can, and let the generator say whether it runs.

## What "the same" means

The replacement must do everything the original does, on every input:

- the same **return value**;
- the same effect on its **arguments**, an object's own attributes included;
- the same changes to the **module-level and class-level values** the
  original's code uses;
- the same **files** written;
- the same **printed output** and the same **log records**;
- the same **exception** type.

Nothing in a submission relaxes this. A repair that stops changing the
caller's data — `lst.sort()` becomes `sorted(lst)` — stops updating a
module-level cache, or drops a log call changes what callers can see, and
comes back `not_equivalent`; so does one that returns the same answer in a
different form. Two things are left out on purpose: the numbers inside a log
message, so a logged duration is not behaviour, and a new module-level value
the repair keeps for itself, such as a cache only it reads.

## Running it

```bash
python $SKILL/scripts/verify.py --calibrate                    # optional, see below
python $SKILL/scripts/verify.py submissions.jsonl --repo .     # the whole file
```

`--calibrate` measures two copies of identical code against each other, the
way repairs are measured. The answer must come back
*insignificant*; its width is this host's resolution limit, and the bar every
real effect has to clear. It is kept for the session, and taken automatically
if you forget. If it comes back significant, something else is using the
machine, and nothing measured until it stops means anything.

The second command goes through the file once — about a minute per repair,
plus half a minute to calibrate, after any inputs still being generated are
ready — so give the command a timeout to match, or run it in the background
and wait for it. It writes each result into its line,
as `agent_measurement`, with the verdict in `agent_measurement.status`. Run it again after fixing broken lines and it
measures only what needs it: a line never measured, a line that was
`not_equivalent`, `invalid` or `error` and has since been fixed, and anything
`inconclusive` or `error`, which is simply tried again.

A line with a measured result — `confirmed`, `partial`, `mixed`,
`regressed`, `negligible` — is final and is never measured again. If it has been edited
since, the script reports it `invalid` and leaves the result it had exactly as
it was. A different repair is a new line.

## When the environment gets in the way

- **A package is missing** — the result is `error`, naming it: install it into
  this environment, `python -m pip install <package>`, and run again. Never
  install the repository's own code, and never create another environment.
- **Anything else cannot run here** — the result says what failed: record the
  suspicion as `blocked`, with the message.

Always measure with `--repo .`, against the repository itself: a result taken
against an edited copy is discarded.

## What the script does

1. **Stages** two fresh copies of the repository, the second with your
   replacements spliced in, and loads both side by side in one process.
2. **Equivalence.** Every input from `checks()` and `cases()` runs once
   through both versions, and everything in "What "the same" means" above is
   compared. A mismatch is `not_equivalent`, and nothing is measured.
3. **Measurement.** The two versions take turns, one window of about a second
   each, three pairs per input, the order flipped every pair, so the machine's
   own drift affects both alike.
4. **Statistics.** The energy difference is averaged over the pairs, with a 95%
   confidence interval. Energy decides the verdict; time is reported beside it
   and decides nothing.

## Verdicts

| Verdict | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `confirmed` | saves energy on all four inputs, each clearing the noise floor | nothing — final |
| `partial` | saves energy on some inputs, and moves nothing beyond the noise on the others | nothing — final. A narrower claim: it pays on some of the work the unit does |
| `mixed` | saves energy on some inputs, costs it on others — both clearing the floor | nothing — final. A trade-off: which side wins depends on the input |
| `regressed` | every case that moved measurably, got worse | nothing — final |
| `negligible` | measured on a clean floor, and nothing moved more than the noise | nothing — final |
| `inconclusive` | the host's noise was too high to resolve an effect this size | nothing; the next run measures it again. It is **not** `negligible` |
| `not_equivalent` | the replacement behaves differently from the original | fix the repair and run again |
| `invalid` | the line is malformed, the inputs do not load against the repair, or a measured line was edited | fix it as the message says |
| `no_inputs` | the unit has no inputs: none were requested, or none could be generated | request them; if they could not be generated, record `blocked` with the message |
| `error` | the environment failed: an import, the meter, a library the unit needs | what the message says: install a missing package and run again, or record `blocked` |
| `over_limit` | 20 repairs in this session already have a verdict, the most it measures; this one was not measured | record its suspicion as `deferred` |

Every verdict stays. A file that proposes ten repairs and has three come back
`negligible` says more than one that quietly dropped them.

`negligible` and `inconclusive` are different claims. `negligible` says the
repair does nothing, on a machine quiet enough to tell — that is evidence.
`inconclusive` says this machine could not tell, which is a fact about the host
and says nothing about the code. Reporting the second as the first writes a
busy host down as evidence against the taxonomy.

`mixed` is not a softer `regressed`. Both effects are real: the repair pays on
one input and costs on another, and which one the code actually sees decides
whether it is worth having.

## What the numbers mean

The meter reads the whole machine's CPU package energy over each window, idle
cores included. A version that finishes sooner also spends less idle power, so
the comparison holds, but it cannot tell a change in power from a change in
duration. When energy improves while wall-clock time does not, say so — that is
more interesting than a performance bug.

## When the card is wrong

It happens, and measurement is how you find out.

C10.S4 used to say what every style guide says: growing a string with `+=` in a
loop is quadratic, so collect the parts and join them. Measured, the textbook
example got *slower* — 62 ms against 56 ms at 400 000 iterations. CPython
resizes a string in place when nothing else refers to it, so the classic
example was already linear. The real waste turned out to be about aliasing:
through an attribute, where the optimisation cannot fire, the same repair saves
94.8% ± 0.1%.

If a repair you built faithfully from a card comes back `negligible`, that is a
result. Report it, say which card, and say what you measured. Do not quietly
drop it and try a different root cause until one sticks.

184	    :param schema_file: path to nextflow_schema.json file
185	    :type schema_file: str or Path
186	    :returns: list of custom inputs defined with DNAnexus datatype 
187	    :rtype: list
188	    Creates custom input list from nextflow_schema.json that
189	    will be added in dxapp.json inputSpec field
190	    """
191	
192	    def get_dx_type(nf_type, nf_format=None):
193	        types = {
194	            "string": "string",
195	            "integer": "int",
196	            "number": "float",
197	            "boolean": "boolean",
198	            "object": "hash"
199	        }
200	        str_types = {
201	            "file-path": "file",
202	            "directory-path": "string",  # So far we will stick with strings dx://...
203	            "path": "string"
204	        }
205	        # Handle JSON Schema union types e.g. ["string", "null"], ["boolean", "string"]
206	        if isinstance(nf_type, list):
207	            non_null = [t for t in nf_type if t != "null"]
208	            nf_type = non_null[0] if non_null else "string"
209	        if nf_type == "string" and nf_format in str_types:
210	            return str_types[nf_format]
211	        elif nf_type in types:
212	            return types[nf_type]
213	        raise Exception("type {} is not supported by DNAnexus".format(nf_type))
214	
215	    inputs = []
216	    if not os.path.exists(schema_file):
217	        return inputs
218	
219	    with open(schema_file, "r") as fh:
220	        schema = json.load(fh)
221	    defs_key = "definitions" if "definitions" in schema else "$defs" if "$defs" in schema else None
222	    if defs_key is None:
223	        return inputs
224	    for d_key, d_schema in schema.get(defs_key, {}).items():
225	        required_inputs = d_schema.get("required", [])
226	        for property_key, property in d_schema.get("properties", {}).items():
227	            dx_input = {}
228	            dx_input["name"] = property_key
229	            dx_input["title"] = dx_input['name']
230	            dx_input["class"] = get_dx_type(property.get("type"), property.get("format"))
231	
232	            help_parts = [f"(Nextflow pipeline {'required' if property_key in required_inputs else 'optional'})"]
233	            if "default" in property:
234	                help_parts.append(f"Default value: {property.get('default', '')}.")
235	            help_parts.append(property.get('description', None))
236	            help_parts.append(property.get('help_text', None))
237	            dx_input["help"] = " ".join(filter(lambda x: x, help_parts)).strip()
238	
239	            dx_input["hidden"] = property.get('hidden', False)
240	            dx_input["optional"] = True
241	            if property_key in required_inputs:
242	                inputs.insert(0, dx_input)
243	            else:
244	                inputs.append(dx_input)
245	
246	    return inputs

11	def get_nextflow_dxapp(
12	        custom_inputs=None,
13	        resources_dir="",
14	        region="aws:us-east-1",
15	        profile="",
16	        cache_docker=False,
17	        nextflow_pipeline_params="",
18	        nextflow_version=None
19	):
20	    """
21	    :param custom_inputs: Custom inputs that will be used in the created Nextflow pipeline.
22	    :type custom_inputs: list
23	    :param resources_dir: Directory with all resources needed for the Nextflow pipeline. Usually directory with user's Nextflow files.
24	    :type resources_dir: str or Path
25	    :param region: The name of the region in which the applet will be built.
26	    :type region: str
27	    :param profile: Custom Nextflow profile. More profiles can be provided by using comma separated string (without whitespaces).
28	    :type profile: str
29	    :param cache_docker: Perform pipeline analysis and cache the detected docker images on the platform
30	    :type cache_docker: boolean
31	    :param nextflow_pipeline_params: Custom Nextflow pipeline parameters
32	    :type nextflow_pipeline_params: string
33	    Creates Nextflow dxapp.json from the Nextflow dxapp.json template
34	    """
35	
36	    if custom_inputs is None:
37	        custom_inputs = []
38	    with open(os.path.join(str(get_template_dir()), 'dxapp.json'), 'r') as f:
39	        dxapp = json.load(f)
40	    dxapp["inputSpec"] = custom_inputs + dxapp["inputSpec"]
41	    dxapp["runSpec"]["file"] = get_source_file_name()
42	
43	    # By default, title and summary will be set to the pipeline name
44	    name = get_resources_dir_name(resources_dir)
45	    if name is None or name == "":
46	        name = "Nextflow pipeline"
47	    dxapp["name"] = name
48	    dxapp["title"] = name
49	    dxapp["summary"] = name
50	    # Resolve version once and thread through
51	    resolved_version, version_config = resolve_version(nextflow_version)
52	    dxapp["regionalOptions"] = get_regional_options(region, resources_dir, profile, cache_docker, nextflow_pipeline_params, version_config=version_config)
53	
54	    # Record dxpy version used for this Nextflow build
55	    dxapp["details"]["dxpyBuildVersion"] = TOOLKIT_VERSION
56	    if os.environ.get("DX_JOB_ID") is None or not is_importer_job():
57	        dxapp["details"]["repository"] = "local"
58	
59	    # Record the resolved Nextflow version
60	    dxapp["details"]["nextflowVersion"] = resolved_version
61	
62	    return dxapp

65	def get_nextflow_src(custom_inputs=None, profile=None, resources_dir=None):
66	    """
67	    :param custom_inputs: Custom inputs (as configured in nextflow_schema.json) that will be used in created runtime configuration and runtime params argument
68	    :type custom_inputs: list
69	    :param profile: Custom Nextflow profile to be used when running a Nextflow pipeline, for more information visit https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/config.html#config-profiles
70	    :type profile: string
71	    :param resources_dir: Directory with all source files needed to build an applet. Can be an absolute or a relative path.
72	    :type resources_dir: str or Path
73	    :returns: String containing the whole source file of an applet.
74	    :rtype: string
75	
76	    Creates Nextflow source file from the Nextflow source file template
77	    """
78	    if custom_inputs is None:
79	        custom_inputs = []
80	    with open(os.path.join(str(get_template_dir()), get_source_file_name()), 'r') as f:
81	        src = f.read()
82	
83	    exclude_input_download = ""
84	    applet_runtime_params = ""
85	    for i in custom_inputs:
86	        value = "${%s}" % (i['name'])
87	        if i.get("class") == "file":
88	            value = "dx://${DX_WORKSPACE_ID}:/$(echo ${%s} | jq .[$dnanexus_link] -r | xargs -I {} dx describe {} --json | jq -r .name)" % \
89	                    i['name']
90	            exclude_input_download += "--except {} ".format(i['name'])
91	
92	        # applet_runtime_inputs variable is initialized in the nextflow.sh script template
93	        applet_runtime_params = applet_runtime_params + '''
94	        if [ -n "${}" ]; then
95	            applet_runtime_inputs+=(--{} "{}")
96	        fi
97	        '''.format(i['name'], i['name'], value)
98	
99	    profile_arg = "-profile {}".format(profile) if profile else ""
100	    src = src.replace("@@APPLET_RUNTIME_PARAMS@@", applet_runtime_params)
101	    src = src.replace("@@PROFILE_ARG@@", profile_arg)
102	    src = src.replace("@@EXCLUDE_INPUT_DOWNLOAD@@", exclude_input_download)
103	    src = src.replace("@@DXPY_BUILD_VERSION@@", TOOLKIT_VERSION)
104	    src = src.replace("@@RESOURCES_SUBPATH@@",
105	                          get_resources_subpath(resources_dir))
106	
107	    return src

14	def _load_versions_manifest():
15	    """Load versions.json manifest."""
16	    manifest_path = path.join(path.dirname(dxpy.__file__), 'nextflow', 'versions.json')
17	    try:
18	        with open(manifest_path, 'r') as f:
19	            manifest = json.load(f)
20	    except (FileNotFoundError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
21	        raise dxpy.exceptions.DXCLIError(
22	            f"Failed to load Nextflow versions manifest at {manifest_path}: {e}")
23	    if "default" not in manifest or "versions" not in manifest:
24	        raise dxpy.exceptions.DXCLIError(
25	            "Malformed Nextflow versions manifest: missing 'default' or 'versions' key")
26	    required_keys = {"status", "nextflow_assets", "nextaur_assets", "awscli_assets", "cache_digest_type"}
27	    valid_digest_types = {"config", "manifest"}
28	    for ver, cfg in manifest["versions"].items():
29	        missing = required_keys - set(cfg.keys())
30	        if missing:
31	            raise dxpy.exceptions.DXCLIError(
32	                f"Malformed version entry '{ver}': missing keys {sorted(missing)}")
33	        digest_type = cfg.get("cache_digest_type")
34	        if digest_type not in valid_digest_types:
35	            raise dxpy.exceptions.DXCLIError(
36	                f"Invalid cache_digest_type '{digest_type}' in version '{ver}'; expected one of {sorted(valid_digest_types)}")
37	    return manifest

40	def resolve_version(requested_version=None, warn=True):
41	    """Resolve Nextflow version. Returns (version_key, version_config).
42	    Prints deprecation warning to stderr if version is deprecated and warn=True.
43	    Raises DXError if version is not found.
44	    """
45	    manifest = _load_versions_manifest()
46	    if requested_version is None:
47	        requested_version = manifest["default"]
48	        if requested_version not in manifest["versions"]:
49	            raise dxpy.exceptions.DXCLIError(
50	                f"Nextflow versions manifest is misconfigured: default version '{requested_version}' "
51	                "is not listed in versions")
52	    version_config = manifest["versions"].get(requested_version)
53	    if version_config is None:
54	        available = ", ".join(sorted(manifest["versions"].keys()))
55	        raise dxpy.exceptions.DXCLIError(
56	            f"Nextflow version '{requested_version}' is not supported. "
57	            f"Available versions: {available}")
58	    if warn and version_config["status"] == "deprecated":
59	        sys.stderr.write(
60	            f"WARNING: Nextflow version {requested_version} is deprecated. "
61	            f"Consider upgrading to {manifest['default']}.\n")
62	    return requested_version, version_config

130	def find_readme(dir):
131	    """
132	    Returns first readme (in alphabetical order) from a root of a given folder
133	    :param dir: Directory in which we search for readme files
134	    :type dir: str or Path
135	    :returns: List[str]
136	    """
137	    readme_pattern = re.compile(r"readme(\.(txt|md|rst|adoc|html|txt|asciidoc|org|text|textile|pod|wiki))?", re.IGNORECASE)
138	    file_list = [f for f in listdir(dir) if path.isfile(path.join(dir, f))]
139	    readme_files = [file for file in file_list if readme_pattern.match(file)]
140	    readme_files.sort()
141	    return readme_files[0] if readme_files else None

2	"""
3	Standalone validator for Nextflow asset JSON files.
4	
5	Checks that every asset file referenced in versions.json:
6	  - exists on disk
7	  - is valid JSON
8	  - contains only well-formed DNAnexus record IDs (^record-[A-Za-z0-9]{24}$)
9	  - has identical region key sets in the prod and staging variants
10	  - has identical region key sets across all asset types (nextaur, nextflow, awscli)

12	Also validates app_asset_projects_ids_{prod,staging}.json for project IDs.
13

15
