477	    def _write2(self, data, multithread=True, **kwargs):
478	        '''
479	        :param data: Data to be written
480	        :type data: str or mmap object
481	        :param multithread: If True, sends multiple write requests asynchronously
482	        :type multithread: boolean
483	
484	        Writes the data *data* to the file.
485	
486	        .. note::
487	
488	            Writing to remote files is append-only. Using :meth:`seek`
489	            does not affect where the next :meth:`write` will occur.
490	
491	        '''
492	        assert(isinstance(data, bytes))
493	
494	        self._ensure_write_bufsize(**kwargs)
495	
496	        def write_request(data_for_write_req):
497	            if multithread:
498	                self._async_upload_part_request(data_for_write_req, index=self._cur_part, **kwargs)
499	            else:
500	                self.upload_part(data_for_write_req, self._cur_part, **kwargs)
501	            self._cur_part += 1
502	
503	        if self._write_buf.tell() == 0 and self._write_bufsize == len(data):
504	            # In the special case of a write that is the same size as
505	            # our write buffer size, and no unflushed data in the
506	            # buffer, just directly dispatch the write and bypass the
507	            # write buffer.
508	            #
509	            # This saves a buffer copy, which is especially helpful if
510	            # 'data' is actually mmap'd from a file.
511	            #
512	            # TODO: an additional optimization could be made to allow
513	            # the last request from an mmap'd upload to take this path
514	            # too (in general it won't because it's not of length
515	            # _write_bufsize). This is probably inconsequential though.
516	            write_request(data)
517	            return
518	
519	        remaining_space = self._write_bufsize - self._write_buf.tell()
520	
521	        if len(data) <= remaining_space:
522	            self._write_buf.write(data)
523	        else:
524	            self._write_buf.write(data[:remaining_space])
525	
526	            temp_data = self._write_buf.getvalue()
527	            self._write_buf = BytesIO()
528	            write_request(temp_data)
529	
530	            # TODO: check if repeat string splitting is bad for
531	            # performance when len(data) >> _write_bufsize
532	            self.write(data[remaining_space:], **kwargs)

534	    def write(self, data, multithread=True, **kwargs):
535	        '''
536	        :param data: Data to be written
537	        :type data: str or mmap object
538	        :param multithread: If True, sends multiple write requests asynchronously
539	        :type multithread: boolean
540	
541	        Writes the data *data* to the file.
542	
543	        .. note::
544	
545	            Writing to remote files is append-only. Using :meth:`seek`
546	            does not affect where the next :meth:`write` will occur.
547	
548	        '''
549	        # In python3, the underlying system methods use the 'bytes' type, not 'string'
550	        #
551	        # This is, hopefully, a temporary hack. It is not a good idea for two reasons:
552	        # 1) Performance, we need to make a pass on the data, and need to allocate
553	        #    another buffer of similar size
554	        # 2) The types are wrong. The "bytes" type should be visible to the caller
555	        #    of the write method, instead of being hidden.
556	
557	        # Should we throw an exception if the file is opened in binary mode,
558	        # and the data is unicode/text?
559	        if isinstance(data, str):
560	            bt = data.encode("utf-8")
561	        elif isinstance(data, bytearray):
562	            bt = bytes(data)
563	        elif isinstance(data, bytes):
564	            bt = data
565	        elif isinstance(data, mmap.mmap):
566	            bt = bytes(data)
567	        else:
568	            raise DXFileError("Invalid type {} for write data argument".format(type(data)))
569	        assert(isinstance(bt, bytes))
570	        self._write2(bt, multithread=multithread, **kwargs)

862	            which billing account is billed for this download). If specified,
863	            must be a project in which this file exists. If not specified, the
864	            project ID specified in the handler is used for the download, IF it
865	            contains this file. If set to DXFile.NO_PROJECT_HINT, no project ID
866	            is supplied for the download, even if the handler specifies a
867	            project ID.

870	        :raises: :exc:`~dxpy.exceptions.ResourceNotFound` if *project* is supplied
871	           and it does not contain this file

873	        Returns the next *length* bytes, or all the bytes until the end of file
874	        (if no *length* is given or there are fewer than *length* bytes left in
875	        the file).

878	           passthrough kwargs are not respected while using the same response
879	           iterator (i.e. until next seek).

881	        '''
882	        if self._file_length == None:
883	            desc = self.describe(**kwargs)
884	            if desc["state"] != "closed":
885	                raise DXFileError("Cannot read from file until it is in the closed state")
886	            self._file_length = int(desc["size"])

889	        # to come back before issuing any more requests. This ensures
890	        # that all subsequent requests can take advantage of caching,
891	        # rather than having all of the first DXFILE_HTTP_THREADS

893	        # size for this heuristic so we don't incur the overhead for

902	            length = self._file_length - self._pos

915	                remaining_len = orig_file_pos + length - self._pos

2	
3	'''
4	Runs Python integration tests
5	
6	Assumes  `make python src_libs && source build/py_env/bin/activate`
7	
8	If no arguments are given, all tests in src/python/test/ are run.
9	
10	To run a single test method, e.g. test_basic in class TestDXBashHelpers,
11	in file src/python/test/test_dx_bash_helpers.py:
12	
13	    $ build/run_python_integration_tests.py --tests test_dx_bash_helpers.TestDXBashHelpers.test_basic
14	
15	To run an entire test class:
16	
17	    $ build/run_python_integration_tests.py --tests test_dx_bash_helpers.TestDXBashHelpers
18	
19	To run all tests in a file:
20	
21	    $ build/run_python_integration_tests.py --tests test_dx_bash_helpers
22	'''
23	
24	from __future__ import print_function, unicode_literals
25	
26	import argparse
27	import os
28	import platform
29	import subprocess
30	import sys
31	
32	parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(usage=__doc__)
33	parser.add_argument(
34	    '--tests',
35	    help='Specify a specific test to run.',
36	    metavar='test_module.TestCase.test_method',
37	    nargs='*'
38	)
39	
40	TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(__file__)), '..'))
41	PYTHON_DIR = os.path.join(TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR, 'src', 'python')
42	PYTHON_TEST_DIR = os.path.join(PYTHON_DIR, 'test')
43	os.environ['DNANEXUS_INSTALL_PYTHON_TEST_DEPS'] = 'yes'
44	
45	def run():
46	    # Assumes `make python src_libs` has been run
47	
48	    cmd = ['python3', '-m', 'unittest']
49	    if args.tests:
50	        cmd += ['-v'] + args.tests
51	    else:
52	        cmd += ['discover', '--start-directory', '.', '--verbose']
53	
54	    if platform.system() == 'Windows':
55	        # Grab existing env vars with nt.environ, so that the SystemRoot var
56	        # isn't uppercased - because that can cause _urandom() errors. See:
57	        #   http://bugs.python.org/issue1384175#msg248951
58	        import nt
59	        subproc_env = dict(nt.environ)
60	    else:
61	        subproc_env = dict(os.environ)
62	
63	    try:
64	        subprocess.check_call(cmd, cwd=PYTHON_TEST_DIR, env=subproc_env)
65	    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
66	        print('*** unittest invocation failed with code %d' % (e.returncode,), file=sys.stderr)
67	        sys.exit(1)
68	
69	if __name__ == '__main__':
70	    args = parser.parse_args()
71	    run()

2539	        # at least 1 + 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 = > 10 seconds, so we can't have completed

19	import glob
20	import os
21	import platform
22	import re
23	from setuptools import setup, find_packages
24	import sys
25	
26	# Pypi is the repository for python packages.
27	# It requires that version numbers look like this: X.Y.Z,
28	# where X, Y, and Z are numbers. It is more complicated than that, but that's
29	# the main idea.
30	#
31	# Clean up the version number. It starts like this:
32	#    '0.265.0-77-g059d243f'
33	# and we need 0.265.0
34	def make_valid_pypi_version(raw):
35	    m = re.match(r'(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)', raw)
36	    return m.group(0)
37	
38	
39	# Don't import, but use exec.
40	# Importing would trigger interpretation of the dxpy entry point, which can fail if deps are not installed.
41	#
42	# The result of this trickery is a variable called "version", initialized
43	# to the current version of dxpy.
44	with open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), 'dxpy', 'toolkit_version.py')) as fh:
45	    exec(compile(fh.read(), 'toolkit_version.py', 'exec'))
46	version = make_valid_pypi_version(version)
47	
48	# The readme file is used as the long-description of the package.
49	# It will show up in the pypi site.
50	with open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "Readme.md"), "r") as fh:
51	    readme_content = fh.read()
52	
53	# Grab all the scripts from dxpy/scripts and install them without their .py extension.
54	# Replace underscores with dashes.
55	# See Readme.md for details.
56	scripts = []
57	for module in os.listdir(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), 'dxpy', 'scripts')):
58	    if module == '__init__.py' or module[-3:] != '.py':
59	        continue
60	    module = module[:-3]
61	    script = module.replace('_', '-')
62	    scripts.append("{s} = dxpy.scripts.{m}:main".format(s=script, m=module))
63	
64	dependencies = [line.rstrip() for line in open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "requirements.txt"))]
65	test_dependencies = [line.rstrip() for line in open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "requirements_test.txt"))]
66	
67	if 'DNANEXUS_INSTALL_PYTHON_TEST_DEPS' in os.environ:
68	    dependencies.extend(test_dependencies)
69	
70	template_files = []
71	
72	for directory, subdirectories, files in os.walk("dxpy/templating/templates"):
73	    directory = directory[len("dxpy/templating/"):]
74	    template_files.extend([os.path.join(directory, _file) for _file in files])
75	
76	nextflow_files = os.listdir(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), 'dxpy', 'nextflow'))
77	nextflow_records = list(filter(lambda file: file[-5:] == ".json", nextflow_files))
78	
79	dx_extract_files = os.listdir(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), 'dxpy', 'dx_extract_utils'))
80	dx_extract_records = list(filter(lambda file: file[-5:] == ".json", dx_extract_files))
81	
82	
83	setup(
84	    name='dxpy',
85	    version=version,
86	    description='DNAnexus Platform API bindings for Python',
87	    long_description=readme_content,
88	    long_description_content_type="text/markdown",
89	    author='Aleksandra Zalcman, Andrey Kislyuk, Anurag Biyani, Geet Duggal, Katherine Lai, Kurt Jensen, Marek Hrvol, Ohad Rodeh, Phil Sung',
90	    author_email='support@dnanexus.com',
91	    url='https://github.com/dnanexus/dx-toolkit',
92	    zip_safe=False,
93	    license='Apache Software License',
94	    packages = find_packages(exclude=['test']),
95	    package_data={'dxpy.templating': template_files, 'dxpy.nextflow': nextflow_records, 'dxpy.dx_extract_utils': dx_extract_records},
96	    scripts = glob.glob(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), 'scripts', 'dx*')),
97	    entry_points = {
98	        "console_scripts": scripts,
99	    },
100	    python_requires = '>=3.8',
101	    install_requires = dependencies,
102	    extras_require={
103	        'pandas': ["pandas==2.0.3; python_version == '3.8'", "pandas==2.2.3; python_version >= '3.9'", "numpy<2.0.0"],
104	        'xattr': ["xattr==1.1.4; sys_platform == 'linux2' or sys_platform == 'linux'"]
105	    },
106	    tests_require = test_dependencies,
107	    test_suite = "test",
108	    classifiers=[
109	        'Environment :: Console',
110	        'Intended Audience :: Developers',
111	        'License :: OSI Approved :: Apache Software License',
112	        'Operating System :: MacOS :: MacOS X',
113	        'Operating System :: POSIX',
114	        'Programming Language :: Python',
115	        'Programming Language :: Unix Shell',
116	        'Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries :: Python Modules'
117	    ]
118	)

62	def wait_for_all_futures(futures, print_traceback=False):
63	    """
64	    Wait indefinitely for all futures in the input iterable to complete.
65	    Use a timeout to enable interrupt handling.
66	    Call os._exit() in case of KeyboardInterrupt. Otherwise, the atexit registered handler in concurrent.futures.thread
67	    will run, and issue blocking join() on all worker threads, requiring us to listen to events in worker threads
68	    in order to enable timely exit in response to Ctrl-C.

74	    import __main__ as main; if hasattr(main, '__file__'): os._exit() else: os.exit()
75	    """
76	    try:

89	def response_iterator(request_iterator, thread_pool, max_active_tasks=None, do_first_task_sequentially=True):
90	    """
91	    :param request_iterator:
92	        An iterator producing inputs for consumption by the worker pool.
93	    :type request_iterator: iterator of callable, args, kwargs
94	    :param thread_pool: thread pool to submit the requests to
95	    :type thread_pool: concurrent.futures.thread.ThreadPoolExecutor
96	    :param max_active_tasks:
97	        The maximum number of tasks that may be either running or
98	        waiting for consumption of their result. If not given, defaults
99	        to the number of CPU cores on the machine.
100	    :type max_active_tasks: int
101	    :param do_first_task_sequentially:
102	        If True, executes (and returns the result of) the first request
103	        before submitting any other requests (the subsequent requests
104	        are submitted with *max_active_tasks* parallelism).
105	    :type do_first_task_sequentially: bool
106	
107	    Rate-limited asynchronous multithreaded task runner. Consumes tasks
108	    from *request_iterator*. Yields their results in order, while
109	    allowing up to *max_active_tasks* to run simultaneously. Unlike
110	    concurrent.futures.Executor.map, prevents new tasks from starting
111	    while there are *max_active_tasks* or more unconsumed results.
112	
113	    """
114	    tasks_in_progress = collections.deque()
115	    if max_active_tasks is None:
116	        max_active_tasks = cpu_count()
117	
118	    # The following two functions facilitate GC by not adding extra variables to the enclosing scope.
119	    def submit_task(task_iterator, executor, futures_queue):
120	        retval  = next(task_iterator, None)
121	        if retval is None:
122	            return False
123	        task_callable, task_args, task_kwargs = retval
124	        task_future = executor.submit(task_callable, *task_args, **task_kwargs)
125	        futures_queue.append(task_future)
126	        return True
127	
128	    def next_result(tasks_in_progress):
129	        future = tasks_in_progress.popleft()
130	        try:
131	            result = future.result(timeout=THREAD_TIMEOUT_MAX)
132	        except KeyboardInterrupt:
133	            print('')
134	            os._exit(os.EX_IOERR)
135	        return result
136	
137	    if do_first_task_sequentially:
138	        task_callable, task_args, task_kwargs = next(request_iterator)
139	        yield task_callable(*task_args, **task_kwargs)
140	
141	    for _i in range(max_active_tasks):
142	        retval = submit_task(request_iterator, thread_pool, tasks_in_progress)
143	        if not retval:
144	            break
145	
146	    while len(tasks_in_progress) > 0:
147	        result = next_result(tasks_in_progress)
148	        submit_task(request_iterator, thread_pool, tasks_in_progress)
149	        yield result

160	def normalize_time_input(t, future=False, default_unit='ms'):
161	    """
162	    :param default_unit: units of the input time *t*; must be one of "s" or
163	        "ms". This param is only respected if *t* looks like an int (e.g.
164	        "12345", 12345).
165	    :type default_unit: string
166	
167	    Converts inputs such as:
168	       "2012-05-01"
169	       "-5d"
170	       1352863174
171	       "1352863174"
172	    to milliseconds since epoch. See http://labix.org/python-dateutil and :meth:`normalize_timedelta`.
173	    """
174	    error_msg = 'Error: Expected an int timestamp, a date format (e.g. YYYY-MM-DD), or an int with a single-letter suffix (s=seconds, m=minutes, h=hours, d=days, w=weeks, M=months, y=years; e.g. "-10d" indicates 10 days ago); but got {t}'
175	    if isinstance(t, basestring) and t.isdigit():
176	        t = int(t)
177	
178	    if isinstance(t, basestring):
179	        try:
180	            t = normalize_timedelta(t)
181	        except ValueError:
182	            try:
183	                t = int(time.mktime(dateutil.parser.parse(t).timetuple())*1000)
184	                assert t > 0
185	            except (ValueError, OverflowError, AssertionError):
186	                raise ValueError(error_msg.format(t=t))
187	    elif isinstance(t, numbers.Integral):
188	        units_multipliers = {'ms': 1, 's': 1000}
189	        if default_unit not in units_multipliers:
190	            raise ValueError("Expected default_unit to be one of 's' or 'ms'")
191	        t = t * units_multipliers[default_unit]
192	    else:
193	        raise ValueError(error_msg.format(t=t))
194	    now = int(time.time()*1000)
195	    if t < 0 or (future and t < now):
196	        t += now
197	    return t

199	def normalize_timedelta(timedelta):
200	    """
201	    Given a string like "1w" or "-5d", convert it to an integer in milliseconds.
202	    Integers without a suffix are interpreted as seconds.
203	    Note: not related to the datetime timedelta class.
204	    """
205	    try:
206	        return int(timedelta) * 1000
207	    except ValueError as e:
208	        t, suffix = timedelta[:-1], timedelta[-1:]
209	        suffix_multipliers = {'s': 1000, 'm': 1000*60, 'h': 1000*60*60, 'd': 1000*60*60*24, 'w': 1000*60*60*24*7,
210	                              'M': 1000*60*60*24*30, 'y': 1000*60*60*24*365}
211	        if suffix not in suffix_multipliers:
212	            raise ValueError()
213	        return int(t) * suffix_multipliers[suffix]

216	class OrderedDefaultdict(collections.OrderedDict):
217	    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
218	        newdefault = None
219	        newargs = ()
220	        if args:
221	            newdefault = args[0]
222	            if not (newdefault is None or callable(newdefault)):
223	                raise TypeError('first argument must be callable or None')
224	            newargs = args[1:]
225	        self.default_factory = newdefault
226	        super(self.__class__, self).__init__(*newargs, **kwargs)
227	
228	    def __missing__(self, key):
229	        if self.default_factory is None:
230	            raise KeyError(key)
231	        self[key] = value = self.default_factory()
232	        return value

234	    def __reduce__(self):
235	        args = self.default_factory if self.default_factory else tuple()

47	class DXConfig(MutableMapping):
48	    """This class provides the dxpy configuration manager, available as
49	    ``dxpy.config``. When first accessed, the config manager looks up
50	    environment variables used to configure dxpy, and if they are not
51	    found, then attempts to resolve them by looking in the file
52	    ~/.dnanexus_config/environment, followed by the installed defaults
53	    in /etc/dnanexus.
54	
55	    To assign to and access variables managed by the configuration
56	    manager, use ``dxpy.config["VAR_NAME"]``. When assigning a
57	    variable, the manager sets it as a process environment variable
58	    and updates any dxpy variable bound to it
59	    (e.g. dxpy.SECURITY_CONTEXT when setting
60	    DX_SECURITY_CONTEXT). When accessing a variable, it is looked up
61	    from the process environment.
62	
63	    To save (serialize) the value of a variable to a persistent dxpy
64	    configuration file, use ``dxpy.config.write(key, value)`` or
65	    ``dxpy.config.save()`` after assigning variable values. To clear
66	    the values in persistent dxpy configuration, use
67	    ``dxpy.config.clear()``.
68	    """
69	    CORE_VAR_NAMES = {"DX_APISERVER_HOST", "DX_APISERVER_PORT",
70	                      "DX_APISERVER_PROTOCOL", "DX_PROJECT_CONTEXT_ID",
71	                      "DX_WORKSPACE_ID", "DX_SECURITY_CONTEXT", "DX_JOB_ID"}
72	    STANDALONE_VAR_NAMES = {"DX_CLI_WD", "DX_USERNAME",
73	                            "DX_PROJECT_CONTEXT_NAME"}
74	    """
75	    List of variable names supported by the configuration manager.
76	    """
77	    VAR_NAMES = set.union(CORE_VAR_NAMES, STANDALONE_VAR_NAMES)
78	    defaults = {
79	        "DX_SECURITY_CONTEXT": json.dumps({"auth_token": "PUBLIC", "auth_token_type": "Bearer"}),
80	        "DX_APISERVER_PROTOCOL": DEFAULT_APISERVER_PROTOCOL,
81	        "DX_APISERVER_HOST": DEFAULT_APISERVER_HOST,
82	        "DX_APISERVER_PORT": DEFAULT_APISERVER_PORT,
83	        "DX_CLI_WD": "/"
84	    }
85	    _global_conf_dir = "/etc/dnanexus"
86	
87	    def __init__(self, suppress_warning=False):
88	        """
89	        :param suppress_warning:
90	            Whether to suppress the warning message for any mismatch found in the environment variables and the dx
91	            configuration file
92	        :type suppress_warning: boolean
93	        """
94	        try:
95	            dxpy._DEBUG = int(os.environ.get("_DX_DEBUG", 0))
96	        except ValueError as e:
97	            warn("WARNING: Expected _DX_DEBUG to be an integer, but got", os.environ["_DX_DEBUG"])
98	            dxpy._DEBUG = 0
99	
100	        try:
101	            dxpy._INJECT_ERROR = bool(os.environ.get("_DX_INJECT_ERROR", 0))
102	        except:
103	            dxpy._INJECT_ERROR = False
104	
105	        self._user_conf_dir = os.path.expanduser(os.environ.get("DX_USER_CONF_DIR", "~/.dnanexus_config"))
106	
107	        dxpy._UPGRADE_NOTIFY = os.path.join(self._user_conf_dir, ".upgrade_notify")
108	        # If last upgrade notification was less than 24 hours ago, disable it
109	        if os.path.exists(dxpy._UPGRADE_NOTIFY) and os.path.getmtime(dxpy._UPGRADE_NOTIFY) > time.time() - 86400:
110	            dxpy._UPGRADE_NOTIFY = False
111	
112	        env_vars = self._read_conf_dir(self.get_global_conf_dir())
113	        env_vars.update(self._read_conf_dir(self.get_user_conf_dir()))
114	        env_vars.update(self._read_conf_dir(self.get_session_conf_dir(cleanup=True)))
115	        env_overrides = []
116	        for var in self.VAR_NAMES:
117	            if var in os.environ:
118	                if var in env_vars and env_vars.get(var) != os.environ[var]:
119	                    env_overrides.append(var)
120	                env_vars[var] = os.environ[var]
121	
122	        for var in env_vars:
123	            if env_vars[var] is not None:
124	                os.environ[var] = env_vars[var]
125	
126	        if sys.stdout.isatty():
127	            if not suppress_warning and len(env_overrides) > 0:
128	                msg = "WARNING: The following environment variables were found to be different than the values " + \
129	                      "last stored by dx: "
130	                warn(fill(msg + ", ".join(env_overrides), width=80))
131	                msg = "To use the values stored by dx, unset the environment variables in your shell by running " + \
132	                      '"source ~/.dnanexus_config/unsetenv".  To clear the dx-stored values, run "dx clearenv".'
133	                warn(fill(msg, width=80))
134	
135	        self._sync_dxpy_state()
136	
137	    def _sync_dxpy_state(self):
138	        dxpy.set_api_server_info(host=os.environ.get("DX_APISERVER_HOST", None),
139	                                 port=os.environ.get("DX_APISERVER_PORT", None),
140	                                 protocol=os.environ.get("DX_APISERVER_PROTOCOL", None))
141	
142	        if "DX_SECURITY_CONTEXT" in os.environ:
143	            dxpy.set_security_context(json.loads(os.environ["DX_SECURITY_CONTEXT"]))
144	
145	        if "DX_JOB_ID" in os.environ:
146	            dxpy.set_job_id(os.environ["DX_JOB_ID"])
147	            dxpy.set_workspace_id(os.environ.get("DX_WORKSPACE_ID"))
148	        else:
149	            dxpy.set_job_id(None)
150	            dxpy.set_workspace_id(os.environ.get("DX_PROJECT_CONTEXT_ID"))
151	        
152	        if "DX_WATCH_PORT" in os.environ:
153	            dxpy.set_watch_port(os.environ.get("DX_WATCH_PORT"))
154	        else:
155	            dxpy.set_watch_port(None)
156	
157	        dxpy.set_project_context(os.environ.get("DX_PROJECT_CONTEXT_ID"))
158	
159	    def get_global_conf_dir(self):
160	        return self._global_conf_dir
161	
162	    def get_user_conf_dir(self):
163	        return self._user_conf_dir
164	
165	    def get_session_conf_dir(self, cleanup=False):
166	        """
167	        Tries to find the session configuration directory by looking in ~/.dnanexus_config/sessions/<PID>,
168	        where <PID> is pid of the parent of this process, then its parent, and so on.
169	        If none of those exist, the path for the immediate parent is given, even if it doesn't exist.
170	
171	        If *cleanup* is True, looks up and deletes all session configuration directories that belong to nonexistent
172	        processes.
173	        """
174	        sessions_dir = os.path.join(self._user_conf_dir, "sessions")
175	        try:
176	            from psutil import Process, pid_exists
177	
178	            if cleanup:
179	                try:
180	                    session_dirs = os.listdir(sessions_dir)
181	                except OSError as e:
182	                    # Silently skip cleanup and continue if we are unable to
183	                    # enumerate the session directories for any reason
184	                    # (including, most commonly, because the sessions dir
185	                    # doesn't exist)
186	                    session_dirs = []
187	                for session_dir in session_dirs:
188	                    try:
189	                        session_pid = int(session_dir)
190	                    except ValueError:
191	                        # If dir name doesn't look like an int, leave it
192	                        # alone
193	                        continue
194	                    if not pid_exists(session_pid):
195	                        rmtree(os.path.join(sessions_dir, session_dir), ignore_errors=True)
196	
197	            parent_process = Process(os.getpid()).parent()
198	            if parent_process is None:
199	                parent_process = Process(os.getpid())
200	            default_session_dir = os.path.join(sessions_dir, str(parent_process.pid))
201	            while parent_process is not None and parent_process.pid != 0:
202	                session_dir = os.path.join(sessions_dir, str(parent_process.pid))
203	                if os.path.exists(session_dir):
204	                    return session_dir
205	                parent_process = parent_process.parent()
206	            return default_session_dir
207	        except (ImportError, IOError, AttributeError) as e:
208	            # We don't bundle psutil with Windows, so failure to import
209	            # psutil would be expected.
210	            if platform.system() != 'Windows':
211	                warn(fill("Error while retrieving session configuration: " + format_exception(e)))
212	        except Exception as e:
213	            warn(fill("Unexpected error while retrieving session configuration: " + format_exception(e)))
214	        return self._get_ppid_session_conf_dir(sessions_dir)
215	
216	    def _get_ppid_session_conf_dir(self, sessions_dir):
217	        try:
218	            return os.path.join(sessions_dir, str(os.getppid()))
219	        except AttributeError:
220	            pass # os.getppid is not available on Windows
221	        except Exception as e:
222	            warn(fill("Unexpected error while retrieving session configuration: " + format_exception(e)))
223	        return os.path.join(sessions_dir, str(os.getpid()))
224	
225	    def _read_conf_dir(self, dirname):
226	        try:
227	            with open(os.path.join(dirname, "environment.json")) as fd:
228	                env_vars = json.load(fd)
229	        except Exception:
230	            env_vars = {}
231	
232	        for standalone_var in self.STANDALONE_VAR_NAMES:
233	            try:
234	                with open(os.path.join(dirname, standalone_var)) as fd:
235	                    env_vars[standalone_var] = fd.read()
236	            except Exception:
237	                pass
238	        return env_vars
239	
240	    def __getitem__(self, item):
241	        if item not in self.VAR_NAMES:
242	            raise KeyError(item)
243	        return os.environ[item]
244	
245	    def __setitem__(self, key, value):
246	        if key not in self.VAR_NAMES:
247	            raise KeyError(key)
248	        if value is None:
249	            value = self.defaults.get(key, "")
250	        os.environ[key] = value
251	        if key in self.CORE_VAR_NAMES:
252	            self._sync_dxpy_state()
253	
254	    def __delitem__(self, key):
255	        if key not in self.VAR_NAMES:
256	            raise KeyError(key)
257	        del os.environ[key]
258	        if key in self.CORE_VAR_NAMES:
259	            self._sync_dxpy_state()
260	
261	    def __iter__(self):
262	        for item in self.VAR_NAMES:
263	            if item in os.environ:
264	                yield item
265	
266	    def __len__(self):
267	        return len([var for var in self.VAR_NAMES if var in os.environ])
268	
269	    def __repr__(self):
270	        desc = "<{module}.{classname} object at 0x{mem_loc:x}: {data}>"
271	        return desc.format(module=self.__module__,
272	                           classname=self.__class__.__name__,
273	                           mem_loc=id(self),
274	                           data=dict(self))
275	
276	    def write(self, item, value):
277	        self[item] = value
278	        self.save()
279	
280	    def save(self):
281	        self._write_conf_dir(self._user_conf_dir)
282	        self._write_conf_dir(self.get_session_conf_dir())
283	        self._write_unsetenv(self._user_conf_dir)
284	
285	    def _write_unsetenv(self, conf_dir):
286	        if not os.path.exists(os.path.join(conf_dir, "unsetenv")):
287	            with open(os.path.join(conf_dir, "unsetenv"), "w") as fd:
288	                fd.writelines("unset {}\n".format(var) for var in self.CORE_VAR_NAMES)
289	
290	    def _write_conf_dir(self, conf_dir):
291	        try:
292	            os.makedirs(conf_dir, 0o700)
293	        except OSError:
294	            try:
295	                os.chmod(conf_dir, 0o700)
296	            except OSError as e:
297	                warn(fill("Error while writing configuration data: " + format_exception(e)))
298	                return
299	
300	        env_jsonfile_path = os.path.join(conf_dir, "environment.json")
301	        # Make sure the file has 600 permissions
302	        with _open_for_writing_with_permissions(env_jsonfile_path, 0o600) as fd:
303	            json.dump({k: self.get(k, self.defaults.get(k)) for k in self}, fd, indent=4)
304	            fd.write("\n")
305	
306	        for var in self.STANDALONE_VAR_NAMES:
307	            # Make sure the file has 600 permissions
308	            with _open_for_writing_with_permissions(os.path.join(conf_dir, var), 0o600) as fd:
309	                value = self.get(var, self.defaults.get(var, ""))
310	                fd.write(value)
311	
312	    def clear(self, reset=False):
313	        rmtree(self.get_session_conf_dir(), ignore_errors=True)
314	        _remove_ignore_errors(os.path.join(self._user_conf_dir, "environment"))
315	        _remove_ignore_errors(os.path.join(self._user_conf_dir, "environment.json"))
316	        for f in self.STANDALONE_VAR_NAMES:
317	            _remove_ignore_errors(os.path.join(self._user_conf_dir, f))
318	
319	        if reset:
320	            for var in self.VAR_NAMES:
321	                self[var] = self.defaults.get(var, "")
322	            self.save()

140	def pager(content, pager=None, file=None):
141	    if file is None:
142	        file = sys.stdout
143	
144	    pager_process = None
145	    try:
146	        if file != sys.stdout or not file.isatty():
147	            raise DXCLIError() # Just print the content, don't use a pager
148	        content_lines = content.splitlines()
149	        content_rows = len(content_lines)
150	        content_cols = max(len(i) for i in content_lines)
151	
152	        if tty_rows > content_rows and tty_cols > content_cols:
153	            raise DXCLIError() # Just print the content, don't use a pager
154	
155	        if pager is None:

166	        pager_process.stdin.close()
167	        pager_process.wait()

169	            raise DXCLIError() # Pager had a problem, print the content without it

178	def refill_paragraphs(string, ignored_prefix='    '):
179	    """Refills the given text, where the text is composed of paragraphs
180	    separated by blank lines (i.e. '\n\n'). Lines that begin with
181	    ignored_prefix are not touched; this can be used to keep indented
182	    code snippets from being incorrectly reformatted.
183	
184	    """
185	    paragraphs = string.split('\n\n')
186	    refilled_paragraphs = [fill(paragraph) if not paragraph.startswith(ignored_prefix) else paragraph for paragraph in paragraphs]
187	    return '\n\n'.join(refilled_paragraphs).strip('\n')

84	def format_tree(tree, root=None):
85	    ''' Tree pretty printer.
86	    Expects trees to be given as mappings (dictionaries). Keys will be printed; values will be traversed if they are
87	    mappings. To preserve order, use collections.OrderedDict.
88	
89	    Example:
90	
91	        print format_tree(collections.OrderedDict({'foo': 0, 'bar': {'xyz': 0}}))
92	
93	    '''
94	    formatted_tree = [root] if root is not None else []
95	    def _format(tree, prefix='    '):
96	        nodes = list(tree.keys())
97	        for i in range(len(nodes)):
98	            node = nodes[i]
99	            if i == len(nodes)-1 and len(prefix) > 1:
100	                my_prefix = prefix[:-4] + '└── '
101	                my_multiline_prefix = prefix[:-4] + '    '
102	            else:
103	                my_prefix = prefix[:-4] + '├── '
104	                my_multiline_prefix = prefix[:-4] + '│   '
105	            n = 0
106	            for line in node.splitlines():
107	                if n == 0:
108	                    formatted_tree.append(my_prefix + line)
109	                else:
110	                    formatted_tree.append(my_multiline_prefix + line)
111	                n += 1
112	
113	            if isinstance(tree[node], Mapping):
114	                subprefix = prefix
115	                if i < len(nodes)-1 and len(prefix) > 1 and prefix[-4:] == '    ':
116	                    subprefix = prefix[:-4] + '│   '
117	                _format(tree[node], subprefix + '    ')
118	    _format(tree)
119	    return '\n'.join(formatted_tree)

121	def format_table(table, column_names=None, column_specs=None, max_col_width=32,
122	                 report_dimensions=False):
123	    ''' Table pretty printer.
124	    Expects tables to be given as arrays of arrays.
125	
126	    Example:
127	
128	        print format_table([[1, "2"], [3, "456"]], column_names=['A', 'B'])
129	
130	    '''
131	    if len(table) > 0:
132	        col_widths = [0] * len(list(table)[0])
133	    elif column_specs is not None:
134	        col_widths = [0] * (len(column_specs) + 1)
135	    elif column_names is not None:
136	        col_widths = [0] * len(column_names)
137	    my_column_names = []
138	    if column_specs is not None:
139	        column_names = ['Row']
140	        column_names.extend([col['name'] for col in column_specs])
141	        column_specs = [{'name': 'Row', 'type': 'float'}] + column_specs
142	    if column_names is not None:
143	        for i in range(len(column_names)):
144	            my_col = str(column_names[i])
145	            if len(my_col) > max_col_width:
146	                my_col = my_col[:max_col_width-1] + '…'
147	            my_column_names.append(my_col)
148	            col_widths[i] = max(col_widths[i], len(my_col))
149	    my_table = []
150	    for row in table:
151	        my_row = []
152	        for i in range(len(row)):
153	            my_item = escape_unicode_string(str(row[i]))
154	            if len(my_item) > max_col_width:
155	                my_item = my_item[:max_col_width-1] + '…'
156	            my_row.append(my_item)
157	            col_widths[i] = max(col_widths[i], len(my_item))
158	        my_table.append(my_row)
159	
160	    def border(i):
161	        return WHITE() + i + ENDC()
162	
163	    type_colormap = {'boolean': BLUE(),
164	                     'integer': YELLOW(),
165	                     'float': WHITE(),
166	                     'string': GREEN()}
167	    for i in 'uint8', 'int16', 'uint16', 'int32', 'uint32', 'int64':
168	        type_colormap[i] = type_colormap['integer']
169	    type_colormap['double'] = type_colormap['float']
170	
171	    def col_head(i):
172	        if column_specs is not None:
173	            return BOLD() + type_colormap[column_specs[i]['type']] + column_names[i] + ENDC()
174	        else:
175	            return BOLD() + WHITE() + column_names[i] + ENDC()
176	
177	    formatted_table = [border('┌') + border('┬').join(border('─')*i for i in col_widths) + border('┐')]
178	    if len(my_column_names) > 0:
179	        padded_column_names = [col_head(i) + ' '*(col_widths[i]-len(my_column_names[i])) for i in range(len(my_column_names))]
180	        formatted_table.append(border('│') + border('│').join(padded_column_names) + border('│'))
181	        formatted_table.append(border('├') + border('┼').join(border('─')*i for i in col_widths) + border('┤'))
182	
183	    for row in my_table:
184	        padded_row = [row[i] + ' '*(col_widths[i]-len(row[i])) for i in range(len(row))]
185	        formatted_table.append(border('│') + border('│').join(padded_row) + border('│'))
186	    formatted_table.append(border('└') + border('┴').join(border('─')*i for i in col_widths) + border('┘'))
187	
188	    if report_dimensions:
189	        return '\n'.join(formatted_table), len(formatted_table), sum(col_widths) + len(col_widths) + 1
190	    else:
191	        return '\n'.join(formatted_table)

193	def flatten_json_array(json_string, array_name):
194	    """
195	    Flattens all arrays with the same name in the JSON string
196	
197	    :param json_string: JSON string
198	    :type json_string: str
199	    :param array_name: Array name to flatten
200	    :type array_name: str
201	    """
202	
203	    result = re.sub('"{}": \\[\r?\n\\s*'.format(array_name), '"{}": ['.format(array_name), json_string, flags=re.MULTILINE)
204	    flatten_regexp = re.compile('"{}": \\[(.*)(?<=,)\r?\n\\s*'.format(array_name), flags=re.MULTILINE)
205	    while flatten_regexp.search(result):
206	        result = flatten_regexp.sub('"{}": [\\1 '.format(array_name), result)
207	    result = re.sub('"{}": \\[(.*)\r?\n\\s*\\]'.format(array_name), '"{}": [\\1]'.format(array_name), result, flags=re.MULTILINE)
208	    return result

210	def format_timedelta(timedelta, in_seconds=False, largest_units=None, auto_singulars=False):
211	    """
212	    Formats timedelta (duration) to a human readable form
213	
214	    :param timedelta: Duration in miliseconds or seconds (see in_seconds)
215	    :type timedelta: int
216	    :param in_seconds: Whether the given duration is in seconds
217	    :type in_seconds: bool
218	    :param largest_units: Largest units to be displayed. Allowed values are miliseconds, seconds, minutes, hours, days and years
219	    :type largest_units: str
220	    :param auto_singulars: Automatically use singular when value of given units is 1
221	    :type auto_singulars: bool
222	    """
223	
224	    units = TIME_UNITS[1:] if in_seconds else TIME_UNITS
225	
226	    if largest_units is None:
227	        largest_units = units[-1][0]
228	    elif largest_units not in map(lambda x: x[0], units):
229	        raise ValueError('Invalid largest units specified')
230	
231	    if timedelta == 0:
232	        return '0 ' + units[0][0]
233	
234	    out_str = ''
235	
236	    for name, diviser in units:
237	        if timedelta == 0:
238	            break
239	
240	        if largest_units == name:
241	            diviser = None
242	
243	        val = timedelta % diviser if diviser else timedelta
244	        if val != 0:
245	            out_str = str(val) + ' ' + (name[:-1] if auto_singulars and val == 1 else name) + ', ' + out_str
246	
247	        if diviser is None:
248	            break
249	
250	        timedelta //= diviser
251	
252	    return out_str.strip(', ')

44	# Check if a program (wget, curl, etc.) is on the path, and

46	def which(program):
47	    def is_exe(fpath):
48	        return os.path.isfile(fpath) and os.access(fpath, os.X_OK)
49	
50	    for path in os.environ["PATH"].split(os.pathsep):
51	        exe_file = os.path.join(path, program)
52	        if is_exe(exe_file):
53	            return exe_file
54	    return None

57	def md5_checksum(filename):
58	    md5sum_exe = which("md5sum")
59	    if md5sum_exe is None:
60	        err_exit("md5sum is not installed on this system")
61	    cmd = [md5sum_exe, "-b", filename]
62	    try:
63	        print("Calculating checksum")
64	        cmd_out = subprocess.check_output(cmd)
65	    except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
66	        err_exit("Failed to run md5sum: " + str(cmd))
67	
68	    line = cmd_out.strip().split()
69	    if len(line) != 2:
70	        err_exit("md5sum returned weird results: " + str(line))
71	    result = line[0]
72

74	    assert(isinstance(result, bytes))
75	    result = result.decode("ascii")

218	def _hierarchy_from_parents(codes_to_parent: dict, all_codes: list) -> list:
219	    """
220	    Rebuilds a nested `display` tree for a hierarchical coding from its complete
221	    code -> parent_code edges, once every fragment of a coding split across pages has been
222	    merged. Siblings are ordered by code, since the wire format carries no other order for
223	    a coding the server had to slice.
224	    """
225	    children_of = collections.OrderedDict()
226	    for code in all_codes:
227	        children_of.setdefault(codes_to_parent.get(code, ""), []).append(code)
228	
229	    def subtree(parent_code):
230	        return [
231	            {code: subtree(code)} if code in children_of else code
232	            for code in children_of.get(parent_code, [])
233	        ]
234	
235	    return subtree("")

238	def _finalize_split_codings(codings: dict) -> dict:
239	    """
240	    Turns any coding still carrying `codes_to_parent` back into the canonical shape, now
241	    that every fragment of it has been merged: its edges are a complete parent map, so the
242	    tree hare couldn't safely build from a single page can be built here (see
243	    _hierarchy_from_parents), and the coding is no longer distinguishable from a whole one.
244	    """
245	    for coding in codings.values():
246	        if "codes_to_parent" not in coding:
247	            continue
248	        all_codes = list(coding["codes_to_meanings"])
249	        coding["display"] = _hierarchy_from_parents(
250	            coding.pop("codes_to_parent"), all_codes
251	        )
252	        coding.pop(CODING_PAGINATED_KEY, None)
253	    return codings

256	def get_codings(resp: dict, project_context: str, limit: Optional[int] = None) -> dict:
257	    """
258	    Returns all of the dataset's codings as a dict of coding name to coding, following the
259	    server's pagination cursor and reassembling any coding split across pages.
260	
261	    Each coding has the same shape as a descriptor's `model["codings"]` entry. On the wire, a
262	    hierarchical coding the server had to split sends `codes_to_parent` in place of `display`,
263	    since a tree built from a single page could be wrong; once every fragment is in hand the
264	    edges are complete, so this rebuilds `display` from them before returning -- callers never
265	    see `codes_to_parent`.
266	    """
267	    codings = collections.OrderedDict()
268	    payload = {"project_context": project_context}
269	    if limit is not None:
270	        payload["limit"] = limit
271	
272	    for _ in range(MAX_CODINGS_PAGES):
273	        page = viz_meta_codings_page(resp, payload)
274	        for name, coding in page["results"].items():
275	            if name not in codings:
276	                # Deep-copied so a stored coding never aliases the response, and so every
277	                # key -- not just the ones this function knows to merge -- is safe to keep.
278	                codings[name] = copy.deepcopy(coding)
279	                continue
280	
281	            # Seen already, so the server split this coding across pages. `existing` aliases
282	            # the accumulated coding and is merged into in place.
283	            existing = codings[name]
284	            existing[CODING_PAGINATED_KEY] = True
285	            existing["codes_to_meanings"].update(coding.get("codes_to_meanings") or {})
286	            existing["codes_to_concepts"].update(coding.get("codes_to_concepts") or {})
287	            if "codes_to_parent" in coding:
288	                # A tree built from a single page is wrong, since a code's children can fall
289	                # on the next page; parent edges hold however the pages divide.
290	                existing.setdefault("codes_to_parent", {}).update(
291	                    coding["codes_to_parent"] or {}
292	                )
293	                existing.pop("display", None)
294	            elif "display" in coding and "display" in existing:
295	                existing["display"].extend(coding["display"] or [])
296	
297	        if not page.get("next"):
298	            return _finalize_split_codings(codings)
299	        # Echoed back verbatim as `starting`: when a coding has more codes than `limit`,
300	        # `next` carries that coding's real `after_code` so the next page resumes mid-coding
301	        # at the right code, rather than always just advancing to the next coding name.
302	        payload["starting"] = page["next"]
303	
304	    raise DXError(
305	        "Codings pagination did not complete after {} pages".format(MAX_CODINGS_PAGES)
306	    )

5	#
6	# Scatter-process-gather execution pattern: Your app will split its
7	# input into multiple pieces, each of which will be processed in
8	# parallel, after which they are gathered together in some final
9	# output.
10	#
11	# This pattern is very similar to the "parallelized" template.  What
12	# it does differently is that it formally breaks out the "scatter"
13	# phase as a separate black-box entry point in the app.  (As a side
14	# effect, this requires a "map" entry point to call "process" on each
15	# of the results from the "scatter" phase.)
16	#
17	# Note that you can also replace any entry point in this execution
18	# pattern with an API call to run a separate app or applet.
19	#
20	# The following is a Unicode art picture of the flow of execution.
21	# Each box is an entry point, and vertical lines indicate that the
22	# entry point connected at the top of the line calls the entry point
23	# connected at the bottom of the line.  The letters represent the
24	# different stages in which the input is transformed, e.g. the output
25	# of the "scatter" entry point ("array:B") is given to the "map" entry
26	# point as input.  The "map" entry point calls as many "process" entry
27	# points as there are elements in its array input and gathers the
28	# results in its array output.
29	#
30	#          ┌──────┐
31	#       A->│ main │->D (output from "postprocess")
32	#          └┬─┬─┬─┘
33	#           │ │ │
34	#          ┌┴──────┐
35	#       A->│scatter│->array:B
36	#          └───────┘
37	#             │ │
38	#            ┌┴──────────────┐
39	#   array:B->│      map      │->array:C
40	#            └─────────┬─┬─┬─┘
41	#               │      │ . .
42	#               │     ┌┴──────┐
43	#               │  B->│process│->C
44	#               │     └───────┘
45	#            ┌──┴────────┐
46	#   array:C->│postprocess│->D
47	#            └───────────┘
48	#
49	# A = original app input, split up by "scatter" into pieces of type B
50	# B = an input that will be provided to a "process" entry point
51	# C = the output of a "process" entry point
52	# D = app output aggregated from the outputs of the "process" entry points
53	#
54	# See https://documentation.dnanexus.com/developer for documentation and
55	# tutorials on how to modify this file.
56	#
57	# DNAnexus Python Bindings (dxpy) documentation:
58	#   http://autodoc.dnanexus.com/bindings/python/current/

60	import os
61	import dxpy
62	
63	@dxpy.entry_point("postprocess")
64	def postprocess(process_outputs, additional_input):
65	    # This is the "gather" phase which aggregates and performs any
66	    # additional computation after the "map" (and therefore after all
67	    # the "process") jobs are done.
68	
69	    for item in process_outputs:
70	        print(item)
71	
72	    return { "final_output": "postprocess placeholder output" }
73

76	    # Fill in code here to process the input and create output.
77	
78	    # As always, you can choose not to return output if the
79	    # "postprocess" stage does not require any input, e.g. rows have
80	    # been added to a file that has been created in advance.  Just
81	    # make sure that the "postprocess" job does not run until all
82	    # "process" jobs have finished by making it wait for "map" to
83	    # finish using the depends_on argument (this is already done for
84	    # you in the invocation of the "postprocess" job in "main").
85	
86	    return { "process_output": "process placeholder output" }
87	
88	@dxpy.entry_point("map")
89	def map_entry_point(array_of_scattered_input, process_input):
90	    # The following calls "process" for each of the items in
91	    # *array_of_scattered_input*, using as input the item in the
92	    # array, as well as the rest of the fields in *process_input*.
93	    process_jobs = []
94	    for item in array_of_scattered_input:
95	        process_input["scattered_input"] = item
96	        process_jobs.append(dxpy.new_dxjob(fn_input=process_input, fn_name="process"))
97	    return { "process_outputs": [subjob.get_output_ref("process_output") for subjob in process_jobs] }
98	
99	@dxpy.entry_point("scatter")
100	def scatter(input_to_scatter):
101	    # Fill in code here to do whatever is necessary to scatter the
102	    # input.
103	    array_of_scattered_input = []
104	
105	    return { "array_of_scattered_input": array_of_scattered_input }
106	
107	@dxpy.entry_point("main")
108	def main(DX_APP_WIZARD_INPUT_SIGNATURE):
109	DX_APP_WIZARD_INITIALIZE_INPUTDX_APP_WIZARD_DOWNLOAD_ANY_FILES
110	    # We first create the "scatter" job which will scatter some input
111	    # (replace with your own input as necessary).
112	    input_to_scatter = "placeholder value"
113	    scatter_job = dxpy.new_dxjob(fn_input={ "input_to_scatter": input_to_scatter },
114	                                 fn_name="scatter")
115	
116	    # We will want to call "process" on each output of "scatter", so
117	    # we call the "map" entry point to do so.  We can also provide
118	    # here additional input that we want each "process" entry point to
119	    # receive, e.g. a file ID to which the "process" function should
120	    # add rows of data.
121	    map_input = {
122	        "array_of_scattered_input": scatter_job.get_output_ref("array_of_scattered_input"),
123	        "process_input": { "additional_input": "file ID, for example" }
124	        }
125	    map_job = dxpy.new_dxjob(fn_input=map_input, fn_name="map")
126	
127	    # Finally, we want the "postprocess" job to run after "map" is
128	    # done calling "process" on each of its inputs.  Note that a job
129	    # is marked as "done" only after all of its child jobs are also
130	    # marked "done".
131	    postprocess_input = {
132	        "process_outputs": map_job.get_output_ref("process_outputs"),
133	        "additional_input": "file ID, for example"
134	        }
135	    postprocess_job = dxpy.new_dxjob(fn_input=postprocess_input,
136	                                     fn_name="postprocess",
137	                                     depends_on=[map_job])
138	DX_APP_WIZARD_UPLOAD_ANY_FILES
139	    # If you would like to include any of the output fields from the
140	    # postprocess_job as the output of your app, you should return it
141	    # here using a job-based object reference.
142	    #
143	    # return { "app_output_field": postprocess_job.get_output_ref("final_output"), ...}

146	    # objects (such as files) which will be closed by a job that
147	    # finishes later.  The system will check to make sure that the
148	    # output object is closed and will attempt to clone it out as
149	    # output into the parent container only after all subjobs have
150	    # finished.

67	def _get_version_suffix(src_dir, version):
68	    # If anything goes wrong, fall back to the date-based suffix.
69	    try:
70	        if os.path.exists(os.path.join(src_dir, ".git")):
71	            abbrev_sha1 = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], cwd=src_dir).strip()[:7]
72	            # We ensure that if VERSION is semver-compliant, then
73	            # VERSION + SUFFIX will be too. In particular that means
74	            # (here and in _get_timestamp_version_suffix above) we add
75	            # what semver refers to as a "build metadata" section
76	            # (delimited by "+"), unless one already exists, in which
77	            # case we append to the existing one.
78	            if "+" in version:
79	                return ".git." + abbrev_sha1
80	            else:

83	        pass

238	def _check_syntax(code, lang, temp_dir, enforce=True):
239	    """
240	    Checks that the code whose text is in CODE parses as LANG.
241	
242	    Raises DXSyntaxError if there is a problem and "enforce" is True.
243	    """
244	    # This function needs the language to be explicitly set, so we can
245	    # generate an appropriate temp filename.
246	    if lang == 'python2.7' or 'python3' in lang:
247	        temp_basename = 'inlined_code_from_dxapp_json.py'
248	    elif lang == 'bash':
249	        temp_basename = 'inlined_code_from_dxapp_json.sh'
250	    else:
251	        raise ValueError('lang must be one of "python2.7", "python3", or "bash"')
252	    # Dump the contents out to a temporary file, then call _check_file_syntax.
253	    with open(os.path.join(temp_dir, temp_basename), 'w') as ofile:
254	        ofile.write(code)
255	    _check_file_syntax(os.path.join(temp_dir, temp_basename), temp_dir, override_lang=lang, enforce=enforce)

258	# convert the error message embedded in the exception to a proper string
259	def _error_message_to_string(e, message):
260	    if isinstance(message, str):
261	        return message
262	    elif isinstance(message, bytes):
263	        return message.decode("utf-8")
264	    else:
265	        # What kind of object is this?

269	def _check_file_syntax(filename, temp_dir, override_lang=None, enforce=True):
270	    """
271	    Checks that the code in FILENAME parses, attempting to autodetect
272	    the language if necessary.
273	
274	    Raises IOError if the file cannot be read.
275	
276	    Raises DXSyntaxError if there is a problem and "enforce" is True.
277	    """
278	    def check_python(filename):
279	        # Generate a semi-recognizable name to write the pyc to. Of
280	        # course it's possible that different files being scanned could
281	        # have the same basename, so this path won't be unique, but the
282	        # checks don't run concurrently so this shouldn't cause any
283	        # problems.
284	        pyc_path = os.path.join(temp_dir, os.path.basename(filename) + ".pyc")
285	        try:
286	            py_compile.compile(filename, cfile=pyc_path, doraise=True)
287	        finally:
288	            try:
289	                os.unlink(pyc_path)
290	            except OSError:
291	                pass
292	    def check_bash(filename):
293	        if platform.system() == 'Windows':
294	            logging.warn(
295	                    'Skipping bash syntax check due to unavailability of bash on Windows.')
296	        else:
297	            subprocess.check_output(["/bin/bash", "-n", filename], stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
298	    python_unsure = False
299	    if override_lang == 'python2.7' and USING_PYTHON2:
300	        checker_fn = check_python
301	    elif override_lang == 'python3' and not USING_PYTHON2:
302	        checker_fn = check_python
303	    elif override_lang == 'bash':
304	        checker_fn = check_bash
305	    elif filename.endswith('.py'):
306	        checker_fn = check_python
307	        # don't enforce and ignore if the shebang is ambiguous and we're not sure
308	        # that the file version is the same as the one we're running
309	        read_mode = "r"
310	        with open(filename, read_mode) as f:
311	            first_line = f.readline()
312	            if not (('python3' in first_line and not USING_PYTHON2) or
313	                    ('python2' in first_line and USING_PYTHON2)):
314	                enforce = False
315	                python_unsure = True
316	    elif filename.endswith('.sh'):
317	        checker_fn = check_bash
318	    else:
319	        # Ignore other kinds of files.
320	        return
321	
322	    # Do a test read of the file to catch errors like the file not
323	    # existing or not being readable.
324	    open(filename)
325	
326	    try:
327	        checker_fn(filename)
328	    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
329	        print(filename + " has a syntax error! Interpreter output:", file=sys.stderr)
330	        errmsg = _error_message_to_string(e, e.output)
331	        for line in errmsg.strip("\n").split("\n"):
332	            print("  " + line.rstrip("\n"), file=sys.stderr)
333	        if enforce:
334	            raise DXSyntaxError(filename + " has a syntax error")
335	    except py_compile.PyCompileError as e:
336	        if python_unsure:
337	            print("Unsure if " + filename + " is using Python 2 or Python 3, the following error might not be relevant", file=sys.stderr)
338	        print(filename + " has a syntax error! Interpreter output:", file=sys.stderr)
339	        errmsg = _error_message_to_string(e, e.msg)
340	        print("  " + errmsg.strip(), file=sys.stderr)
341	        if enforce:
342	            raise DXSyntaxError(e.msg.strip())

401	                if not isinstance(manifest.get('access'), dict) or 'network' not in manifest['access']:
402	                    msg = '\n'.join(['runSpec.execDepends specifies non-APT dependencies, but no network access spec is given.',
403	                    'Add {"access": {"network": ["*"]}} to allow dependencies to install.',
404	                    'See https://documentation.dnanexus.com/developer/apps/execution-environment#network-access.',
405	                    'Rerun with --no-check-syntax to proceed anyway.'])
406	                    raise dxpy.app_builder.AppBuilderException(msg)

435	                try:
436	                    _check_file_syntax(os.path.join(dirpath, filename), temp_dir, enforce=True)
437	                except IOError as e:
438	                    raise dxpy.app_builder.AppBuilderException(
439	                        'Could not open file in resources directory %r. The problem was: %s' %
440	                        (os.path.join(dirpath, filename), e)
441	                    )
442	                except DXSyntaxError:
443	                    # Suppresses errors from _check_file_syntax so we
444	                    # only print a nice error message
445	                    files_with_problems.append(os.path.join(dirpath, filename))
446	
447	    if files_with_problems:
448	        # Make a message of the form:
449	        #    "/path/to/my/app.py"
450	        # OR "/path/to/my/app.py and 3 other files"
451	        files_str = files_with_problems[0] if len(files_with_problems) == 1 else (files_with_problems[0] + " and " + str(len(files_with_problems) - 1) + " other file" + ("s" if len(files_with_problems) > 2 else ""))
452	        logging.warn('%s contained syntax errors, see above for details' % (files_str,))

455	def _get_all_cluster_bootstrap_script_names(manifest):
456	    # runSpec.systemRequirements is deprecated. Enforce use of regionalOptions.
457	    if 'systemRequirements' in manifest['runSpec']:
458	        sys_reqs = manifest['runSpec']['systemRequirements']
459	        for entry_point in sys_reqs:
460	            if 'clusterSpec' in sys_reqs[entry_point]:
461	                err_msg = "\"clusterSpec\" in \"runSpec.systemRequirements\" is not accepted."
462	                err_msg += " It must be specified in \"systemRequirements\" under the \"regionalOptions\" field in all enabled regions of the app."
463	                raise dxpy.app_builder.AppBuilderException(err_msg)
464	
465	    script_names = []
466	    if 'regionalOptions' in manifest:
467	        for region in manifest['regionalOptions']:
468	            if 'systemRequirements' in manifest['regionalOptions'][region]:
469	                sys_reqs = manifest['regionalOptions'][region]['systemRequirements']
470	                for entry_point in sys_reqs:
471	                    try:
472	                        filename = sys_reqs[entry_point]['clusterSpec']['bootstrapScript']
473	                        script_names.append(filename)
474	                    except KeyError:
475	                        # either no "clusterSpec" or no "bootstrapScript" within "clusterSpec"
476	                        continue
477	
478	    return script_names

507	def _build_app_remote(mode, src_dir, publish=False, destination_override=None,
508	                      version_override=None, bill_to_override=None,
509	                      do_version_autonumbering=True, do_try_update=True, do_parallel_build=True,
510	                      do_check_syntax=True, region=None, watch=True):
511	    if mode == 'app':
512	        builder_app = 'app-tarball_app_builder'
513	    else:
514	        builder_app = 'app-tarball_applet_builder'
515	
516	    app_spec = _parse_app_spec(src_dir)
517	    builder_versions = {"12.04": "", "14.04": "_trusty", "16.04": "_xenial",
518	                        "20.04": "_focal", "24.04": "_noble"}
519	    release = app_spec['runSpec'].get('release')
520	    # Remote builder app/applet for 16.04 version 1
521	    if release == "16.04" and app_spec['runSpec'].get('version', '0') == '1':
522	        builder_app += "_xenial_v1"
523	    else:
524	        builder_app += builder_versions.get(release, "")
525	
526	
527	    temp_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
528	
529	    build_options = {}
530	
531	    if version_override:
532	        build_options['version_override'] = version_override
533	    elif do_version_autonumbering:
534	        # If autonumbering is DISABLED, the interior run of dx-build-app
535	        # will detect the correct version to use without our help. If it
536	        # is ENABLED, the version suffix might depend on the state of
537	        # the git repository. Since we'll remove the .git directory
538	        # before uploading, we need to determine the correct version to
539	        # use here and pass it in to the interior run of dx-build-app.
540	        if do_version_autonumbering:
541	            original_version = app_spec['version']
542	            app_describe = None
543	            try:
544	                app_describe = dxpy.api.app_describe("app-" + app_spec["name"], alias=original_version, always_retry=False)
545	            except dxpy.exceptions.DXAPIError as e:
546	                if e.name == 'ResourceNotFound' or (mode == 'applet' and e.name == 'PermissionDenied'):
547	                    pass
548	                else:
549	                    raise e
550	            if app_describe is not None:
551	                if 'published' in app_describe or not do_try_update:
552	                    # The version we wanted was taken; fall back to the
553	                    # autogenerated version number.
554	                    build_options['version_override'] = original_version + _get_version_suffix(src_dir, original_version)
555	
556	    # The following flags are basically passed through verbatim.
557	    if bill_to_override:
558	        build_options['bill_to_override'] = bill_to_override
559	    if not do_version_autonumbering:
560	        build_options['do_version_autonumbering'] = False
561	    if not do_try_update:
562	        build_options['do_try_update'] = False
563	    if not do_parallel_build:
564	        build_options['do_parallel_build'] = False
565	    if not do_check_syntax:
566	        build_options['do_check_syntax'] = False
567	
568	    using_temp_project_for_remote_build = False
569	
570	    # If building an applet, run the builder app in the destination
571	    # project. If building an app, run the builder app in a temporary
572	    # project.
573	    dest_folder = None
574	    dest_applet_name = None
575	    if mode == "applet":
576	        # Translate the --destination flag as follows. If --destination
577	        # is PROJ:FOLDER/NAME,
578	        #
579	        # 1. Run the builder app in PROJ
580	        # 2. Make the output folder FOLDER
581	        # 3. Supply --destination=NAME to the interior call of dx-build-applet.
582	        build_project_id = dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID
583	        if destination_override:
584	            build_project_id, dest_folder, dest_applet_name = parse_destination(destination_override)
585	        if build_project_id is None:
586	            parser.error("Can't create an applet without specifying a destination project; please use the -d/--destination flag to explicitly specify a project")
587	        if dest_applet_name:
588	            build_options['destination_override'] = '/' + dest_applet_name
589	
590	    elif mode == "app":
591	        using_temp_project_for_remote_build = True
592	        try:
593	            build_project_id = _create_temporary_build_project(
594	                "dx-build-app --remote temporary project",
595	                bill_to=bill_to_override,
596	                region=region)
597	        except:
598	            err_exit()
599	
600	    try:
601	        # Resolve relative paths and symlinks here so we have something
602	        # reasonable to write in the job name below.
603	        src_dir = os.path.realpath(src_dir)
604	
605	        # Show the user some progress as the tarball is being generated.
606	        # Hopefully this will help them to understand when their tarball
607	        # is huge (e.g. the target directory already has a whole bunch
608	        # of binaries in it) and interrupt before uploading begins.
609	        app_tarball_file = os.path.join(temp_dir, "app_tarball.tar.gz")
610	        tar_subprocess = subprocess.Popen(["tar", "-czf", "-", "--exclude", "./.git", "."], cwd=src_dir, stdout=subprocess.PIPE)
611	        with open(app_tarball_file, 'wb') as tar_output_file:
612	            total_num_bytes = 0
613	            last_console_update = 0
614	            start_time = time.time()
615	            printed_static_message = False
616	            # Pipe the output of tar into the output file
617	            while True:
618	                tar_exitcode = tar_subprocess.poll()
619	                data = tar_subprocess.stdout.read(4 * 1024 * 1024)
620	                if tar_exitcode is not None and len(data) == 0:
621	                    break
622	                tar_output_file.write(data)
623	                total_num_bytes += len(data)
624	                current_time = time.time()
625	                # Don't show status messages at all for very short tar
626	                # operations (< 1.0 sec)
627	                if current_time - last_console_update > 0.25 and current_time - start_time > 1.0:
628	                    if sys.stderr.isatty():
629	                        if last_console_update > 0:
630	                            sys.stderr.write("\r")
631	                        sys.stderr.write("Compressing target directory {dir}... ({kb_so_far:,} kb)".format(dir=src_dir, kb_so_far=total_num_bytes // 1024))
632	                        sys.stderr.flush()
633	                        last_console_update = current_time
634	                    elif not printed_static_message:
635	                        # Print a message (once only) when stderr is not
636	                        # going to a live console
637	                        sys.stderr.write("Compressing target directory %s..." % (src_dir,))
638	                        printed_static_message = True
639	
640	        if last_console_update > 0:
641	            sys.stderr.write("\n")
642	        if tar_exitcode != 0:
643	            raise Exception("tar exited with non-zero exit code " + str(tar_exitcode))
644	
645	        dxpy.set_workspace_id(build_project_id)
646	
647	        remote_file = dxpy.upload_local_file(app_tarball_file, media_type="application/gzip",
648	                                             wait_on_close=True, show_progress=True)
649	
650	        try:
651	            input_hash = {
652	                "input_file": dxpy.dxlink(remote_file),
653	                "build_options": build_options
654	                }
655	            if mode == 'app':
656	                input_hash["publish"] = publish
657	            api_options = {
658	                "name": "Remote build of %s" % (os.path.basename(src_dir),),
659	                "input": input_hash,
660	                "project": build_project_id,
661	                }
662	            if dest_folder:
663	                api_options["folder"] = dest_folder
664	            app_run_result = dxpy.api.app_run(builder_app, input_params=api_options)
665	            job_id = app_run_result["id"]
666	            print("Started builder job %s" % (job_id,))
667	            if watch:
668	                try:
669	                    subprocess.check_call(["dx", "watch", job_id])
670	                except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
671	                    if e.returncode == 3:
672	                        # Some kind of failure to build the app. The reason
673	                        # for the failure is probably self-evident from the
674	                        # job log (and if it's not, the CalledProcessError
675	                        # is not informative anyway), so just propagate the
676	                        # return code without additional remarks.
677	                        sys.exit(3)
678	                    else:
679	                        raise e
680	
681	            dxpy.DXJob(job_id).wait_on_done(interval=1)
682	
683	            if mode == 'applet':
684	                applet_id, _ = dxpy.get_dxlink_ids(dxpy.api.job_describe(job_id)['output']['output_applet'])
685	                return applet_id
686	            else:
687	                # TODO: determine and return the app ID, to allow
688	                # running the app if args.run is specified
689	                return None
690	        finally:
691	            if not using_temp_project_for_remote_build:
692	                dxpy.DXProject(build_project_id).remove_objects([remote_file.get_id()])
693	    finally:
694	        if using_temp_project_for_remote_build:
695	            dxpy.api.project_destroy(build_project_id, {"terminateJobs": True})
696	        shutil.rmtree(temp_dir)
697

699	def build_app_from(applet_desc, version, publish=False, do_try_update=True, bill_to_override=None,
700	                   return_object_dump=False, confirm=True, brief=False, **kwargs):
701	
702	    applet_id = applet_desc["id"]
703	    app_name = applet_desc["name"]
704	    dxpy.executable_builder.verify_developer_rights('app-' + app_name)
705	    if not brief:
706	        logger.info("Will create app from the applet: %s (%s)" % (applet_desc["name"], applet_desc['id'],))
707	
708	    applet_region = dxpy.api.project_describe(applet_desc["project"],
709	                                              input_params={"fields": {"region": True}})["region"]
710	
711	    #TODO: make it possible to build multi region app by uploadling
712	    # the applet tarball to different regions
713	    regional_options = {
714	        applet_region: {'applet': applet_id}
715	    }
716	
717	    # Certain metadata is not copied from an applet to the app
718	    # It must be passed explicitly otherwise default values will be
719	    # set by the API server or an error will be throw during app build
720	    # for required non-empty fields
721	    fields_to_inherit = (
722	        "summary", "title", "description", "developerNotes",
723	        "details", "access", "ignoreReuse"
724	    )
725	    inherited_metadata = {}
726	    for field in fields_to_inherit:
727	        if field in applet_desc:
728	            inherited_metadata[field] = applet_desc[field]
729	
730	    required_non_empty = ("summary", "title", "description", "developerNotes")
731	    for field in required_non_empty:
732	        if field not in inherited_metadata or not inherited_metadata[field]:
733	            inherited_metadata[field] = applet_desc["name"]
734	
735	    app_id = dxpy.app_builder.create_app_multi_region(regional_options,
736	                                                      app_name,
737	                                                      None,
738	                                                      publish=publish,
739	                                                      set_default=publish,
740	                                                      billTo=bill_to_override,
741	                                                      try_versions=version,
742	                                                      try_update=do_try_update,
743	                                                      confirm=confirm,
744	                                                      inherited_metadata=inherited_metadata,
745	                                                      brief=brief)
746	    app_describe = dxpy.api.app_describe(app_id)
747	
748	    if not brief:
749	        if publish:
750	            logger.info("Uploaded and published app %s/%s (%s) successfully" % (app_describe["name"], app_describe["version"], app_id))
751	        else:
752	            logger.info("Uploaded app %s/%s (%s) successfully" % (app_describe["name"], app_describe["version"], app_id))
753	            logger.info("You can publish this app with: dx publish {n}/{v}".format(n=app_describe["name"], v=app_describe["version"]))
754	
755	    return app_describe if return_object_dump else {"id": app_id}

758	def build_and_upload_locally(src_dir, mode, overwrite=False, archive=False, publish=False, destination_override=None,
759	                             version_override=None, bill_to_override=None, use_temp_build_project=True,
760	                             do_parallel_build=True, do_version_autonumbering=True, do_try_update=True,

773	    using_temp_project = False

782	
783	    # Prepare projects in which the app's underlying applets will be built (one per region).

793	        region = dxpy.api.project_describe(working_project,

796	    elif mode == "app" and use_temp_build_project and not dry_run:
797	        projects_by_region = {}
798	        if enabled_regions is not None:

813	        else:
814	            # Create a temp project

816	                working_project = _create_temporary_build_project(
817	                    "Temporary build project for dx-build-app",
818	                    bill_to=bill_to_override)
819	            except:
820	                err_exit()
821	            region = dxpy.api.project_describe(working_project,
822	                                               input_params={"fields": {"region": True}})["region"]
823	            projects_by_region[region] = working_project
824	            logger.debug("Created temporary project %s to build in" % (working_project,))

840	            parser.error("Can't create an applet without specifying a destination project; please use the -d/--destination flag to explicitly specify a project")
841	
842	        if mode == "applet":

904	                    resources_bundles_by_region[region],

907	                    archive=archive and mode == "applet",
908	                    project=project,
909	                    override_folder=override_folder,
910	                    override_name=override_applet_name,
911	                    dry_run=dry_run,
912	                    brief=brief,
913	                    **kwargs)
914	                if not dry_run:

916	                applet_ids_by_region[region] = applet_id
917	        except:
918	            # Avoid leaking any bundled_resources files we may have

925	                    if objects_to_delete:

1740	def validate_cohort_ids(descriptor, project, resp, ids):

1748	    # Prepare a payload to find entries matching the input ids in the dataset
1749	    if gpk_type in ["integer", "bigint"]:
1750	        lambda_for_list_conv = lambda a, b: a+[int(b)]
1751	    elif gpk_type in ["float", "double"]:
1752	        lambda_for_list_conv = lambda a, b: a+[float(b)]
1753	    elif gpk_type in ["string"]:

1755	    else:
1756	        err_msg = "Invalid input record. Cohort ID field in the input dataset or cohortbrowser record is of type, {type}. Support is currently only available for Cohort ID fields having one of the following types; string, integer and float".format(type = gpk_type)
1757	        raise ValueError(err_msg) 
1758	    id_list = reduce(lambda_for_list_conv, ids, [])
1759	
1760	    entity_field_name = "{}${}".format(entity_name, field_name)
1761	    fields_list = [{field_name: entity_field_name}]
1762

1769	                "filters": {
1770	                    entity_field_name: [

1772	                    ]
1773	                }
1774	            }
1775	        }
1776	    }
1777	
1778	    # Use the dxpy raw_api_function to send a POST request to the server with our payload
1779	    try:
1780	        resp_raw = raw_api_call(resp, payload)

1782	        raise VizserverError(
1783	            "Exception caught while validating cohort ids.  Bad response from Vizserver."
1784	            "Original Error message:\n{}"
1785	        ).format(str(exc))
1786	    # Order of samples doesn't matter so using set here
1787	    discovered_ids = set()
1788	    # Parse the results objects for the cohort ids
1789	    for result in resp_raw["results"]:
1790	        discovered_ids.add(result[field_name])
1791	
1792	    # Compare the discovered cohort ids to the user-provided cohort ids
1793	    if discovered_ids != set(id_list):

1795	        missing_ids = set(id_list).difference(discovered_ids)
1796	        err_msg = "The following supplied IDs do not match IDs in the main entity of dataset, {dataset_name}: {ids}".format(dataset_name = resp["dataset"], ids = missing_ids)

1974	class DXDatasetDescriptor:
1975	    """
1976	    A class to represent a parsed descriptor of a Dataset record object.

1978	    Attributes
1979	        Representation of JSON object stored in descriptor file
