755	def _validate_resolution_output_length(path, entity_name, results, allow_mult=False, all_mult=False,
756	                                       ask_to_resolve=True):
757	    """
758	    :param path: Path to the object that required resolution; propagated from
759	                 command-line
760	    :type path: string
761	    :param entity_name: Name of the object
762	    :type entity_name: string
763	    :param results: Result of resolution; non-empty list of object
764	                    specifications (each specification is a dictionary with
765	                    keys "project" and "id")
766	    :type results: list of dictionaries
767	    :param allow_mult: If True, it is okay to choose from multiple results
768	                       of a single resolved object, or return all results
769	                       found; if False, raise an error if multiple results
770	                       are found
771	    :type allow_mult: boolean
772	    :param all_mult: If True, return all results if multiple results are
773	                     found for a single resolved object; if False, user needs
774	                     to choose a single result if multiple are found; the value
775	                     of all_mult only has an effect if allow_mult is True)
776	    :type all_mult: boolean
777	    :param ask_to_resolve: Whether picking may be necessary (if True, a
778	                           list is returned; if False, only one result
779	                           is returned); if specified as True, then all
780	                           results will be returned, regardless of the
781	                           values of allow_mult and all_mult
782	    :type ask_to_resolve: boolean
783	    :returns: The results of resolving entity_name, expected to be of the
784	              following form:
785	              <resolved_object>  # If only one result is present or the user
786	                                 # is able to select from multiple
787	              OR
788	              [<resolved_object>, ...]  # If multiple results are present and
789	                                        # it is allowed
790	              where <resolved_object> is of the following form:
791	              {"project": <project_id>, "id": <object_id>}
792	    :rtype: dict or list of dicts
793	    :raises: ValueError if results is empty
794	    :raises: ResolutionError if too many results are found and the user is
795	             not in interactive mode and cannot select one
796	
797	    Precondition: results must be a nonempty list
798	
799	    Validates length of results.
800	
801	    If there are multiple results found and the user is in interactive mode,
802	    then the user will be prompted to select a single result to be returned.
803	    """
804	    if len(results) == 0:
805	        raise ValueError("'results' must be nonempty.")
806	
807	    # Caller wants ALL results, so return the entire results list
808	    # At this point, do not care about the values of allow_mult or all_mult
809	    if not ask_to_resolve:
810	        return results
811	
812	    if len(results) > 1:
813	        # The other way the caller can specify it wants all results is by setting
814	        # allow_mult to be True and allowing all_mult to be True (or if the object name is a glob pattern)
815	        if allow_mult and (all_mult or is_glob_pattern(entity_name)):
816	            return results
817	        if INTERACTIVE_CLI:
818	            print('The given path "' + path + '" resolves to the following data objects:')
819	            if any(['describe' not in result for result in results]):
820	                # findDataObject API call must be made to get 'describe' mappings
821	                project, folderpath, entity_name = resolve_path(path, expected='entity')
822	                results = _resolve_global_entity(project, folderpath, entity_name)
823	            choice = pick([get_ls_l_desc(result['describe']) for result in results],
824	                          allow_mult=allow_mult)
825	            if allow_mult and choice == '*':
826	                return results
827	            else:
828	                return [results[choice]] if allow_mult else results[choice]
829	        else:
830	            raise ResolutionError('The given path "' + path + '" resolves to ' +
831	                                  str(len(results)) + ' data objects')
832	    else:
833	        return [results[0]] if allow_mult else results[0]

941	def resolve_multiple_existing_paths(paths):
942	    """
943	    :param paths: A list of paths to items that need to be resolved
944	    :type paths: list
945	    :returns: A dictionary mapping a specified path to either its resolved
946	              object or Nones, if the object could not be resolved
947	    :rtype: dict
948	
949	    For each input given in paths, attempts to resolve the path, and returns
950	    the resolved object in a dictionary.
951	
952	    The return value will look like:
953	    {<path1>: <resolved_object1>, <path2>: <resolved_object2>,...}
954	
955	    If entity_id is a DX ID that can be described,
956	        <resolved_object*> ::= {"project": None,
957	                                "folder": None,
958	                                "name": {"id": <id>,
959	                                         "describe": <describe_output>}}
960	
961	    Else if a general resolution (or search) method will be used to resolve
962	    the entity,
963	        <resolved_object*> ::= {"project": <project>,
964	                                "folder": None,
965	                                "name": {"project": <project>,
966	                                         "id": <resolved_id>}}
967	
968	    Else if <project> is a job ID,
969	        <resolved_object*> ::= {"project": None,
970	                                "folder": None,
971	                                "name": {"project": <project>,
972	                                         "id": <resolved_id>}}
973	
974	    Else if the path refers to a folder instead of a data object,
975	        <resolved_object*> ::= {"project": <project>,
976	                                "folder": <folder>,
977	                                "name": None}
978	
979	    Else if description or resolution fails,
980	        <resolved_object*> ::= {"project": None, "folder": None, "name": None}
981	    """
982	    done_objects = {}  # Return value
983	    to_resolve_in_batch_paths = []  # Paths to resolve
984	    to_resolve_in_batch_inputs = []  # Project, folderpath, and entity name
985	    for path in paths:
986	        project, folderpath, entity_name = resolve_path(path, expected='entity')
987	        try:
988	            must_resolve, project, folderpath, entity_name = _check_resolution_needed(
989	                path, project, folderpath, entity_name)
990	        except:
991	            must_resolve = False
992	
993	        if must_resolve:
994	            if is_glob_pattern(entity_name):
995	                # TODO: Must call findDataObjects because resolveDataObjects does not support glob patterns
996	                try:
997	                    find_results = _resolve_global_entity(project, folderpath, entity_name)
998	                    done_objects[path] = _format_resolution_output(path, project, folderpath, entity_name,
999	                                                                   find_results)
1000	                except ResolutionError:
1001	                    # Catches any ResolutionError thrown by _resolve_global_entity
1002	                    done_objects[path] = {"project": None, "folder": None, "name": None}
1003	            else:
1004	                # Prepare batch call for resolveDataObjects
1005	                to_resolve_in_batch_paths.append(path)
1006	                to_resolve_in_batch_inputs.append({"project": project, "folder": folderpath, "name": entity_name})
1007	        else:
1008	            # No need to resolve
1009	            done_objects[path] = {"project": project, "folder": folderpath, "name": entity_name}
1010	
1011	    # Call resolveDataObjects
1012	    resolution_results = dxpy.resolve_data_objects(to_resolve_in_batch_inputs)
1013	    for path, inputs, result in zip(to_resolve_in_batch_paths, to_resolve_in_batch_inputs,
1014	                                    resolution_results):
1015	        done_objects[path] = _format_resolution_output(path, inputs["project"], inputs["folder"], inputs["name"],
1016	                                                       result)
1017	    return done_objects

17	'''

19	   location of the input and output directories. It also has a utility for parsing
20	   the job input file ('job_input.json').
21	
22	We use the following shorthands
23	   <idir> == input directory     $HOME/in
24	   <odir> == output directory    $HOME/out
25	
26	A simple example of the job input, when run locally, is:
27	
28	{
29	    "seq2": {
30	        "$dnanexus_link": {
31	            "project": "project-1111",
32	            "id": "file-1111"
33	        }
34	    },
35	    "seq1": {
36	        "$dnanexus_link": {
37	            "project": "project-2222",
38	            "id": "file-2222"
39	        }
40	    }
41	    "blast_args": "",
42	    "evalue": 0.01
43	}
44	
45	The first two elements are files {seq1, seq2}, the other elements are
46	{blast_args, evalue}. The files for seq1,seq2 should be saved into:
47	<idir>/seq1/<filename>
48	<idir>/seq2/<filename>
49	
50	An example for a shell command that would create these arguments is:
51	    $ dx run coolapp -iseq1=NC_000868.fasta -iseq2=NC_001422.fasta
52	It would run an app named "coolapp", with file arguments for seq1 and seq2. Both NC_*
53	files should be the names of files in a DNAnexus project (and should be resolved to their
54	file IDs by dx). Subsequently, after dx-download-all-inputs is run,
55	file seq1 should appear in the execution environment at path:
56	    <idir>/seq1/NC_000868.fasta
57	
58	File Arrays
59	
60	{
61	    "reads": [{
62	        "$dnanexus_link": {
63	            "project": "project-3333",
64	            "id": "file-3333"
65	        }
66	    },
67	    {
68	        "$dnanexus_link": {
69	            "project": "project-4444",
70	            "id": "file-4444"
71	        }
72	    }]
73	}
74	
75	This is a file array with two files. Running a command like this:
76	    $ dx run coolapp -ireads=A.fastq -ireads=B.fasta
77	will download into the execution environment:
78	<idir>/reads/A.fastq
79	             B.fastq
80

178	def make_unix_filename(fname):
179	    """
180	    :param fname: the basename of a file (e.g., xxx in /zzz/yyy/xxx).
181	    :returns: a valid unix filename
182	    :rtype: string
183	    :raises: DXError if the filename is invalid on a Unix system
184	
185	    The problem being solved here is that *fname* is a python string, it
186	    may contain characters that are invalid for a file name. We replace all the slashes with %2F.
187	    Another issue, is that the user may choose an invalid name. Since we focus
188	    on Unix systems, the only possibilies are "." and "..".
189	    """
190	    # sanity check for filenames
191	    bad_filenames = [".", ".."]
192	    if fname in bad_filenames:
193	        raise DXError("Invalid filename {}".format(fname))
194	    return fname.replace('/', '%2F')

202	def get_job_input_filenames(job_input_file):
203	    """Extract list of files, returns a set of directories to create, and
204	    a set of files, with sources and destinations. The paths created are
205	    relative to the input directory.
206	
207	    Note: we go through file names inside arrays, and create a
208	    separate subdirectory for each. This avoids clobbering files when
209	    duplicate filenames appear in an array.
210	    """
211	    def get_input_hash():
212	        with open(job_input_file) as fh:
213	            job_input = json.load(fh)
214	            return job_input
215	    job_input = get_input_hash()
216	
217	    files = collections.defaultdict(list)  # dictionary, with empty lists as default elements
218	    dirs = []  # directories to create under <idir>
219	
220	    # Local function for adding a file to the list of files to be created
221	    # for example:
222	    #    iname == "seq1"
223	    #    subdir == "015"
224	    #    value == { "$dnanexus_link": {
225	    #       "project": "project-BKJfY1j0b06Z4y8PX8bQ094f",
226	    #       "id": "file-BKQGkgQ0b06xG5560GGQ001B"
227	    #    }
228	    # will create a record describing that the file should
229	    # be downloaded into seq1/015/<filename>
230	    def add_file(iname, subdir, value):
231	        if not dxpy.is_dxlink(value):
232	            return
233	        handler = dxpy.get_handler(value)
234	        if not isinstance(handler, dxpy.DXFile):
235	            return
236	        filename = make_unix_filename(handler.name)
237	        trg_dir = iname
238	        if subdir is not None:
239	            trg_dir = os.path.join(trg_dir, subdir)
240	        files[iname].append({'trg_fname': os.path.join(trg_dir, filename),
241	                             'handler': handler,
242	                             'src_file_id': handler.id})
243	        dirs.append(trg_dir)
244	
245	    # An array of inputs, for a single key. A directory
246	    # will be created per array entry. For example, if the input key is
247	    # FOO, and the inputs are {A, B, C}.vcf then, the directory structure
248	    # will be:
249	    #   <idir>/FOO/00/A.vcf
250	    #   <idir>/FOO/01/B.vcf
251	    #   <idir>/FOO/02/C.vcf
252	    def add_file_array(input_name, links):
253	        num_files = len(links)
254	        if num_files == 0:
255	            return
256	        num_digits = len(str(num_files - 1))
257	        dirs.append(input_name)
258	        for i, link in enumerate(links):
259	            subdir = str(i).zfill(num_digits)
260	            add_file(input_name, subdir, link)
261	
262	    for input_name, value in list(job_input.items()):
263	        if isinstance(value, list):
264	            # This is a file array
265	            add_file_array(input_name, value)
266	        else:
267	            add_file(input_name, None, value)
268	
269	    ## create a dictionary of the all non-file elements
270	    rest_hash = {key: val for key, val in list(job_input.items()) if key not in files}
271	    return dirs, files, rest_hash

274	def get_input_spec_patterns():
275	    ''' Extract the inputSpec patterns, if they exist -- modifed from dx-upload-all-outputs
276	
277	    Returns a dict of all patterns, with keys equal to the respective
278	    input parameter names.
279	    '''
280	    input_spec = None
281	    if 'DX_JOB_ID' in os.environ:
282	        # works in the cloud, not locally
283	        job_desc = dxpy.describe(dxpy.JOB_ID)
284	        if job_desc["function"] == "main":
285	            # The input spec does not apply for subjobs
286	            desc = dxpy.describe(job_desc.get("app", job_desc.get("applet")))
287	            if "inputSpec" in desc:
288	                input_spec = desc["inputSpec"]
289	    elif 'DX_TEST_DXAPP_JSON' in os.environ:
290	        # works only locally
291	        path_to_dxapp_json = os.environ['DX_TEST_DXAPP_JSON']
292	        with open(path_to_dxapp_json) as fd:
293	            dxapp_json = json.load(fd)
294	            input_spec = dxapp_json.get('inputSpec')
295	
296	    # convert to a dictionary. Each entry in the input spec
297	    # has {name, class} attributes.
298	    if input_spec is None:
299	        return {}
300	
301	    # For each field name, return its patterns.
302	    # Make sure a pattern is legal, ignore illegal patterns.
303	    def is_legal_pattern(pattern):
304	        return "*" in pattern
305	    patterns_dict = {}
306	    for spec in input_spec:
307	        name = spec['name']
308	        if 'patterns' in spec:
309	            patterns_dict[name] = []
310	            for p in spec['patterns']:
311	                if is_legal_pattern(p):
312	                    patterns_dict[name].append(p)
313	    return patterns_dict

317	def choose_shorter_string(p, q):

319	        return q
320	    if q is None:
321	        return p
322	    if len(q) < len(p):
323	        return q

327	def analyze_bash_vars(job_input_file, job_homedir):
328	    '''
329	    This function examines the input file, and calculates variables to
330	    instantiate in the shell environment. It is called right before starting the
331	    execution of an app in a worker.
332	
333	    For each input key, we want to have
334	    $var
335	    $var_filename
336	    $var_prefix
337	       remove last dot (+gz), and/or remove patterns
338	    $var_path
339	       $HOME/in/var/$var_filename
340	
341	    For example,
342	    $HOME/in/genes/A.txt
343	                   B.txt
344	
345	    export genes=('{"$dnanexus_link": "file-xxxx"}' '{"$dnanexus_link": "file-yyyy"}')
346	    export genes_filename=("A.txt" "B.txt")
347	    export genes_prefix=("A" "B")
348	    export genes_path=("$HOME/in/genes/A.txt" "$HOME/in/genes/B.txt")
349	
350	    If there are patterns defined in the input spec, then the prefix respects them.
351	    Here are several examples, where the patterns are:
352	       *.bam, *.bwa-index.tar.gz, foo*.sam, z*ra.sam
353	
354	    file name                prefix     matches
355	    foo.zed.bam              foo.zed    *.bam
356	    xxx.bwa-index.tar.gz     xxx        *.bwa-index.tar.gz
357	    food.sam                 food       foo*.sam
358	    zebra.sam                zebra      z*ra.sam
359	    xx.c                     xx
360	    xx.c.gz                  xx
361	
362	    The only patterns we recognize are of the form x*.y. For example:
363	      legal    *.sam, *.c.py,  foo*.sam,  a*b*c.baz
364	      ignored  uu.txt x???.tar  mon[a-z].py
365	    '''
366	    _, file_entries, rest_hash = get_job_input_filenames(job_input_file)
367	    patterns_dict = get_input_spec_patterns()
368	
369	    # Note: there may be multiple matches, choose the shortest prefix.
370	    def get_prefix(basename, key):
371	        best_prefix = None
372	        patterns = patterns_dict.get(key)
373	        if patterns is not None:
374	            for pattern in patterns:
375	                if fnmatch.fnmatch(basename, pattern):
376	                    _, _, right_piece = pattern.rpartition("*")
377	                    best_prefix = choose_shorter_string(best_prefix, basename[:-len(right_piece)])
378	        if best_prefix is not None:
379	            return best_prefix
380	        else:
381	            # no matching rule
382	            parts = os.path.splitext(basename)
383	            if parts[1] == ".gz":
384	                parts = os.path.splitext(parts[0])
385	            return parts[0]
386	
387	    def factory():
388	        return {'handler': [], 'basename': [],  'prefix': [], 'path': []}
389	    file_key_descs = collections.defaultdict(factory)
390	    rel_home_dir = get_input_dir(job_homedir)
391	    for key, entries in list(file_entries.items()):
392	        for entry in entries:
393	            filename = entry['trg_fname']
394	            basename = os.path.basename(filename)
395	            prefix = get_prefix(basename, key)
396	            k_desc = file_key_descs[key]
397	            k_desc['handler'].append(entry['handler'])
398	            k_desc['basename'].append(basename)
399	            k_desc['prefix'].append(prefix)
400	            k_desc['path'].append(os.path.join(rel_home_dir, filename))
401	    return file_key_descs, rest_hash
402	
403	
404	def gen_bash_vars(job_input_file, job_homedir=None, check_name_collision=True):
405	    """
406	    :param job_input_file: path to a JSON file describing the job inputs
407	    :param job_homedir: path to home directory, used for testing purposes
408	    :param check_name_collision: should we check for name collisions?
409	    :return: list of lines
410	    :rtype: list of strings
411	
412	    Calculates a line for each shell variable to instantiate.
413	    If *check_name_collision* is true, then detect and warn about
414	    collisions with essential environment variables.
415	    """
416	    file_key_descs, rest_hash = analyze_bash_vars(job_input_file, job_homedir)
417	
418	    def string_of_elem(elem):
419	        result = None
420	        if isinstance(elem, basestring):
421	            result = elem
422	        elif isinstance(elem, dxpy.DXFile):
423	            result = json.dumps(dxpy.dxlink(elem))

428	    def string_of_value(val):
429	        if isinstance(val, list):

44	    """

14	system requirements.

17	class SystemRequirementsDict(object):
18	    """
19	    A class representing system requirements that can be passed as
20	    "systemRequirements" or an entry of the "systemRequirementsByExecutable"
21	    to the class-xxxx/run or job/new API call (after converting
22	    it to a dictionary with as_dict()).
23	    """
24	
25	    def __init__(self, entrypoints):
26	        """
27	        Example of the entrypoints input:
28	        {"main":
29	            {"instanceType": "mem2_hdd2_x2"},
30	         "other_function":
31	            {"instanceType": "mem2_hdd2_x1",
32	             "clusterSpec": {"type": "spark",
33	                             "version": "2.4.0",
34	                             "initialInstanceCount": 2}}}
35	        """
36	        if entrypoints is not None and not isinstance(entrypoints, dict):
37	            raise DXError("Expected entrypoints to be a dict or None")
38	        self.entrypoints = copy.deepcopy(entrypoints)
39	
40	    @classmethod
41	    def from_instance_count(cls, instance_count_arg, entrypoint="*"):
42	        """
43	        Returns a SystemRequirementsDict that can be passed as a
44	        "systemRequirements" input or an entry of the "systemRequirementsByExecutable" mapping
45	        to job/new or run/ API calls.
46	        The instance_count_arg should be either a:
47	        * string or int eg. "6" or 8
48	        * dictionary, eg. {"main": 4, "other_function": 2}
49	        """
50	        try:
51	            if instance_count_arg is None:
52	                return cls(None)
53	            if isinstance(instance_count_arg, basestring) or isinstance(instance_count_arg, int):
54	                return cls({entrypoint: {"clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": int(instance_count_arg)}}})
55	            if isinstance(instance_count_arg, dict):
56	                return cls({k: {"clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": int(v)}} for k, v in instance_count_arg.items()})
57	            raise ValueError
58	        except ValueError:
59	            DXError('Expected instance_count field to be either an int, string or a dict')
60	
61	    @classmethod
62	    def from_instance_type(cls, instance_type_arg, entrypoint="*"):
63	        """
64	        Returns SystemRequirementsDict that can be passed as a
65	        "systemRequirements" input or an entry of the "systemRequirementsByExecutable" mapping
66	        to job/new or run/ API calls.
67	        The instance_type_arg should be either a:
68	        * string, eg. mem1_ssd1_x2
69	        * dictionary, eg. {"main": "mem2_hdd2_x2", "other_function": "mem2_hdd2_x1"}
70	        """
71	        if instance_type_arg is None:
72	            return cls(None)
73	        if isinstance(instance_type_arg, basestring):
74	            # By default, all entry points ("*") should use this instance type
75	            return cls({entrypoint: {"instanceType": instance_type_arg}})
76	        if isinstance(instance_type_arg, dict):
77	            # instance_type is a map of entry point to instance type
78	            return cls({fn: {"instanceType": fn_inst} for fn, fn_inst in instance_type_arg.items()})
79	        raise DXError('Expected instance_type field to be either a string or a dict')

83	        """

85	        It can extract only entrypoints with specific fields ('clusterSpec',
86	        'instanceType', 'instanceTypeSelector', etc), depending on the value of _type.
87	        """

89	        if _type not in (allowed_types):
90	            raise DXError("Expected '_type' to be one of the following: {}".format(allowed_types))
91	
92	        if _type == 'all':
93	            return cls(system_requirements)
94	
95	        extracted = defaultdict(dict)
96	        for entrypoint, req in system_requirements.items():
97	            if _type in req:
98	                extracted[entrypoint][_type] = req[_type]
99	        return cls(dict(extracted))
100	
101	    def override_cluster_spec(self, srd):
102	        """
103	        Returns SystemRequirementsDict can be passed in a "systemRequirements"
104	        input or as an entry of the "systemRequirementsByExecutable" mapping
105	        to app-xxx/run, e.g. {'fn': {'clusterSpec': {initialInstanceCount: 3, version: "2.4.0", ..}}}
106	        Since full clusterSpec must be passed to the API server, we need to retrieve the cluster
107	        spec defined in app doc's systemRequirements and overwrite the field initialInstanceCount
108	        with the value the user passed to dx run for each entrypoint.
109	        initialInstanceCount is currently the only clusterSpec's field the user is allowed to change
110	        at runtime.
111	        A few scenarios when requesting instance count for different entrypoints with dx run 
112	        and the resulting merged systemRequirements (merged_cluster_spec). The bootstapScript
113	        field here is only one of many (version, ports, etc) that should be copied from app
114	        spec to merged_cluster_spec:
115	
116	        Requested: {"*": 5}

118	                "other": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 9, bootstrapScript: "y.sh"}}

120	                "other": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 5, bootstrapScript: "y.sh"}}

124	                  "other": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 9, bootstrapScript: "y.sh"},
125	                  "*": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 11, bootstrapScript: "y.sh"}}
126	        Merged: {"main": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 15, bootstrapScript: "x.sh"},
127	                 "other": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 15, bootstrapScript: "y.sh"},
128	                 "*": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 15, bootstrapScript: "y.sh"}}
129

132	                  "other": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 9, bootstrapScript: "y.sh"}}
133	        Merged: {"main": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 12, bootstrapScript: "x.sh"}}

137	        Merged: {"main": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 33, bootstrapScript: "z.sh"}}

140	        App doc: {"*": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 2, bootstrapScript: "t.sh"}}
141	        Merged: {"main": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 22, bootstrapScript: "t.sh"},
142	                 "*": "clusterSpec": {"initialInstanceCount": 11, bootstrapScript: "t.sh"}}
143	        """

145	        merged_cluster_spec = copy.deepcopy(self.entrypoints)
146	
147	        # Remove entrypoints without "clusterSpec"
148	        merged_cluster_spec = dict([(k, v) for k, v in merged_cluster_spec.items() if v.get("clusterSpec") is not None])

def dump_executable(executable, destination_directory, omit_resources=False, describe_output={}):
    """
    Reconstitutes an app, applet, or a workflow into a directory that would
    create a functionally identical executable if "dx build" were run on it.
    destination_directory will be the root source directory for the
    executable.

    :param executable: executable, i.e. app, applet, or workflow, to be dumped
    :type executable: DXExecutable (either of: DXApp, DXApplet, DXWorkflow, DXGlobalWorkflow)
    :param destination_directory: an existing, empty, and writable directory
    :type destination_directory: str
    :param omit_resources: if True, executable's resources will not be downloaded
    :type omit_resources: boolean
    :param describe_output: output of a describe API call on the executable
    :type describe_output: dictionary
    """
    try:
        old_cwd = os.getcwd()
        os.chdir(destination_directory)
        if isinstance(executable, dxpy.DXWorkflow):
            _dump_workflow(executable, describe_output)
        elif isinstance(executable, dxpy.DXGlobalWorkflow):
            # Add inputs, outputs, stages. These fields contain region-specific values
            # e.g. files or applets, that's why:
            # * if the workflow is global, we will unpack the underlying workflow
            #   from the region of the current project context
            # * if this is a regular, project-based workflow, we will just use
            #   its description (the describe_output that we already have)
            # Underlying workflows are workflows stored in resource containers
            # of the global workflow (one per each region the global workflow is
            # enabled in). #TODO: add a link to documentation.
            current_project = dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID
            if not current_project:
                raise DXError(
                    'A project needs to be selected to "dx get" a global workflow. You can use "dx select" to select a project')
            region = dxpy.api.project_describe(current_project,
                                               input_params={"fields": {"region": True}})["region"]
            describe_output = executable.append_underlying_workflow_desc(describe_output, region)
            _dump_workflow(executable, describe_output)
        else:
            _dump_app_or_applet(executable, omit_resources, describe_output)
    except:
        err_exit()
    finally:
        os.chdir(old_cwd)

    if info["runSpec"]["interpreter"] == "bash":

    elif info["runSpec"]["interpreter"].startswith("python"):
        suffix = "py"
    else:

            info["runSpec"]["interpreter"]), file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    # Entry point script
    script = "src/code.{}".format(suffix)
    os.mkdir("src")

        f.write(info["runSpec"]["code"])

        """
        Writes the string `code` into a file at the relative path
        "src/<region>_<entry_point>_clusterBootstrap.<suffix>"
        """
        script_name = "src/{}_{}_clusterBootstrap.{}".format(region, entry_point, suffix)
        with open(script_name, "w") as f:

41	def get_parsed_destination(dest_str):
42	    """
43	    Parses dest_str, which is (roughly) of the form
44	    PROJECT:/FOLDER/NAME, and returns a tuple (project, folder, name)
45	    """
46	    # Interpret strings of form "project-XXXX" (no colon) as project. If

65	def inline_documentation_files(json_spec, src_dir):
66	    """
67	    Modifies the provided json_spec dict (which may be an app, applet,
68	    workflow spec) to inline the contents of the readme file into
69	    "description" and the developer readme into "developerNotes".
70	    """
71	    # Inline description from a readme file
72	    if 'description' not in json_spec:
73	        readme_filename = None
74	        for filename in 'README.md', 'Readme.md', 'readme.md':
75	            if os.path.exists(os.path.join(src_dir, filename)):
76	                readme_filename = filename

79	            with open(os.path.join(src_dir, readme_filename)) as fh:
80	                json_spec['description'] = fh.read()

82	    # Inline developerNotes from Readme.developer.md

84	        for filename in 'README.developer.md', 'Readme.developer.md', 'readme.developer.md':
85	            if os.path.exists(os.path.join(src_dir, filename)):

101	def get_valid_bill_to(bill_to, executable_builder_exception):
102	    """
103	    Check if the requesting user can perform billable activities on behalf of the billTo
104	    If not specified, default to the billTo of the requesting user
105	    otherwise it must be either the ID of the requesting user, 
106	    or an org of which the requesting user is a member with 'allowBillableActivities' permission
107	    """
108	    user_id = dxpy.whoami()
109	    if not bill_to:
110	        return dxpy.api.user_describe(user_id)['billTo']
111	
112	    exception_msg = None
113	    if bill_to.startswith('user-') and bill_to != user_id:
114	        exception_msg = 'Cannot request another user to be the "billTo"'
115	    elif bill_to.startswith('org-'):
116	        try:
117	            member_access = dxpy.api.org_describe(bill_to)
118	            if not member_access['allowBillableActivities']:
119	                exception_msg='You are not a member in {} with allowBillableActivities permission. Please check the billing policy of the org.'.format(bill_to)
120	        except:
121	            exception_msg='Cannot retrieve billing information for {}. Please check your access level and the billing policy of the org.'.format(bill_to)
122	    else:
123	        exception_msg='The field "billTo" must be a valid ID of a user/org.'
124	    
125	    if exception_msg:
126	        raise executable_builder_exception(exception_msg)
127	    
128	    return bill_to

130	def verify_developer_rights(prefixed_name):
131	    """
132	    Checks if the current user is a developer of the app or global workflow
133	    with the given name. If the app/global workflow exists and the user has
134	    developer rights to it, the function returns a named tuple representing
135	    the executable that was queried.
136	    """
137	    assert(prefixed_name.startswith('app-') or prefixed_name.startswith('globalworkflow-'))
138	
139	    if prefixed_name.partition('-')[0] == 'app':
140	        exception_type = dxpy.app_builder.AppBuilderException
141	        describe_method = dxpy.api.app_describe
142	        exception_msg = \
143	            'An app with the given name already exists and you are not a developer of that app'
144	    else:
145	        exception_type = dxpy.workflow_builder.WorkflowBuilderException
146	        describe_method = dxpy.api.global_workflow_describe
147	        exception_msg = \
148	            'A global workflow with the given name already exists and you are not a developer of that workflow'
149	    
150	    name_already_exists = True
151	    is_developer = False
152	    version = None
153	    executable_id = None
154	    FoundExecutable = collections.namedtuple('FoundExecutable', ['name', 'version', 'id'])
155	    try:
156	        describe_output = describe_method(prefixed_name,
157	                                          input_params={"fields": {"isDeveloperFor": True,
158	                                                                   "version": True,
159	                                                                   "id": True}})
160	        is_developer = describe_output['isDeveloperFor']
161	        version = describe_output['version']
162	        executable_id = describe_output['id']
163	    except dxpy.exceptions.DXAPIError as e:
164	        if e.name == 'ResourceNotFound':
165	            name_already_exists = False
166	        elif e.name == 'PermissionDenied':
167	            raise exception_type(exception_msg)
168	        else:
169	            raise e
170	
171	    if not name_already_exists:
172	        # This app/workflow doesn't exist yet so its creation will succeed
173	        # (or at least, not fail on the basis of the ACL).
174	        return FoundExecutable(name=None, version=None, id=None)
175	
176	    name_without_prefix = prefixed_name.partition('-')[2]
177	    if not is_developer:
178	        raise exception_type('You are not a developer for {n}'.format(n=name_without_prefix))
179	
180	    return FoundExecutable(name=name_without_prefix, version=version, id=executable_id)

183	def assert_consistent_regions(from_spec, from_command_line, executable_builder_exception):
184	    """
185	    Verifies the regions passed with --region CLI argument and the ones
186	    specified in regionalOptions are the same (if both CLI and spec were used)
187	    """
188	    if from_spec is None or from_command_line is None:
189	        return
190	    if set(from_spec) != set(from_command_line):
191	        raise executable_builder_exception("--region and the 'regionalOptions' key in the JSON file or --extra-args do not agree")

194	def assert_consistent_reg_options(exec_type, json_spec, executable_builder_exception):
195	    """
196	    Validates the "regionalOptions" field and verifies all the regions used
197	    in "regionalOptions" have the same options.
198	    """
199	    reg_options_spec = json_spec.get('regionalOptions')
200	    json_fn = 'dxapp.json or --extra-args' if exec_type == 'app' else 'dxworkflow.json or --extra-args'
201	
202	    if not isinstance(reg_options_spec, dict):
203	        raise executable_builder_exception("The field 'regionalOptions' in  must be a mapping")
204	    if not reg_options_spec:
205	        raise executable_builder_exception(
206	            "The field 'regionalOptions' in " + json_fn + " must be a non-empty mapping")
207	    regional_options_list = list(reg_options_spec.items())
208	    for region, opts_for_region in regional_options_list:
209	        if not isinstance(opts_for_region, dict):
210	            raise executable_builder_exception("The field 'regionalOptions['" + region +
211	                            "']' in " + json_fn + " must be a mapping")
212	        if set(opts_for_region.keys()) != set(regional_options_list[0][1].keys()):
213	            if set(opts_for_region.keys()) - set(regional_options_list[0][1].keys()):
214	                with_key, without_key = region, regional_options_list[0][0]
215	                key_name = next(iter(set(opts_for_region.keys()) - set(regional_options_list[0][1].keys())))
216	            else:
217	                with_key, without_key = regional_options_list[0][0], region
218	                key_name = next(iter(set(regional_options_list[0][1].keys()) - set(opts_for_region.keys())))
219	            raise executable_builder_exception(
220	                "All regions in regionalOptions must specify the same options; " +
221	                "{} was given for {} but not for {}" .format (key_name, with_key, without_key)
222	            )
223	
224	        if exec_type == 'app':
225	            for key in opts_for_region:
226	                if key in json_spec.get('runSpec', {}):
227	                    raise executable_builder_exception(
228	                    key + " cannot be given in both runSpec and in regional options for " + region)

230	def get_permitted_regions(bill_to, executable_builder_exception):
231	    """
232	    Validates requested bill_to and returns the set of its permitted regions.
233	    """
234	    billable_regions = set()
235	    try:
236	        billable_regions= set(dxpy.DXHTTPRequest('/' + bill_to + '/describe', {}).get("permittedRegions"))
237	    except:
238	        raise executable_builder_exception("Failed to get permitted regions of {}".format(bill_to))

241	def get_enabled_regions(exec_type, json_spec, from_command_line, executable_builder_exception):
242	    """
243	    Return a list of regions in which the global executable (app or global workflow)
244	    will be enabled, based on the "regionalOption" in their JSON specification
245	    and/or --region CLI argument used with "dx build".
246	
247	    :param exec_type: 'app' or 'globalworkflow'
248	    :type json_spec: str.
249	    :param json_spec: The contents of dxapp.json or dxworkflow.json
250	    :type json_spec: dict or None.
251	    :param from_command_line: The regional options specified on the command-line via --region.
252	    :type from_command_line: list or None.
253	    :param executable_builder_exception: Exception that will be thrown.
254	    :type executable_builder_exception: AppBuilderException or WorkflowBuilderException.
255	    """
256	
257	    from_spec = json_spec.get('regionalOptions')
258	
259	    if from_spec is not None:
260	        assert_consistent_reg_options(exec_type, json_spec, executable_builder_exception)
261	
262	    assert_consistent_regions(from_spec, from_command_line, executable_builder_exception)
263	
264	    enabled_regions = None
265	    if from_spec is not None:
266	        enabled_regions = from_spec.keys()
267	    elif from_command_line is not None:
268	        enabled_regions = from_command_line
269	
270	    return enabled_regions

140	def parse_destination(dest_str):
141	    """
142	    Parses dest_str, which is (roughly) of the form
143	    PROJECT:/FOLDER/NAME, and returns a tuple (project, folder, name)
144	    """
145	    # Interpret strings of form "project-XXXX" (no colon) as project. If
146	    # we pass these through to resolve_path they would get interpreted
147	    # as folder names...
148	    if is_container_id(dest_str):
149	        return (dest_str, None, None)
150	
151	    # ...otherwise, defer to resolver.resolve_path. This handles the
152	    # following forms:
153	    #
154	    # /FOLDER/
155	    # /ENTITYNAME
156	    # /FOLDER/ENTITYNAME
157	    # [PROJECT]:
158	    # [PROJECT]:/FOLDER/
159	    # [PROJECT]:/ENTITYNAME
160	    # [PROJECT]:/FOLDER/ENTITYNAME
161	    return try_call(resolve_path, dest_str)

164	def get_asset_tarball(asset_name, src_dir, dest_project, dest_folder, json_out):
165	    """

167	    the archived file is uploaded to the platform

169	    if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(src_dir, "resources")):
170	        temp_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
171	        try:
172	            resource_file = os.path.join(temp_dir, asset_name + "_resources.tar.gz")
173	            cmd = ["tar", "-czf", resource_file, "-C", os.path.join(src_dir, "resources"), "."]
174	            subprocess.check_call(cmd)
175	            file_id = dx_upload(resource_file, dest_project, dest_folder, json_out)
176	            return file_id
177	        finally:

833	'''
834	This function is used for reading a part of an S3 object. It returns a string containing the data. If there is an
835	error, and exception is thrown.
836	
837	There is special handling if a DXIncompleteReadsError is thrown, for which urllib3 gets only part of the requested
838	range from the chunk of data. The range is split into smaller chunks, and each sub-chunk is tried in a DXHTTPRequest.
839	The smaller chunks are then concatenated to form the original range of data. If a DXIncompleteReadsError is thrown
840	(after retrying the sub-chunk 6 times) while reading a sub-chunk, then we fail.
841	'''
842	
843	
844	def _dxhttp_read_range(url, headers, start_pos, end_pos, timeout, sub_range=True):
845	    if sub_range:
846	        headers['Range'] = "bytes=" + str(start_pos) + "-" + str(end_pos)
847	    try:
848	        data = DXHTTPRequest(url, '', method='GET', headers=headers, auth=None, jsonify_data=False, prepend_srv=False,
849	                             always_retry=True, timeout=timeout, decode_response_body=False)
850	        _raise_error_for_testing()
851	        return data
852	
853	    # When chunk fails to be read, it gets broken into sub-chunks
854	    except exceptions.DXIncompleteReadsError:
855	        chunk_buffer = StringIO()
856	        subchunk_len = int(math.ceil((end_pos - start_pos + 1)/INCOMPLETE_READS_NUM_SUBCHUNKS))
857	        subchunk_start_pos = start_pos
858	
859	        while subchunk_start_pos <= end_pos:
860	            subchunk_end_pos = min(subchunk_start_pos + subchunk_len - 1, end_pos)
861	            headers['Range'] = "bytes=" + str(subchunk_start_pos) + "-" + str(subchunk_end_pos)
862	            subchunk_start_pos += subchunk_len
863	            data = DXHTTPRequest(url, '', method='GET', headers=headers, auth=None, jsonify_data=False,
864	                                 prepend_srv=False, always_retry=True, timeout=timeout,
865	                                 decode_response_body=False)
866	
867	            # Concatenate sub-chunks
868	            chunk_buffer.write(data)
869	
870	        concat_chunks = chunk_buffer.getvalue()
871	        chunk_buffer.close()
872	        return concat_chunks

158	def path_completer(text, expected=None, classes=None, perm_level=None,
159	                   include_current_proj=False, typespec=None, visibility=None):
160	    '''
161	    :param text: String to tab-complete to a path matching the syntax project-name:folder/entity_or_folder_name
162	    :type text: string
163	    :param expected: "folder", "entity", "project", or None (no restriction) as to the types of answers to look for
164	    :type expected: string
165	    :param classes: if expected="entity", the possible data object classes that are acceptable
166	    :type classes: list of strings
167	    :param perm_level: the minimum permissions level required, e.g. "VIEW" or "CONTRIBUTE"
168	    :type perm_level: string
169	    :param include_current_proj: Indicate whether the current project's name should be a potential result
170	    :type include_current_proj: boolean
171	    :param visibility: Visibility with which to restrict the completion (one of "either", "visible", or "hidden") (default behavior is dependent on *text*)
172	
173	    Returns a list of matches to the text and restricted by the
174	    requested parameters.
175	    '''
176	    colon_pos = get_last_pos_of_char(':', text)
177	    slash_pos = get_last_pos_of_char('/', text)
178	    delim_pos = max(colon_pos, slash_pos)
179	
180	    # First get projects if necessary
181	    matches = []
182	    if expected == 'project' and colon_pos > 0 and colon_pos == len(text) - 1:
183	        if dxpy.find_one_project(zero_ok=True, name=text[:colon_pos]) is not None:
184	            return [text + " "]
185	
186	    if colon_pos < 0 and slash_pos < 0:
187	        # Might be tab-completing a project, but don't ever include
188	        # whatever's set as dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID unless expected == "project"
189	        # Also, don't bother if text=="" and expected is NOT "project"
190	        # Also, add space if expected == "project"
191	        if text != "" or expected == 'project':
192	            results = dxpy.find_projects(describe=True, level=perm_level)
193	            if not include_current_proj:
194	                results = [r for r in results if r['id'] != dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID]
195	            matches += [escape_colon(r['describe']['name'])+':' for r in results if r['describe']['name'].startswith(text)]
196	
197	    if expected == 'project':
198	        return matches
199	
200	    # Attempt to tab-complete to a folder or data object name
201	    if colon_pos < 0 and slash_pos >= 0:
202	        # Not tab-completing a project, and the project is unambiguous
203	        # (use dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID)
204	        if dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID is not None:
205	            # try-catch block in case dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID is garbage
206	            try:
207	                dxproj = dxpy.get_handler(dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID)
208	                folderpath, entity_name = clean_folder_path(text)
209	                matches += get_folder_matches(text, slash_pos, dxproj, folderpath)
210	                if expected != 'folder':
211	                    if classes is not None:
212	                        for classname in classes:
213	                            matches += get_data_matches(text, slash_pos, dxproj,
214	                                                        folderpath, classname=classname,
215	                                                        typespec=typespec,
216	                                                        visibility=visibility)
217	                    else:
218	                        matches += get_data_matches(text, slash_pos, dxproj,
219	                                                    folderpath, typespec=typespec,
220	                                                    visibility=visibility)
221	            except:
222	                pass
223	    else:
224	        # project is given by a path, but attempt to resolve to an
225	        # object or folder anyway
226	        try:
227	            proj_ids, folderpath, entity_name = resolve_path(text, multi_projects=True)
228	        except ResolutionError as details:
229	            sys.stderr.write("\n" + fill(str(details)))
230	            return matches
231	        for proj in proj_ids:
232	            # protects against dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID being garbage
233	            try:
234	                dxproj = dxpy.get_handler(proj)
235	                matches += get_folder_matches(text, delim_pos, dxproj, folderpath)
236	                if expected != 'folder':
237	                    if classes is not None:
238	                        for classname in classes:
239	                            matches += get_data_matches(text, delim_pos, dxproj,
240	                                                        folderpath, classname=classname,
241	                                                        typespec=typespec, visibility=visibility)
242	                    else:
243	                        matches += get_data_matches(text, delim_pos, dxproj,
244	                                                    folderpath, typespec=typespec,
245	                                                    visibility=visibility)
246	            except:
247	                pass
248	    return matches

{"unit": "src/python/dxpy/nextflow/collect_images.py::_populate_cached_file_ids", "suspicions": [{"label": "a", "root_cause": "C8.S4", "lines": [401, 407], "why": "The loop `for ref in cacheable` issues one `find_data_objects(...)` call per ref. collect_docker_images emits one entry per process, so an image used by k processes produces k identical queries. The query depends only on ref.image_name, ref.tag and ref.digest (cache_folder, name, and the properties filter), so every repeat returns the same answer. The test test_duplicate_refs_each_get_cache_hit asserts mock_find.call_count == 2 for two identical refs. A lookup keyed on (image_name, tag, digest) would issue one query per distinct image. collect_docker_images already memoizes resolved_digests by image for the digest step, so the same reuse is missing here. bundle_docker_images dedups by identifier only after these calls have run."}]}
{"unit": "src/python/dxpy/nextflow/ImageRef.py::ImageRef._package_bundle", "suspicions": [{"label": "a", "root_cause": "C8.S4", "lines": [81, 93], "why": "For a cache hit, _populate_cached_file_ids already matched the file by name=cache_file_name (collect_images.py line 412) and received its name in results[0]['describe']['name'] (line 425), which it uses only for a progress message. The ref then carries only file_id, so _package_bundle takes the else branch (line 92) and calls self._dx_file_get_name() (line 93). That builds a DXFile and calls .describe() (lines 81-82), a second API request for a name already in hand. For these refs the name equals self._construct_cache_file_name() (line 90). The describe is needed only for dx:// refs, where image_name is the file id and no name was ever fetched. This branch cannot tell the two cases apart today, so a fix has to carry the name on the ref or add a flag. The cost is one request per distinct cache-hit image per build."}]}
{"unit": "src/python/test/dxpy_testutil.py::DXTestCase.setUp", "suspicions": [{"label": "a", "root_cause": "C1.S6", "lines": [330, 332], "why": "Every test on DXTestCase creates a real platform project (dxpy.api.project_new on line 330), spawns a dx cd subprocess (line 332), and destroys the project in tearDown. Tests that never call the platform still pay for this. TestVersion in src/python/test/utils/test_version.py only compares Version objects, and both of its tests are local. TestImageRef in src/python/test/test_nextflow_ImageRefFactory.py builds ImageRef objects from dicts and never calls bundled_depends. test_ImageRef_cache in src/python/test/test_nextflow_ImageRef.py only checks that an abstract method raises. The one project-dependent test in that set, test_DockerImageRef_cache, is already gated on DXTEST_NF_DOCKER. The setup is therefore unconditional work for tests that do not use it. Those classes could inherit unittest.TestCase, or the project setup could move into the tests that need it."}]}
{"unit": "src/python/test/mock_api/api.py::set_payload", "suspicions": [{"label": "a", "root_cause": "C6.S3", "lines": [27, 29, 31], "why": "The handler materializes the whole payload before any request is served. The loop writes 1024 chunks of 512 KiB each into one BytesIO (lines 29-30), so app.payload holds 512 MiB for the life of the server (line 31). serve_download (line 75) only slices app.payload[start:stop+1] for one range at a time. Each chunk is struct.pack of one random.getrandbits(64) value repeated 65536 times, so the full content is fixed by 1024 integers, about 8 KiB in total. Ranges could be generated on demand from those integers, and the md5 on line 35 could be computed chunk by chunk without keeping the buffer. Served bytes would be identical for the same seeds. The saving is largest when a client reads only part of the file. Callers of /system/setPayload live outside this repository, so how often it runs is unknown."}]}

NOTES:
Every listed file was read in full, and the unit counts come from an AST walk. Nested functions were not counted as units. reference/root-causes/ was not opened, as instructed.

Considered and left out. nextflow_builder.py line 125 calls wait_on_done(interval=1), which polls twice as often as the library default of 2 (src/python/dxpy/bindings/dxjob.py line 311). Each poll is a describe request during a build that runs for minutes. A longer interval trades response latency for fewer requests, and the author may have picked 1 s on purpose, so I did not decide this.

Left out as too small to matter. These are the += string build in get_nextflow_src (nextflow_templates.py lines 88-97), which scales with the number of schema parameters. Also the repeated manifest reads in resolve_version (at most two per run), the .copy() in bundle_docker_images (collect_images.py line 68), sorted(...)[0] in find_readme, and re-validating shared asset files per version in validate_assets.

Undecided. DXTestCaseBuildWorkflows.setUp (dxpy_testutil.py lines 460-464) creates a platform applet for every test in its subclasses in test_dxpy.py and test_dxclient.py. Only some of those tests use self.test_applet_id. I did not read those subclasses in full, so I did not record it.

Left out on behaviour grounds. DockerImageRef._cache runs sudo docker pull before docker save. The pull may contact the registry for an image already present, but it also refreshes the tag, so removing it would change behaviour.

Unused class. TemporaryFile.__exit__ (dxpy_testutil.py lines 702-704) never closes its handle, which has the C6.S6 shape. Nothing in this repository uses the class, so it costs nothing here.

Those classes could inherit unittest.TestCase, or the project setup could move into the tests that need it."}]}
{"unit": "src/python/test/mock_api/api.py::set_payload", "suspicions": [{"label": "a", "root_cause": "C6.S3", "lines": [27, 29, 31], "why": "The handler materializes the whole payload before any request is served. The loop writes 1024 chunks of 512 KiB each into one BytesIO (lines 29-30), so app.payload holds 512 MiB for the life of the server (line 31). serve_download (line 75) only slices app.payload[start:stop+1] for one range at a time. Each chunk is struct.pack of one random.getrandbits(64) value repeated 65536 times, so the full content is fixed by 1024 integers, about 8 KiB in total. Ranges could be generated on demand from those integers, and the md5 on line 35 could be computed chunk by chunk without keeping the buffer. Served bytes would be identical for the same seeds. The saving is largest when a client reads only part of the file. Callers of /system/setPayload live outside this repository, so how often it runs is unknown."}]}

Every listed file was read in full, and the unit counts come from an AST walk. Nested functions were not counted as units. reference/root-causes/ was not opened, as instructed.

Considered and left out. nextflow_builder.py line 125 calls wait_on_done(interval=1), which polls twice as often as the library default of 2 (src/python/dxpy/bindings/dxjob.py line 311). Each poll is a describe request during a build that runs for minutes. A longer interval trades response latency for fewer requests, and the author may have picked 1 s on purpose, so I did not decide this.

Left out as too small to matter. These are the += string build in get_nextflow_src (nextflow_templates.py lines 88-97), which scales with the number of schema parameters. Also the repeated manifest reads in resolve_version (at most two per run), the .copy() in bundle_docker_images (collect_images.py line 68), sorted(...)[0] in find_readme, and re-validating shared asset files per version in validate_assets.

Undecided. DXTestCaseBuildWorkflows.setUp (dxpy_testutil.py lines 460-464) creates a platform applet for every test in its subclasses in test_dxpy.py and test_dxclient.py. Only some of those tests use self.test_applet_id. I did not read those subclasses in full, so I did not record it.

Left out on behaviour grounds. DockerImageRef._cache runs sudo docker pull before docker save. The pull may contact the registry for an image already present, but it also refreshes the tag, so removing it would change behaviour.

Unused class. TemporaryFile.__exit__ (dxpy_testutil.py lines 702-704) never closes its handle, which has the C6.S6 shape. Nothing in this repository uses the class, so it costs nothing here.

units = []
def walk(node, qual, parent_is_func):
    for child in ast.iter_child_nodes(node):
        if isinstance(child, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
            q = (qual + '.' + child.name) if qual else child.name
            # a function is a unit unless it is nested directly inside another function

            walk(child, q, True)
        elif isinstance(child, ast.ClassDef):
            q = (qual + '.' + child.name) if qual else child.name
            walk(child, q, parent_is_func)
        else:
            walk(child, qual, parent_is_func)
walk(tree, '', False)
for q, a, b in units:
    print(a, b, q)

content.content:
# The taxonomy, in full

An **energy smell** is code that spends energy on work the program does not
need, and that a specific refactoring can remove without changing what the
program does. This taxonomy names them: twelve categories, sixty-five root
causes.

This page is what to look for in step 1. Read it before you read the code, and
keep it beside you: of every function, ask whether any of these is happening
there. The **category table** says what each family of waste covers; the
**root cause table** below it lists all sixty-five, one line each — enough to
recognise one, not enough to decide it. Deciding is step 2, with the root
cause's card.

Cards live at `reference/categories/<ID>.md` — a category's root causes, with
the repair for each — and `reference/root-causes/<ID>.<S>.md`, which open at
`step.py done 1`.

## Categories

| ID | Category | Covers | Card |
|---|---|---|---|
| **C1** | Redundant Computation | Energy waste from executing work that does not contribute to the program's required output or that leaves program state unchanged | `reference/categories/C1.md` (8) |
| **C2** | Unnecessary Call Overhead | Energy waste from extra layers of function calls, method delegation, or dynamic dispatch that add overhead without proportional benefit | `reference/categories/C2.md` (3) |
| **C3** | Inefficient Iteration Patterns | Energy waste from loops that perform more per-iteration work than necessary, iterate more times than required, use suboptimal loop constructs, or fail to terminate correctly | `reference/categories/C3.md` (7) |
| **C4** | Inefficient Control Flow | Energy waste from branching, conditions, or dispatch logic that performs unnecessary checks, uses suboptimal evaluation order, or employs patterns that prevent interpreter optimization | `reference/categories/C4.md` (8) |
| **C5** | Suboptimal Data Structures | Energy waste from choosing, provisioning, or converting data structures that do not match the workload's access pattern or size requirements | `reference/categories/C5.md` (4) |
| **C6** | Unnecessary Memory Usage | Patterns that allocate, copy, retain, or leak memory beyond what the workload requires, increasing garbage collection overhead, memory-bus traffic, and system energy consumption | `reference/categories/C6.md` (7) |
| **C7** | Suboptimal Algorithmic | Energy waste from choosing an algorithm, decomposition, or computation strategy that explores more of the problem space than necessary or uses higher complexity than the problem requires | `reference/categories/C7.md` (5) |
| **C8** | Missing Reuse | Energy waste from failing to store and reuse results of expensive computations, lookups, or data fetches, causing the same work to be repeated across calls, requests, or access sites | `reference/categories/C8.md` (4) |
| **C9** | Inefficient External Data Access | Energy waste from inefficient interaction with external systems: databases, file systems, network services, and APIs | `reference/categories/C9.md` (4) |
| **C10** | Underused Language Primitives | Energy waste from not using available optimized language features, standard library functions, or runtime-specific constructs that would accomplish the same task more efficiently | `reference/categories/C10.md` (6) |
| **C11** | Inefficient Concurrency Management | Energy waste from thread/task misuse, synchronization overhead, contention, or failure to exploit available parallelism | `reference/categories/C11.md` (5) |
| **C12** | Poor Hardware Locality Usage | Energy waste driven by CPU and memory hierarchy behavior such as cache misses, branch misprediction, and suboptimal memory access patterns | `reference/categories/C12.md` (4) |

## Every root cause, one line each

### C1 — Redundant Computation

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C1.S1** | Dead Code | a value computed and bound to a name that nothing ever reads |
| **C1.S2** | Redundant Assignment | a store that leaves the program's state exactly as it already was |
| **C1.S3** | Redundant Control Flow | a branch whose outcome is the same whichever way it goes |
| **C1.S4** | Repeated Computation | the same value computed twice in one scope, where one local would serve both |
| **C1.S5** | Resultless Computation | a computation run in full whose result nothing downstream actually needs |
| **C1.S6** | Unnecessary Initialization | setup done unconditionally that only one path actually needs |
| **C1.S7** | Unnecessary Variable | a name bound, read exactly once, and never needed again |
| **C1.S8** | Excessive Runtime-Management Calls | runtime housekeeping invoked far more often than anything needs it |

### C2 — Unnecessary Call Overhead

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C2.S1** | Unnecessary Method Delegation | a wrapper or property that forwards, adds nothing, and sits on a hot path |
| **C2.S2** | Missing Static Declaration | a method that never touches `self` and still pays to be bound to an instance |
| **C2.S3** | Excessive Modularization in Hot Path | a chain of thin layers whose frames cost more than the work at the bottom |

### C3 — Inefficient Iteration Patterns

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C3.S1** | Inefficient Iteration Construct | a loop written in a form that does more interpreter work per element than it needs to |
| **C3.S2** | Recomputing Loop-Invariant Values | an expression recomputed every iteration whose answer never changes |
| **C3.S3** | Inefficient Per-Iteration Setup | an object or resource created once per iteration that the whole loop could share |
| **C3.S4** | Inefficient Nested Iteration | an inner loop that searches, where a lookup would turn n*m into n+m |
| **C3.S5** | Missing Loop Early Exit | a loop that keeps going after its answer is already settled |
| **C3.S6** | Unfiltered Bulk Iteration | the whole collection processed when only a subset was ever wanted |
| **C3.S7** | Inefficient Array Mutation in Loop | a collection edited while it is being walked |

### C4 — Inefficient Control Flow

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C4.S1** | Poor Short-Circuit Ordering | a boolean chain that evaluates its expensive operand before the cheap one that usually decides |
| **C4.S2** | Redundant Conditional Evaluation | a test whose answer was already settled before it ran |
| **C4.S3** | Inefficient Conditional Nesting | a nest or chain of branches that tests more than it has to, where a lookup would test once |
| **C4.S4** | Missing Else-If | consecutive `if`s on one subject that are exclusive in fact but not in form |
| **C4.S5** | Expensive Comparison | a type check made per element where the answer never varies or the types could dispatch themselves |
| **C4.S6** | Expensive Exception Control Flow | an exception used as ordinary control flow, on a path where it is raised often |
| **C4.S7** | Missing Edge-Case Guards | a missing cheap test that would let a common trivial input skip the expensive path |
| **C4.S8** | Non-Idiomatic Condition | a condition spelled the long way round, missing the interpreter's fast path |

### C5 — Suboptimal Data Structures

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C5.S1** | Inefficient Data Structure Choice | a container whose type makes its most frequent operation the expensive one |
| **C5.S2** | Missing Helper Type | a collection searched again and again where one index built beside it would answer every question |
| **C5.S3** | Over-Provisioned Data Type | a representation heavier than the data it holds actually requires |
| **C5.S4** | Unnecessary Representation Change | a conversion between representations that the code on either side did not need |

### C6 — Unnecessary Memory Usage

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C6.S1** | Unnecessary Object | objects created and thrown away that never needed to exist |
| **C6.S2** | Unnecessary Copying | data duplicated when the original could have been used or changed in place |
| **C6.S3** | Unnecessary Data Materialization | a whole sequence built in memory when the consumer wanted it one element at a time |
| **C6.S4** | Oversized Data Retaining | something long-lived holding far more data than anything later reads |
| **C6.S5** | Over-Allocation | capacity reserved up front for data that never arrives |
| **C6.S6** | Leaked Resource Handles | a file, socket or connection acquired with nothing guaranteeing its release |
| **C6.S7** | Leaking Mutable Default Arguments | a mutable default argument that quietly accumulates across every call |

### C7 — Suboptimal Algorithmic

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C7.S1** | Suboptimal Algorithm Choice | an algorithm of worse complexity than the problem requires |
| **C7.S2** | Inefficient Problem Decomposition | a search exploring subproblems it could have pruned, reordered or reused |
| **C7.S3** | Avoidable Recursive Implementation | a recursion paying a frame per level where a loop would use one |
| **C7.S4** | Inefficient Operation Ordering | two commuting operations in the order that makes the expensive one see more data |
| **C7.S5** | Unsimplified Operation | an operation doing more work than an algebraic fact about its inputs requires |

### C8 — Missing Reuse

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C8.S1** | Missing Memoization Cache | a deterministic computation repeated across calls that a cache would answer |
| **C8.S2** | Missing Derived-Value Reuse | an expensive artefact derived again on every use instead of once for the process |
| **C8.S3** | Missing Local Lookup Caching | a name or attribute chain re-resolved every iteration for a value that never moves |
| **C8.S4** | Redundant Data Fetching | the same external data fetched again when the copy in memory was still good |

### C9 — Inefficient External Data Access

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C9.S1** | Fragmented I/O Calls | many small independent external operations where one bulk operation would do |
| **C9.S2** | Oversized Data Retrieval | more data pulled across a process boundary than the program ever consults |
| **C9.S3** | Inefficient Retrieval Paths | one fetch per row of an earlier fetch, where a join would have taken one trip |
| **C9.S4** | Expensive Query Pattern | a query whose shape makes the engine do far more work than the answer needs |

### C10 — Underused Language Primitives

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C10.S1** | Skipping Optimized Built-ins | a hand-written loop doing bulk work a C-level primitive already does |
| **C10.S2** | Inefficient Built-in Choice | one primitive used where a cheaper primitive computes the same answer |
| **C10.S3** | Missing Bulk Primitive Usage | a per-element call inside a loop that a single batched call would replace |
| **C10.S4** | Inefficient String Concatenation | a string grown with `+=` in a loop, where the target is aliased or the parts are many |
| **C10.S5** | Inefficient Scope Lookup | a global or builtin re-resolved through the module namespace on every iteration |
| **C10.S6** | Expensive Operator Overloads | an operator on a user-defined type dispatching and allocating once per element |

### C11 — Inefficient Concurrency Management

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C11.S1** | Excessive Lock Contention | a lock held across work that shares nothing, serialising what could overlap |
| **C11.S2** | Forced Serial Bottleneck | concurrency paid for in full while one shared resource serialises all of it |
| **C11.S3** | Leaked Background Threads | workers started and never stopped, accumulating for the life of the process |
| **C11.S4** | Blocking The Main Thread | a synchronous blocking call inside a coroutine, stopping every other task |
| **C11.S5** | Missed Parallelism Opportunities | independent work run one item at a time when the waits could have overlapped |

### C12 — Poor Hardware Locality Usage

| ID | Name | Looks for |
|---|---|---|
| **C12.S1** | Inefficient Large-Stride Traversal | a contiguous buffer traversed against the direction its memory is laid out in |
| **C12.S2** | Sparse Element Access | scattered reads into a large buffer, using one element of every cache line fetched |
| **C12.S3** | Unpredictable Branches | a data-dependent branch in a compiled hot loop that the CPU cannot predict |
| **C12.S4** | Inefficient Array Declaration Order | a declared struct whose field order puts cold data in front of hot data |

## Using this well

**Any category may apply to any code.** Nothing about a repository rules a
category in or out in advance. Work from what the code actually does.

**Read the card, not the name, and not the line above.** These names are three
or four words long and several of them cover something narrower — or wider —
than they sound like. The one-line summaries here are index entries, precise
enough to recognise something by and not enough to decide anything from. The
card is the claim.

**The index tells you what to look for, not what you will find.** A unit goes
on your list because of what its code does, not because a line here sounds
like it. Finding nothing in a category is a perfectly ordinary outcome.

**Cards overlap.** When two root causes both describe what you repaired,
either attribution is fine — say which you chose.

## What tools can and cannot contribute

Any static rule, in any tool, recognises a syntactic shape that somebody
described in advance. That makes rules dependable about the shapes they know
and completely blind to everything else. Two consequences, and they point in
opposite directions:

- **A rule firing has observed a pattern, not diagnosed a problem.** Every
  pattern in this taxonomy is the right thing to write somewhere, which is what
  each card's `Looks like it, but is not` section records.
  Some of what any rule reports is therefore wrong here, and saying which is
  part of the job.
- **A rule staying quiet has observed nothing.** Waste that lives in the
  arrangement of a program — work computed and discarded, a data shape that
  forces every later step to compensate, a query issued once per row — has no
  fixed syntactic shape at all, and is usually the expensive kind.

Reading the code is the primary method here. Anything a tool tells you is a
second opinion to reconcile with what you already worked out.
----

116	        raise Exception("value={} cannot be converted into class {}".format(val, klass))

118	# For a column that represents files, assume it is named "pair", look for
119	# the index of column "pair ID".
120	def _search_column_id(col_name, header_line):
121	    for i, col_name2 in enumerate(header_line):
122	        if col_name2 == (col_name + " ID"):
123	            return i
124	    raise Exception("Could not find a column with file IDs for {}".format(col_name))
125	
126	# Parse the TSV file. Create a dictionary with the input arguments for
127	# each invocation. Return an array of dictionaries.
128	#
129	# For each line, except the header:
130	#   remove informational columns
131	#   create a dictionary of inputs we can pass to the executable
132	#
133	# Example TSV input:
134	# batch ID, pair1,       pair1 ID, pair2,       pair2 ID
135	# 23,       SRR123_1.gz, file-XXX, SRR223_2.gz, file-YYY
136	#
137	def batch_launch_args(executable, input_json, batch_tsv_file):
138	    header_line = []
139	    lines = []
140	    read_mode = "r"
141	    with open(batch_tsv_file, read_mode) as f:
142	        reader = csv.reader(f, delimiter=str(u'\t'))
143	        header_line = next(reader)
144	        lines = list(reader)
145	
146	    # Get the classes for the executable inputs
147	    input_classes = _get_types_for_inputs(executable)
148	
149	    # which columns to use. Note that a file input uses two columns.
150	    # For example, argument 'pair1' exposes two columns {'pair1, 'pair1 ID'}.
151	    batch_index = None
152	    index_2_column = {}
153	    for i, col_name in enumerate(header_line):
154	        if col_name == BATCH_ID:
155	            batch_index = i
156	        if col_name not in input_classes:
157	            continue
158	        if input_classes[col_name] in ['file', 'array:file']:
159	            idx = _search_column_id(col_name, header_line)
160	            index_2_column[idx] = col_name
161	        else:
162	            index_2_column[i] = col_name
163	    if batch_index is None:
164	        raise Exception("Could not find column {}".format(BATCH_ID))
165	
166	    # A dictionary of inputs. Each column in the TSV file is mapped to a row.
167	    # {
168	    #    "a": [{dnanexus_link: "file-xxxx"}, {dnanexus_link: "file-yyyy"}, ....],
169	    #    "b": [1,null, ...]
170	    # }
171	    columns=defaultdict(list)
172	    all_files=[]
173	    for line in lines:
174	        for i, val in enumerate(line):
175	            if i not in index_2_column:
176	                continue
177	            col_name = index_2_column[i]
178	            klass = input_classes[col_name]
179	            val_w_correct_type, ref_files = _type_convert(val.strip(), klass)
180	            all_files += ref_files
181	            columns[col_name].append(val_w_correct_type)
182	
183	    # Create an array of batch_ids
184	    batch_ids = [line[batch_index].strip() for line in lines]
185	
186	    # call validate
187	    #
188	    # Output: list of dictionaries, each dictionary corresponds to expanded batch call
189	    expanded_args = dxpy.api.applet_validate_batch(executable.get_id(),
190	                                                   { "batchInput": columns,
191	                                                     "commonInput": input_json,
192	                                                     "files": all_files,
193	                                                     "instanceTypes": [] })
194	
195	    ## future proofing
196	    if isinstance(expanded_args, dict):
197	        assert('expandedBatch' in expanded_args)
198	        launch_args = expanded_args['expandedBatch']
199	    else:
200	        launch_args = expanded_args
201	    if len(launch_args) != len(batch_ids):
202	        raise Exception("Mismatch in number of launch_args vs. batch_ids ({} != {})"
203	                        .format(len(launch_args), len(batch_ids)))
204	
205	    return { "launch_args": launch_args,
206	             "batch_ids": batch_ids }
207	
208	#
209	# executable: applet, app, or workflow
210	# launch_args: array of dictionaries, each of which contains all arguments needed to
211	#     invoke the executable.
212	# set_batch_folders: boolean, if True, the results from each batch
213	#     run will be placed in a separate output folder named after batch ID.
214	#     The folders will be created/used relative to the output folder set with
215	#     the --destination arg
216	def batch_run(executable, b_args, run_kwargs, set_batch_folders=False):
217	    run_args = run_kwargs.copy()
218	    exec_name = executable.describe()["name"]
219	    launch_args = b_args["launch_args"]
220	    batch_ids = b_args["batch_ids"]
221	    executions = []
222	    for idx, input_json in enumerate(launch_args):
223	        batch_id = batch_ids[idx]
224	        name = "{}-{}".format(exec_name, batch_id)
225	        properties = {
226	            'batch-id': batch_id,
227	            'batch-name': name
228	        }
229	        run_args['name'] = name
230	        if run_args.get('properties') is not None:
231	            run_args['properties'].update(properties)
232	        else:
233	            run_args['properties'] = properties
234	
235	        if set_batch_folders:
236	            run_args['folder'] = run_kwargs['folder'] + "/" + batch_id
237	
238	        try:
239	            dxexecution = executable.run(input_json, **run_args)
240	            executions.append(dxexecution)
241	        except Exception:
242	            err_exit()
243	    return executions

37	def _remove_ignore_errors(filename):
38	    try:
39	        os.remove(filename)
40	    except Exception:
41	        pass

43	def _open_for_writing_with_permissions(filename, perms=0o600):
44	    _remove_ignore_errors(filename)
45	    return os.fdopen(os.open(filename, os.O_CREAT | os.O_WRONLY, perms), "w")
